agencyDescription:

We enable employers to build a skilled, future-ready workforce, design quality jobs, and adopt skills recognition practices. Together with our partners, we build a trusted, high-quality, industry-relevant, and innovative ecosystem that meets the evolving workforce needs of both businesses and workers.   

Guided by our vision of a Singapore where everyone can grow in fulfilling careers, we live our promise of Building Skills, Growing Careers by nurturing lifelong learning, strengthening employability and enabling career growth for all, including our own officers, through a continuous learning culture and a supportive, flexible, inclusive working environment that fosters innovation, collaboration, and well-being.

So, join us to be part of a dynamic team driving the national SkillsFuture movement and building a strong Singaporean core. Together, we create opportunities, transform lives, and shape the future of work.

The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.

jobDescription:
The operating environment of the Public Service is undergoing fundamental and rapid change. The issues we face are complex and multi-faceted, which impact the way the Public Service operates and organises itself. To prepare the Public Service for these changes, we have begun the journey towards Public Sector Transformation (PST). 

As part of the current phase of PST, ServiceSG aims to be on par with globally leading companies in our delivery of public services. A key transformation in the delivery of citizen services is to take a citizen-centric service journey approach to organising services in an integrated manner via a) a digital concierge via the LifeSG app, b) a physical concierge via an expanded network of Service Centres; and c) a central contact centre. Our aim is to transform the current citizen experience of having to navigate across different public agencies to an experience of the Public Service “knowing, understanding and interacting with me as One”.

ServiceSG set up its first central contact centre in Aug 2022, operated by an outsourced partner, with 16 agencies onboard as users. Its wide scope and diverse operations have allowed ServiceSG to respond swiftly handle call surges within days.  It has built-in levers to allow swift scale up a hired workforce whenever needed, and is working to expand the pool of manpower it could tap on, by identifying, tagging and training a group of public officers from the service delivery job role, to prepare them for immediate mobilisation to handle calls during a national emergency. 

By doing these, ServiceSG provides greater capacity and flexibility to manage call centre operations during a crisis, rather than relying on the call centre and/or staff capacity of one lead agency which could be overwhelmed.
jobResponsibilities:
As Assistant Director / Senior Manager, ServiceSG Contact Centre Planning and Operations, you play a pivotal role in supporting the Director in the establishment and operationalisation of the Whole-of-Government (WOG) Resilience Community.

This includes working with agency stakeholders to identify and train Public Service officers   to manage high-volume, fast-paced contact centre operations, driving innovation and transformation projects, and ensuring the seamless delivery of citizen-facing services during both peacetime and crisis situations. The role also involves strategic vendor and stakeholder management, surge operations planning, and the implementation of technological solutions to enhance service delivery and productivity. You will set up a WOG Resilience Community, partnering with some of the biggest government contact centres to strengthen Singapore’s readiness for the next emergency.  

Responsibilities 
Reporting to the Director, you will be responsible for implementing ServiceSG’s strategy of developing manpower contingency plans, integration of systems for WOG crisis readiness to support, while building strong partnerships with agency stakeholders to ensure operational excellence in service delivery during crisis.

[Key Areas of Responsibilities]

• Develop and execute manpower contingency plans for crisis response, including the identification and training of public officers for the Resilience Community
• Establish and maintain partnerships with agency contact centres to create an integrated network for crisis response
• Design and implement training curriculum 
• Coordinate with agencies to maintain and update the Knowledge Management (KM) system
• Develop and set up central crisis contact channels such as AI bots, hotlines and livechat channels
• Manage capacity planning and workforce development for both steady state and crisis operations
• Lead the annual readiness planning activities, including simulation exercises, systems integration and interoperability checks
• Operationalise ServiceSG’s contingency plans during crisis
• Set up monitoring processes and analyse contact centre performance indicators to gain insights to inform decision-making for partner agencies during crisis
• Oversee vendor management for outsourced contact centre operations
• Obtain and manage budget and procurement matters for contact centre transformation initiatives
jobRequirements:
[Work Experience & Competencies]
An ideal candidate should possess:
• Minimum 8 years of experience in contact centre operations or service delivery transformation, with demonstrated experience in implementing AI solutions
• Strong understanding of contact centre technologies and digital transformation initiatives
• Experience in crisis management and contingency planning
• Proven track record in managing large-scale transformation projects involving multiple stakeholders
• Strong leadership skills with experience in managing hybrid teams (both in-house and outsourced)

We seek a leader who thrives in a dynamic, start-up-like environment. The ideal candidate will be adept at navigating ambiguity, fostering innovation, and solving problems with a focus on action.

[Work Experience & Competencies]

The ideal candidate will exhibit:
•	[Leadership in Customer Service]: A proven track record of leading teams to deliver empathetic and effective customer service, with a knack for understanding and addressing citizen needs.
•	[Strategic Customer Experience Vision]: A visionary approach to transforming service delivery, leveraging new technologies to enhance customer-centricity and productivity.

agencyDescription:
The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors so as to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

• Civil Aviation and Air Transport
• Maritime and Ports
• Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region.

The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).
jobDescription:

If you share our vision and possess the qualities we seek, join us!
jobResponsibilities:
The Assistant Director (Futures & Research) will play a key role in shaping, delivering, and stewarding MOT’s research and development (R&D) agenda. The officer will partner closely with the National Research Foundation (NRF), MOT's statutory boards (e.g., CAAS, MPA, LTA), and the wider research ecosystem to design funding initiatives, drive programme governance, and ensure rigorous management of Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) programmes across RIE2020, RIE2025 and the upcoming RIE2030.  

The role is central to ensuring MOT’s long‑term innovation capability, supporting national strategic objectives, and delivering impact through a transport-focused flagship programme (FP).      

Key Responsibilities:

(Programme Design & Strategy Development): 
- Co‑design and refine Funding Initiatives (FIs) under the FP with academia, government and industry stakeholders, including articulating problem statements, R&D agendas, and desired outcomes aligned to MOT's long-term requirements.  
- Support the development and review of long‑term RIE strategies for the transport and logistics sector.  

(Grant & Programme Administration): 
- Administer the FIs and other RIE funding initiatives in accordance with rules and guidelines set by NRF. Tasks include checking that grantees and research collaborators meet requirements on governance, reporting, disbursement controls, conflict-of-interest declarations, and performance management.  
- Oversee grant call cycles: drafting FI papers, preparing grant disbursement documentation, coordinating evaluations, and facilitating approvals by Approving Authorities and NRF where required.  
- Monitor project progress, KPIs, milestones, budgets and compliance, intervening where necessary to ensure programme integrity.  

(Cross‑Agency & Ecosystem Engagement): 
- Serve as MOT’s liaison with NRF, A*STAR, EnterpriseSG, academia, and industry partners on RIE planning, implementation, and governance matters.  
- Support FC Flagship Committee and related RIE governance fora through preparation of papers, briefings, and analysis.  
- Coordinate joint or cross‑sectoral initiatives across aviation, maritime, land transport, logistics and connectivity domains.  

(Policy, Evaluation & Impact Assessment):  
- Evaluate proposals and provide policy input on scientific merit, translational potential, and alignment with MOT’s sectoral objectives.  
- Track and analyse performance across RIE2020 and RIE2025 programmes transitioning under FC, identifying lessons and shaping improvements to future tranches.  
- Develop insights and recommendations to strengthen innovation governance, capability development, and ecosystems across MOT‑Family.
jobRequirements:
Qualifications: 
- Tertiary qualification in engineering, science, economics, public policy or other relevant fields.  
- Postgraduate qualification is an advantage. 

Experience & Technical Skills: 
- 3 years of experience in management, innovation policy, grant administration, or science and technology strategy.  
- Familiarity with RIE frameworks, NRF processes, FI governance, and public‑sector programme/grant management is an advantage.  
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to assess R&D proposals, financial implications, and strategic relevance.  
- Experience engaging research performers, industry technology players, and government stakeholders.  

Core Competencies: 
- Strong communication (written & verbal), stakeholder management, and cross‑agency coordination skills.  
- Ability to manage multi‑stakeholder programmes with tight deadlines.  
- Sound judgement, attention to detail, and high standards of governance.

jobResponsibilities:
Candidate will review systems infrastructure, design and architecture to ensure cybersecurity factors are considered and in compliance within existing government IM8 requirements. In addition, candidate will support the implementation of cyber and data security measures, and incident response and management for these systems. These systems are software intensive, complex and requires high availability. Depending on the phase of the systems lifecycle, candidate will be assigned to specify the technical requirements of the systems, evaluate on the proposed solutions, work on relevant approvals, execute the implementation of enhancement or technical refresh as well as maintenance of the systems.

Responsibilities

Key responsibilities include:

  • Manage ANS projects/ systems including cyber-security implementations, as well as the design and engineering information security (e.g. authentication, perimeter security, security compliance tools), technology systems (software & hardware), and security policies / procedures.
  • Implement solutions to enhance cyber-security posture (e.g. cyber defenses, mitigation measures) to meet CAAS’, national, international standards and requirements.
  • Work closely with multiple stakeholders both internal and external (including other government agencies, system suppliers, maintenance operators, operation users, IT consultants/auditors etc) which include coordinate, liaise, support and conduct meetings to facilitate and validate the implementation in accordance with national and international cybersecurity standards and requirements.
  • Coordinate, liaise, support and conduct internal as well as external audit needs/issues including technical discussions and internal audits (e.g. scanning exercises, penetration tests).
  • Formulate process and procedures relating to cyber security through continuous engagement with the various stakeholders including the regulator, industry players and relevant agencies.
  • Keep abreast of the latest industry cybersecurity practices and technologies as well as emerging threats and vulnerabilities, then recommend appropriate controls for implementation to improve the ANS systems security posture.
  • Conduct investigations into security breaches to determine the cause of the incidents and work closely with multiple stakeholders both internal and external to resolve the incidents, participate in post-incident reporting and study/implement the proposed enhancement to the systems and infrastructure to close the security gaps.
  • Manage relevant security documentation and updating of the ANS Group's overall security programme, including planning, coordinating and conducting relevant training for security and assurance matters to raise and maintain high cyber security awareness in the ANS Group.
  • Coordinate internal and external audit needs/issues and participate in technical discussions and internal audit (e.g. scanning exercises, penetration tests).
jobRequirements:
• Trained in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering (Computing/ Electrical/ Electronics/ Telecommunication) or equivalent
  • Professional certification such as Certified Information Security Auditors (CISA) and/or Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) would be advantageous.
  • An active professional certification in Cybersecurity or Information Security from ISACA, (ISC)2 or equivalent will be an advantage
  • At least 8-10 years of relevant experience in system project implementation and cybersecurity compliance and/or cybersecurity work experiences in ICT infrastructure or network implementation
  • Possess good experience in managing cybersecurity projects, preferably having gone through at least one project implementation life cycle
  • Strong domain knowledge of information security governance and risk management, controls, vulnerability assessment/penetration testing, compliance, business continuity, investigations, system architecture and design, legal, and industry IT and cyber security best-practices.
  • Able to show understanding of the relationship between cybersecurity and the broader business goals and objectives
  • Self-motivated and independent, a good team player with well-rounded skillset, and can-do attitude
  • Curious and passionate about cybersecurity with a hacker mindset
  • Excellent verbal, written communication and interpersonal skills
  • Strong analytical, presentation and negotiation skill

If you share our passion to make a difference in the aviation cybersecurity landscape, apply now.

Note: Your appointment designation will commensurate with your relevant work experience. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance and may be considered for placement on a permanent tenure or subsequent contract renewal.

jobDescription:

jobDescription:
We are looking for a senior, hands-on Data Architect to own the data design of our investment management platforms. You will define how investment data is sourced and ingested from multiple systems, structured and integrated within the organisation, governed and made available across front, middle and back office. You will stay close to implementation by producing models and specifications, reviewing build quality, and providing technical leadership to the team’s data specialists. The role must deliver solutions that meet MAS technology standards and applicable Whole of Government compliance requirements.

The role sits in a four-person delivery team set up to establish a unified investment data architecture that enables generative AI use cases. You will design and drive implementation of three unified data layers — portfolio holdings, structured market and economic data, and unstructured research, news and sell-side content — together with the reconciliation and retrieval infrastructure that supports specific use cases across the investment value chain. You will join at the start of the build phase, designing against a product vision and user stories.
jobResponsibilities:
Data architecture and modelling

  • Design and develop the conceptual, logical and physical data models for investment data domains: security and reference data, positions and holdings, transactions, valuations and pricing, performance, benchmarks, risk, compliance, accounting and client reporting.
  • Define and govern golden-source, reference-data and master-data standards for instruments, parties, legal entities, accounts and portfolios, including identifier strategy, entity resolution, lifecycle states, schema versioning and change control.
  • Produce implementation-ready artefacts: DDL, transformation and mapping specifications, interface contracts and data quality rules.
  • Define the IBOR / ABOR data design and the reconciliation points between investment and accounting books of record, with end-to-end auditability.
  • Define source-to-target data flows and mappings centred on SimCorp Dimension, covering market and reference data vendors, custodians, counterparties, and downstream reporting and analytics.

Unstructured data and retrieval architecture

  • Develop the conceptual, logical and physical data models for unstructured investment-information domains, including sell-side and broker research, market commentary, news, internal analytics and knowledge assets.
  • Define the architecture and standards for document ingestion, processing and indexing, ensuring that source context, document structure and temporal attributes are preserved.
  • Define metadata, taxonomy and classification standards for unstructured content to support governance, discoverability and retrieval.
  • Define the architecture and technical standards for the vector database and embedding lifecycle, including embedding model selection, index design, evaluation and retrieval optimisation, and guide the AI Engineer’s implementation.
  • Define the entity and metadata mappings that link unstructured content to portfolio holdings and trades, enabling relevant research and news to be retrieved against current exposures.
  • Design hybrid retrieval orchestration spanning all three layers (vector similarity combined with keyword filtering and metadata ranking) to support near-real-time market surveillance.

Platform and integration

  • Define integration patterns and interface standards for batch, API, messaging and event-driven exchange across the investment-data ecosystem.
  • Shape the target data platform for analytics and reporting across on-premise RDBMS / data warehouse and cloud lakehouse, and guide the migration path between them.
  • Evaluate technology and vendor options, weighing performance, resiliency, security, cost and operational complexity.
  • Take part in platform upgrades, replatforming and data migration, owning data mapping, parallel runs, cutover, reconciliation and legacy decommissioning.

Governance, quality and control

  • Develop the data-governance framework and accountable ownership model covering metadata, business and technical lineage, data quality, retention, and access rights.
  • Ensure designs meet MAS technology standards and Whole of Government compliance requirements.
  • Define data classification and access controls for sensitive investment data, applied consistently across all three layers including unstructured research content.
  • Define source-data lineage and audit requirements for reconciliation outcomes and AI retrieval; work with the AI Engineer to ensure end-to-end traceability across data, retrieval, model and application logs.

Leadership and delivery

  • Serve as the design authority for investment-data architecture, lead data design reviews, and steer change proposals through the MAS Architecture Review Committee to validate alignment with Enterprise Architecture standards.
  • Partner with portfolio management, investment operations, risk, finance, compliance and vendor teams to translate business needs into data designs.
  • Work to a defined cadence with the Investment Operations & Data Domain Expert to validate the holdings model, reconciliation logic and document classification against confirmed user stories, and with the AI Engineer to assess data-layer readiness for agent retrieval.
  • Hold decision authority for investment-data architecture. Make cross-cutting architecture and technical trade-offs jointly with the AI Engineer, subject to validation by the Domain Expert that the proposed design meets operational needs.
  • Translate complex data concepts for senior business and technology stakeholders.
  • Ensure that the data architecture provides governed metadata, semantic definitions and access controls for analytics, machine learning and generative AI use cases.
jobRequirements:
Must have:

  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • At least 10 years of relevant experience across data architecture, data modelling or senior data engineering, with substantial experience designing data solutions for investment management, asset management, institutional investment, capital markets or closely related financial-services domains.
  • Deep knowledge of investment data domains including security/reference data, positions and holdings, transactions, valuations/pricing, performance, benchmarks and IBOR/ABOR. Experience designing and implementing reconciliations across IBOR, ABOR, custodians, market data providers and downstream reporting systems.
  • Hands on experience with modern data platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, Spark, Kafka, or cloud-native data services on AWS or Azure; containerised deployment (Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Strong relational database design experience, preferably Oracle, including performance and high-availability considerations.
  • Track record of delivering at least one large-scale data migration or platform replatforming programme in financial services.
  • Working knowledge of data governance, lineage, metadata management and data quality frameworks.
  • Strong hands-on experience in conceptual, logical and physical data modelling, including relational and dimensional modelling, and in producing implementation-ready data specifications.
  • Hands-on experience with vector search and embedding-based retrieval — including vector index design, embedding model selection, and hybrid search combining vector similarity with keyword and metadata filtering.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including producing clear architecture documentation.

Preferred:

  • Hands-on experience with front-to-back investment management platforms, including their data models and data management capabilities.
  • Hands-on experience with document parsing and OCR for scanned and text-native PDFs, including layout and table extraction, and with semantic chunking strategies suited to long-form research documents.
  • Experience with market and reference data vendors such as Bloomberg, Refinitiv (LSEG) or ICE, and with economic indicator providers such as Macrobond.
  • Knowledge of private markets data, ESG data, or multi-asset portfolios.
  • Familiarity with data mesh, data products and federated governance concepts.
  • Experience designing data foundations for retrieval-augmented generation or similar AI retrieval patterns in a regulated environment.
  • Programming experience in SQL, Python or Java.

  • Balances architectural standards with pragmatic delivery.
  • Comfortable owning design decisions and defending them with evidence.
  • Builds trust with business users and engineers alike.
  • Develops others and raises the team’s design quality.
  • Comfortable designing under a human-in-the-loop operating principle, where every automated output must remain reviewable and auditable.

jobDescription:
As end users become more discerning, design is no longer confined to a single space, product or interface. It is holistic, connected and experiential.

We are looking for a designer with a strong background in Interior Design or Spatial Design who is passionate about creating meaningful experiences across spaces, products, services and interactions. You see spaces not merely as physical environments, but as experiences that influence how people engage, connect, navigate and interact.
jobResponsibilities:
In this role, you will shape the next generation of experience designers through teaching, curriculum development, student mentorship, industry collaboration and applied projects. You will bring an Interior Design and Spatial Design lens to the Diploma in Experience Design, helping students understand how human-centred design, placemaking, emerging technologies and spatial storytelling come together to create memorable and meaningful experiences.

  • Conduct lessons and develop curriculum, learning resources and assessments in experience design, covering design research, human-centred design, design thinking, ideation, visualisation, prototyping and design development across products, spaces, services and interactions.

  • Mentor and supervise students through industry projects, exhibitions, competitions and multidisciplinary collaborations involving spaces, products, services and digital experiences.
  • Lead or support industry collaborations, consultancy projects and applied research initiatives related to experience design, spatial innovation and emerging technologies.

  • Keep curriculum and learning experiences current through developments in sustainability, inclusive design, smart environments, immersive and XR-enabled experiences, digital twins and Generative AI for design exploration.
  • Build and sustain strategic industry partnerships to support applied projects, internships, consultancy opportunities, CET initiatives and graduate employability.
  • Support course management, academic administration, student recruitment, outreach activities and school-wide strategic initiatives.
  • Develop, deliver and support Continuing Education and Training (CET) programmes and industry capability development initiatives related to experience design, spatial design and emerging design practices.
jobRequirements:
• Relevant qualification in Interior Design, Spatial Design, Architecture or a related discipline, with at least 5 years of relevant industry experience preferred.
  • Strong industry portfolio demonstrating successful spatial, environmental or experiential design projects.
  • Demonstrated experience in the end-to-end design process, including research, concept development, spatial planning, design development, documentation, prototyping and presentation.
  • Strong understanding of spatial design principles, user-centred design, materiality, construction considerations and experiential environments.
  • Ability to connect spatial design with products, services, interactions and digital technologies to create cohesive user experiences.
  • Awareness of current and emerging practices in sustainable design, inclusive design, smart spaces, immersive environments and experience-led placemaking.
  • Passion for education, mentoring and nurturing the next generation of designers.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation and project management skills.
  • Experience in teaching, mentoring, coaching, training or leading design teams will be an advantage.

• Facilitate communication and follow-ups between the various teams involved in the testing process to ensure timely and effective resolution of issues.
• Maintain clear and accurate project documentation, including meeting minutes, test plans, test cases, defect logs, and status reports.
• Leverage AI tools where appropriate to enhance productivity and the quality of work, such as drafting documentation, analysing data, generating test cases, or summarising meeting discussions.
• Assist with other ad hoc tasks to support the broader project team as needed.

jobDescription:
Rehabilitation & Social Mobility Policy (RSMP) Directorate develops policies and programmes which: 
a) Deliver stability, self-reliance and social mobility for lower income families 
b) Protect individuals and families from abuse and neglect or problem gambling 
c) Rehabilitate individuals from social dysfunction. 

Family Intervention Division develops and reviews policies which enhance intervention, stability and resilience of youths with complex needs, youths-at-risk of offending, youth offenders, and vulnerable families (including those with problem gamblers).
jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of a dynamic team driving policy and service transformation efforts to better support youths with complex needs, youths at risk and youths who offend.

The work involves reviewing, rationalising and developing evidence-based policies, programmes and service models across the youth ecosystem, with the aim of strengthening identification of vulnerable youths, enhancing early intervention, tightening coordination across systems, and improving outcomes for vulnerable youths and their families. You will work closely with partners across Government, social service agencies and community stakeholders to develop integrated and evidence-informed solutions to complex social challenges. 

You will be part of the secretariat for the National Committee on Preventing Offending and Reoffending. Depending on the level of appointment, you may also lead strategic projects, supervise officers, and represent MSF in cross-agency policy discussions and workgroups.
jobRequirements:
•	Develop, review and implement policies relating to vulnerable youths across the continuum - from youths with complex needs, to youths at risk of offending and youth offenders - addressing identification, early intervention and prevention, and rehabilitation needs. This involves conducting horizon scanning, data analysis, and ground sensing to identify emerging social trends, service gaps and system challenges affecting these youths, international best practices, formulating policy responses and integration between different systems such as education, social services, healthcare, and youth justice services.
•	Forge partnerships and closely collaborate with Government agencies, service providers, schools and community partners to facilitate policy formulation, communication and implementation of policies, programmes and service models.
•	Develop outcome-focused performance indicators, and monitoring and evaluation frameworks to assess the effectiveness of programmes and interventions, and developing cross-cutting and longer-term strategies to meet policy objectives.

Overall, your role requires you to be a strategic thinker with strong analytical, research, and communication skills. You will be responsible for developing policies that enhance the outcomes for vulnerable youths and their families.

Competencies required 

•	Strong analytical, conceptual and problem-solving skills.
•	Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
•	Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management capabilities.
•	Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
•	Strong teamwork and collaboration skills.
•	Interest in social policy, youth development, offender rehabilitation, mental health, disability, family services or related fields.

The following would be advantageous:
•	Experience in policy development, service planning, strategy, programme management or research.
•	Knowledge of youth development, youth offending, family intervention. 
•	Experience in programme evaluation or outcomes measurement.
•	Experience working across multiple agencies or sectors to drive policy or service transformation initiatives.

jobDescription:
The Competency-Driven Growth Office (CDGO) in the Public Service Division drives the Public Service’s shift towards Competency-Driven Growth (CDG), where officers’ growth and development are anchored on competencies — the skills, knowledge and behaviours needed to perform and grow in their roles. 

 

As Manager / Senior Manager in CDGO, you will anchor how the CDG story comes together and is experienced by officers across the Public Service. CDG comprises different policies, programmes, tools and initiatives that support officers in their growth and development. A key part of this role is to connect these different efforts into a coherent narrative, so that officers understand not just individual initiatives, but how they fit together and what CDG means for their own growth and careers. You will work closely with the PSD Communications team and Clusters within PSD to shape and implement this narrative and find practical and engaging ways to bring CDG to life for officers.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Steward the CDG narrative 

Develop and maintain a clear and coherent narrative for CDG, connecting the various policies, programmes, tools and initiatives that contribute to officers’ growth and development. 

Work across PSD teams to identify the common threads across different initiatives and translate them into a story that makes sense from an officer’s perspective. 

Help teams position individual initiatives within the broader CDG narrative, so that communications reinforce rather than fragment the overall employee experience. 

Translate complex or policy-heavy concepts into simple, relatable messages that help officers understand what CDG means for them and how they can take charge of their career development. 

Maintain coherence in the CDG narrative as policies and programmes evolve. 

2. Bring CDG to life for officers 

Develop and implement the CDG communications approaches that make CDG tangible, relevant and useful to officers. 

Identify the moments, channels and formats through which officers can encounter and understand CDG, moving beyond awareness towards helping officers take meaningful action for their own growth. 

Develop practical resources, content and experiences that show officers how competencies connect to everyday aspects of their careers — such as understanding their strengths and gaps, having regular career conversations, identifying development opportunities and taking actions to grow. 

Surface stories, examples and practices that demonstrate what competency-driven growth looks like in practice. 

Test and refine communications based on how officers understand and respond to them. 
 

3. Connect communications across CDG initiatives 

Maintain an overview of major CDG-related initiatives and communications across relevant PSD teams. 

Identify opportunities to sequence, connect or consolidate communications so that officers experience CDG as a coherent journey rather than a series of separate programmes. 

Work with initiative owners to sharpen the officer-facing proposition of their work and ensure alignment with the broader CDG narrative. 

Support key CDGO communications and milestones, including presentations, campaigns, resource packs and other officer-facing materials. 

4. Strengthen the overall CDG experience 

Bring an officer-centric perspective to CDGO’s work, continually asking how policies, programmes and communications come together from an officer’s point of view. 

Identify gaps or disconnects in the way officers encounter CDG and work with relevant teams to improve the experience. 

Explore new ways of making CDG easier to understand and act on, including through better content, communications, design and digital approaches. 

Work across organisational boundaries to build greater coherence between policy intent, programme implementation and officers’ lived experience of CDG.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone who is a strong storyteller and systems thinker — someone who can see the connections across multiple initiatives and turn them into a simple, compelling narrative. You should be comfortable working in an environment where the story is still evolving. You will need to understand the substance behind different policies and programmes, identify what matters to officers, and work with communications professionals and policy teams to translate this into something meaningful and actionable. 


You should have: 

Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly the ability to make policy or technical concepts accessible and relevant. 

Some experience in strategic communications and storytelling, with the ability to turn complex and fragmented information into a coherent narrative. 

Strong synthesis and conceptual thinking skills, with the ability to see connections across different policies, programmes and initiatives. 

Good stakeholder management and collaboration skills, particularly when working across teams with different objectives and areas of expertise. 

Good judgement and sensitivity to organisational context. 

An experimental mindset and willingness to test different ways of communicating and engaging officers. 

Experience in strategic communications, employee communications, change communications, policy, organisational development, employee experience or related work would be advantageous. 


Our Core Competencies 

The role will draw particularly strongly on OCCs relating to: 

Thinking clearly and making sound judgements — making sense of multiple policies, programmes and perspectives and identifying the underlying story that connects them. 

Working as One Public Service — working across PSD teams to build a coherent CDG experience. 

Improving and innovating continuously — experimenting with different ways of making CDG tangible and relevant, and refining approaches based on how officers respond. 

Keep learning and putting skills into action — understanding officers’ needs and experiences and applying those insights to improve how CDG is communicated and experienced.

•	Support organisation-wide events and staff welfare activities. 
•	Undertake other duties and special projects assigned by management.
jobRequirements:
Experience 
•	At least 3 to 5 years’ of relevant experience in programme management, training or capability development, administration, or related fields. Either local and/or international experience are welcome.
•	Experience in handling procurement, vendor management, or financial administration processes would be advantageous. 
•	Experience in conducting training needs analysis, organising workshops, or coordinating staff development initiatives would be an asset. 
Competencies 
•	Strong organisational and programme management skills, with meticulous attention to detail. 
•	Sound financial and administrative judgement, with the ability to manage budgets, vendor payments and compliance matters accurately. 
•	Good stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build relationships with internal and external partners, including government agencies and vendors.

•	Curious and committed to continuous learning, with an interest in deepening subject-matter knowledge to enhance work outcomes.

•	Procurement, vendor management and financial administration

•	Evaluating health technologies (e.g. drugs, vaccines, medical technologies, cell and gene therapies). Our evidence-based evaluations inform funding decisions and appropriate use through technology guidances. We also track utilisation and outcomes, and develop strategies to drive adoption; 

•	Developing and publishing clinical guidelines that guide healthcare professionals (HCPs) on specific areas of clinical practice.

•	Providing healthcare professional education to assist HCPs in applying the best available evidence in their practice

•	Delivering healthcare consumer education, through information and tools that help patients and caregivers learn about medical conditions and treatment options.

This role offers the opportunity to develop capabilities in policy development, strategic planning and managing diverse stakeholders across the public and private sectors. You will work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, and contribute to shaping ACE's strategic direction and policies.

•	Be at the forefront of health policy in Singapore, working on issues that directly shape patient care and healthcare system outcomes
•	Gain broad exposure across policy, strategy, stakeholder engagement and corporate functions in a single role
•	Work in a collaborative team that values intellectual rigour, initiative and continuous learning
•	Seek opportunities for professional development, including engagement with international HTA bodies and policy networks.

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.

•	Cultivate strategic partnerships with local and international partners, identifying opportunities for knowledge exchange, joint initiatives and policy learning

About the role
• Drive the adoption of emerging technologies and innovative solutions for underground mapping and infrastructure data management.

  • Work with agencies, industry and academia to address technical and operational barriers to data sharing and integration.

  • Contribute to the development and growth of the SpatialX Community of Practice as a platform for knowledge sharing, collaboration and innovation.
  • Organise and support technical exchanges, learning journeys, industry engagements and showcases of emerging technologies.

jobDescription:
Singapore Tourism Board's Data Exploration and Partnerships (DXP) department is shaping the data landscape for Singapore's tourism sector, and this role is central to that mission.

As our Data Partnerships Manager, you will identify tourism industry data needs, forge strategic data partnerships, and design data use cases that generate actionable insights for STB and the broader tourism ecosystem. This is a high-impact, high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of partnerships development, data strategy and analysis, and industry transformation.

Success in this position means building a robust ecosystem of data partnerships that delivers measurable value to Singapore's tourism sector, while progressively elevating the industry's data capability. You will serve as the bridge between STB's strategic data needs and the broader tourism ecosystem, ensuring that partnerships and data exploration initiatives translate into insights that drive real tourism outcomes. You will report directly to the Head of Department and work closely with line units across STB, government agencies, and industry partners.

What makes this role unique is the breadth of impact it offers: brokering strategic data partnerships, designing and running data pilots that surface actionable insights, and guiding tourism businesses in translating data into real business decisions. All of this within a newly established department where you will help shape how we work and make an impact on Singapore's tourism data landscape.
jobResponsibilities:
Board wide Data Needs Assessment and Coordination
You will consolidate and review data needs from line units across Singapore Tourism Board, conducting comprehensive gap analysis and research to fulfill data gaps within STB. This involves facilitating requirements gathering with line units and external stakeholders, researching data providers in the market, prioritising data requirements based on business impact, and coordinating across departments to resolve overlapping data needs and build a consolidated view of STB's data landscape. You will synthesise these findings into a prioritised data acquisition pipeline that guides STB’s data acquisition and partnership decisions.


Data Partnership Development and Management
You will proactively identify, evaluate, and establish strategic data partnerships with tourism industry players, technology providers, and government agencies. This includes building and maintaining a pipeline of prospective partners, conducting market research, assessing the commercial and strategic value of partnership opportunities, leading negotiations, and structuring agreements that deliver mutual benefit and long-term sustainability.

Beyond establishing partnerships, you will manage ongoing partner relationships to ensure continued value creation, and work with internal departments to develop the governance and processes that underpin our Data Partnerships work, including frameworks, standard operating procedures, partnership templates, and performance monitoring mechanisms. All partnership activities need to be conducted in compliance with data protection regulations and government policies, with best practices documented and scaled across multiple arrangements.


Data Use Case Design and Pilot Implementation
You will design new data use cases that demonstrate the business value of tourism data, including working closely with internal and external stakeholders to define hypotheses, dataset requirements, success metrics, resource requirements, and implementation timelines. You will plan and execute end-to-end data pilots, which involve setting up small-scale data pipelines and data ingestion processes, performing data transformation and calculations, exploratory data analysis, creating dashboards, and generating analysis and insights that inform tourism strategy and operations. You will document pilot findings and translate results into clear recommendations on whether and how to scale successful use cases into sustainable data products on STAN, our core data and analytics platform.


Industry Capability Building
You will design and deliver industry engagement programmes that equip tourism businesses with the knowledge and skills to use STB's data assets and insights for practical business decision-making. This includes conducting outreach and training sessions that guide industry stakeholders — such as hotels, attractions, and tour operators — in interpreting and applying tourism data to their specific business contexts, whether to sharpen their marketing strategies, inform product development, or identify new visitor segments.

To ensure these programmes are targeted and effective, you will assess the data capability and maturity levels of Singapore's tourism industry, mapping existing skills, tools, and practices to identify gaps. Based on these findings, you will develop capability uplift plans, training materials, and long-term strategies that progressively build the industry's ability to leverage data for competitive advantage, while also strengthening STB's internal data capabilities.

You will track and measure the impact of these initiatives using data maturity assessments and engagement outcomes, and contribute to positioning STB as a trusted thought leader and enabler in tourism data capability through publications, industry events, and sector-wide initiatives.

Master planner. Developer. Since its inception in 1968, JTC has played a strategic role in ensuring Singapore stays innovative, dynamic, and sensitive to global manufacturing trends.

jobDescription:
As Director, Asset & Portfolio Management, you will drive the strategic management and performance optimisation of JTC's industrial real estate portfolio. You will shape portfolio strategy, drive capital recycling decisions, and design frameworks that maximise risk-adjusted returns while supporting Singapore's national development objectives. You will play a pivotal role in positioning JTC's portfolio for long-term resilience and relevance, ensuring our industrial estates remain competitive, financially sustainable, and aligned with evolving economic priorities. You will also set the direction for cross-divisional collaboration, stakeholder engagement, and performance reporting.

You will lead a team responsible for asset planning, portfolio analytics, and value creation initiatives across a diverse base of industrial properties—including standard factories, highrise multiple-user developments, business parks, and specialised facilities.

This role combines commercial acumen, stakeholder management, and data-driven decision-making to maximise portfolio value while supporting JTC's broader mission of industrial development and sustainability.
jobResponsibilities:
Portfolio Strategy & Performance

  • Develop and execute asset and portfolio strategies aligned with JTC's corporate objectives, market conditions, and government policy directions.
  • Oversee portfolio performance monitoring, including occupancy, rental income, asset utilisation, and returns analysis.
  • Identify opportunities for value enhancement through repositioning, redevelopment, tenant mix optimisation, and lease restructuring.

Development Pipeline and Building Programme

  • Establish, maintain, and regularly refresh JTC’s long term building programme that translates JTC's portfolio strategy into a sequenced, prioritised development pipeline aligned with Singapore's long-term industrial and economic objectives and responsive to evolving market conditions and national priorities.
  • Determine the appropriate mix of development typologies — including single-user factories, multi-user factories, and specialised facilities — and their phasing across the programme horizon, balancing near-term demand with long-term portfolio needs.
  • Integrate the building programme with capital planning and budgeting cycles, ensuring development commitments are properly funded, phased, and reflected in long-term financial forecasts.
  • Use the building programme as a strategic tool to proactively shape portfolio composition.

Asset Lifecycle Management

  • Lead the lifecycle management of industrial assets, from acquisition and development through operation and divestment or redevelopment.
  • Develop and maintain asset-level business plans for each property, setting clear objectives for income performance, capital expenditure, tenancy strategy, and long-term value creation.
  • Partner with development, engineering, and operations teams to ensure asset quality and operational efficiency.
  • Drive sustainability and ESG initiatives across the portfolio in line with JTC's green growth agenda.

Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of asset and portfolio management professionals.
  • Present portfolio insights and strategic recommendations to senior management and relevant committees.
  • Engage with internal stakeholders (finance, legal, planning, development, cluster and facility management) and external partners to align on portfolio initiatives.

Market Intelligence & Innovation

  • Monitor market trends, competitor activity, and regulatory changes affecting the industrial real estate sector.
  • Champion the use of data analytics, proptech solutions, and digital tools to enhance portfolio decision-making.
jobRequirements:
Experience

  • Minimum 15 years of relevant experience in asset management, portfolio management, or real estate investment—preferably with exposure to industrial, logistics, or commercial properties.
  • Proven track record leading asset or portfolio management functions, including P&L responsibility.
  • Experience in a government, statutory board, REIT, or institutional real estate environment is advantageous.

Qualifications

  • Background in Real Estate, Business Administration, Finance, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Postgraduate qualifications (e.g., MBA, MSc Real Estate) or professional certifications (e.g., CFA, CAIA, RICS) are a plus.

  • Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Collaborative, solutions-oriented mindset with the ability to work across diverse teams.
  • Familiarity with Singapore's industrial real estate landscape and regulatory environment.
  • Understanding of sustainability frameworks and ESG considerations in real estate.

Transit Ticketing System is an integrated fare collection and contactless smart card payment system that enables commuters to pay for their public transport journeys across Singapore and consists of frontend system (MRT/LRT fare gates, bus fare readers, top up machines devices and applications) and backend system (servers, network, infrastructure and applications).

System Delivery
• Lead exciting transformation initiatives, by developing business cases, reviewing business requirements and overseeing enhancement deliveries that improve the ticketing experience for millions of commuters.
• Collaborate with technology partners, operators, vendors and internal teams to turn commuter needs, service insights and market trends to solve real-world operational challenges and uplift the end-to-end ticketing experience.

• Strengthen system governance by managing service provider contracts, audits, compliance actions, metrics and provide recommendation to management to support sound decision-making.

System Maintenance
• Manage and review the operational performance and service level agreement reports of frontend and backend systems from the contractors.

• Oversee incident management, root cause analysis and service recovery for ticketing system disruptions, working closely with operators, contractors, internal technical team and other stakeholders.

• Assess and approve operational, commuter, and financial impact analysis, as well as risk mitigation controls proposed by technical delivery and contractor teams, and seek system owner endorsement where required.

• Serve as the custodian of the Transit Ticketing System Business Continuity Plan by overseeing its maintenance, participating in tabletop exercises and collaborating with stakeholders to support effective crisis management.

• Oversee asset management for the Transit Ticketing System, ensuring contractors maintain frontend and backend assets in accordance with contractual requirements.

You will design, build and maintain components, patterns and design tokens, including variants, theming and documentation. You will build accessibility into every component so products meet the Whole-of-Government Digital Service Standards, including WCAG AA. You will work with front-end engineers to keep design and code aligned, using tools such as Code Connect and Storybook.

AI tooling

You will build AI tools that help designers work faster and stay on-system, such as Figma plugins, custom agents, skills and prompt templates. You will structure the design system so AI tools can read and apply it, through machine-readable documentation, tokens and component data exposed through MCP or similar methods. You will write scripts to automate design system tasks such as audits, token sync and documentation. You will test new AI tools and share what works with the design team.

Adoption and governance

You will support the product designers and engineers who use the system, through reviews and clear guidance. You will audit products for one-off patterns and drift, and decide with the team what joins the system. You will run a contribution model so teams can propose and add components. You will track adoption and report where the system helps and where it falls short.

jobTitle: Deputy/Assistant Director, Monetary & Domestic Markets Management Department
agencyDescription: MAS is the central bank of Singapore. Our mission is to promote sustained non-inflationary economic growth, and a sound and progressive financial centre.
jobDescription: The Monetary & Domestic Markets Management Department (MDD) conducts market operations to implement MAS’ monetary policy and serves as the fiscal agent of the Singapore Government.
jobResponsibilities:
Working within a tight-knit team of high-performing officers, you will undertake foreign exchange intervention operations to manage the Singapore dollar within its policy band, money market operations to manage liquidity conditions within the banking system, and issue Singapore Government Securities. You will also be responsible for gathering market intelligence and providing updates to MAS ministers and senior management.


Besides the above duties, you will be involved in a range of projects, typically working with various internal and external stakeholders including government ministries, foreign central banks, primary dealers and other market participants. Depending on the team in which you are placed, this can include:


  • Monetary management: You will lead projects to enhance the conduct of foreign exchange and liquidity management operations, including to ensure readiness for intervention and lender of last resort functions amidst heightened financial market volatility.
  • Domestic markets: You will drive initiatives to grow the sovereign bond market as the bedrock of Singapore’s capital markets, and participate in sovereign bond issuances. You will also explore ways to enable greater retail access to Singapore Government Securities.
  • Markets information infrastructure: You will develop systems and data analytics solutions to support central bank operations. You will also be involved in projects to re-design processes and explore new tech solutions to improve our operations.

The work is interesting and challenging. You can expect to gain:

  • A first-hand understanding of how Singapore’s monetary policy is implemented and how government borrowings are conducted;
  • Mandate and wherewithal to tangibly impact financial markets, the economy and the general public;
  • The opportunity to engage with experienced industry players (e.g. banks, institutional investors in Singapore Government Securities and other domestic market participants) as well as other central bankers; and
  • Experience across all stages of the policy life cycle, from conceptualisation to implementation.
jobRequirements:
The ideal candidate:


  • Is energetic and keen to learn, with an interest in macroeconomics, financial markets or monetary policy.
  • Is a team player with a strong commitment to public service.
  • Is analytical and detail oriented, with a strong grasp of numerical concepts.
  • Has good writing, communication and presentation skills.
  • Takes initiative and is self-driven to learn and contribute.

No prior work experience or degree in economics / finance is required, as extensive training will be conducted on-the-job. Applicants should be Singapore citizens. Applicants should be prepared that they will be periodically tasked to monitor foreign exchange markets overnight as part of their operational duties.


You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

jobResponsibilities:
Software Engineer, Systems team — Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM), Land Transport Authority. You will build the digital products that make safe autonomous vehicle deployments possible in Singapore, at scale. This role is open at two levels — a core set of responsibilities applies to all hires, with additional ownership and leadership expectations for more senior candidates (see section below).

CAM leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale safely. The Systems team builds the digital tools behind that mission — for instance, developing a monitoring system for AVs to collect and analyse AV operational data to support LTA’s regulatory and safety assurance work. But the role is broader than any single product: wherever software can move AV deployment forward, that is where we will build.

As a software engineer, you will

  • Design and build production-quality digital products end to end: You will be expected to understand and take ownership of problem statements, before designing and architecting systems on cloud infrastructure — owning features from conception through deployment and ongoing maintenance.
  • Build the suite of safety-assurance products LTA needs to regulate AVs reliably: analytics, dashboards and visualisations; implement enforcement and performance tracking, event management and data-anomaly alerts.
  • Identify and address pain points bottlenecking deployment velocity: Work in a tight-knit and cross-functional CAM team, with a clear north-star of driving safe AV deployments at scale — which includes non-passenger vehicles and AVs on public paths (Autonomous Mobile Robots). Talk to users and industry, identify gaps and propose products that move AV deployments forward.
  • Evolve our products to the next bound: Our product portfolio spans several digital products, including the AV Monitoring System that monitors every AV on Singapore’s public roads. We are building for scale so that systems can handle a growing number of AVs and developers amidst evolving needs; strengthening data pipelines and system observability for high-volume telemetry, and potentially integrating with other LTA enterprise platforms for operations and incident management.
  • Keep what we ship healthy: monitor and support production systems that AV operations and regulation depend on, including helping respond to incidents when they arise.

Apply AI, ML and Data Analytics where it adds value

AI is increasingly central to how we build and what our products do. You can expect to apply it in areas such as:

  • Engineering productivity: Safe use of AI tools, including coding assistants and multi-agent workflows, will be expected.
  • Anomaly and risk detection: Automatically surface unsafe patterns found from AV operational telemetry and video data, so issues are caught earlier before scale.
  • Operational intelligence: Address the pain points faced by operations and regulatory colleagues as deployments scale, through natural-language querying and automated summaries of performance and trends.
  • Deployment and planning: Implement tools and optimisation algorithms to inform demand/supply estimation and deployment feasibility.

Because safety assurance is new ground, you will also

  • Help shape what we build, not just how — identify gaps and propose products that strengthen AV safety and drive AV deployments.
  • Work with policy, operations and regulatory colleagues to turn requirements into working software, and explain technical trade-offs to non-technical audiences.
  • Know when to build versus when to adopt open-source or commercial solutions, so effort goes into delivering real value rather than re-solving solved problems.

If you join as a more senior hire, you will also

  • Lead technical discussions, influence architectural decisions, and own technical direction across products.
  • Establish testing, CI/CD and code-quality practices, and balance pragmatic delivery with long-term technical sustainability.
  • Set engineering best practices, mentor other engineers and support recruitment.

If you want your code to shape how a new technology is adopted safely while driving deployment needs at scale, we want to hear from you.

Self-directed and curious in picking up new knowledge, and invested in team success beyond individual contributions. Motivated by the mission of driving safe AV deployments at scale.

Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. It maintains an oversight of national cybersecurity functions and works with sector leads to protect Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. CSA is part of the Prime Minister’s Office and is managed by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information. For more news and information, please visit www.csa.gov.sg
jobDescription:
Singapore’s push for digitalization coupled with cyber threats that are ever evolving in scale and sophistication paved the way for a continuously growing demand for cybersecurity professionals. As a result, there exists a need to strengthen the pipeline of skilled cybersecurity professionals through identifying and empowering individuals with cybersecurity aptitude and good learning attitude to take on cybersecurity roles. 

CSA’s Cybersecurity Development Programme (CSDP) is a 12-month programme designed to develop both fresh graduates and working professionals into cybersecurity talents in the public sector, with the aim of building cybersecurity capabilities to secure Singapore’s digital economy and infrastructure.
jobResponsibilities:
CSDP is a 12-month programme that consists of two phases: a 1-month classroom training phase, followed by an 11-month job posting.*

*Please note that the programme curriculum may be subject to change (including programme duration/training curriculum, etc). The programme stated below is accurate as of August 2026.

Phase 1: Classroom Training

CSDP officers will undergo a rigorous curriculum in their first month to build both technical and professional capabilities. Officers will undergo courses that will lead to cybersecurity certifications such as:

•	SANS SEC504
•	SANS ICS310
•	Cisco Certified CyberOps Associate

Officers will also receive training in professional skills such as Stakeholder Management and Effective Writing in the Public Service.

Phase 2: Job Posting

After the classroom training phase, CSDP officers will be posted to a CSA division or partner government agency for the remaining 11 months. During their posting, officers will gain hands-on experience in mainly one of these cybersecurity domains:

•	Malware Analysis
•	Digital Forensics & Incident Response
•	Emerging Technologies
•	Penetration Testing
•	Cybersecurity Solutions and Consultancy
•	Cybersecurity Operations Centre
•	Threat Intelligence
•	Governance, Risk and Compliance

Job postings will take into consideration each candidate’s interests, suitability and cybersecurity manpower needs across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). Further assessments may be required to determine a candidate’s suitability for specific roles, and the final posting decision rests with CSA.

Gain Exposure Beyond Your Posting

Throughout the programme, CSDP officers will have opportunities to work on cybersecurity projects at the national level, undergo further technical and non-technical training, and engage with recognised industry partners and the public.

These experiences will enable officers to broaden their cybersecurity expertise, develop valuable professional networks and contribute towards strengthening Singapore’s cybersecurity posture.

Upon successful completion of the 12-month programme, CSDP officers may continue their employment with CSA or be forward deployed to another government agency, subject to satisfactory performance and successful matching to a suitable role across the Whole-of-Government (WOG).

CSA is currently located at the Punggol Digital District.

jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of the Board’s network security team responsible for protecting systems, networks, and endpoints from cybersecurity threats. As an NDR & EDR Engineer, you will manage and operationalise Network Detection and Response (NDR) and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) platforms, working closely with internal teams to ensure robust threat detection and response capabilities. 

In this role, you will: 
• Deploy, configure, and maintain NDR and EDR solutions across on-premises and cloud environments, in accordance with applicable ICT security policies and standards.
• Develop, tune, and maintain detection rules and alert policies to improve detection accuracy and minimise false positives across networks and endpoints.
• Monitor, triage security alerts and escalate incidents to the SOC or Incident Response team in accordance with established procedures.
• Support incident response and forensic investigations, including analysis of endpoint and network telemetry, evidence handling and reporting. 
• Conduct proactive threat hunting using NDR and EDR telemetry to identify indicators of compromise, suspicious and advanced persistent threats (APTs) targeting government infrastructure.
• Integrate NDR and EDR platforms with SIEM and security orchestration tools to support effective detection, investigation and response workflows.
• Ensure platform configurations and detection logic comply with applicable security frameworks, including the Government Instruction Manual on IT Management (IM8) and relevant cybersecurity guidelines.
• Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation including platform configurations, standard operating procedures, and incident runbooks.
• Liaise with vendors, GovTech and internal stakeholders on platform updates, threat intelligence sharing, security advisories and related operational matters.
jobRequirements:
We value the diverse talents and experiences that each individual brings to the table. While mastery of every requirement may not be necessary, familiarity and expertise in some of the following areas will position you for success within this team.
• Experience in cybersecurity engineering or security operations, including hands-on experience with EDR and/or NDR platforms such as CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Trend Vision One, Darktrace, ExtraHop, Vectra AI or Corelight. 
• Knowledge of network protocols, traffic analysis, and endpoint telemetry and forensic investigation techniques
• Good understanding of Windows and Linux internals, including processes, memory, registry and security models, with experience analysing event logs for threat detection.
• Familiarity with attack and persistence techniques (e.g. Pass-the-Hash, Kerberoasting, LOLBins, privilege escalation, SSH persistent) and their mapping to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, as well as experience deploying EDR agents and telemetry tools like Sysmon, auditd, and osquery.
• Proficiency in using SIEM platforms (e.g. Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, QRadar) for security log analysis and investigation.
• Ability to develop and tune detection rules and queries using languages and formats such as KQL, SPL, Sigma rules. 
• Experience supporting incident response investigations, including evidence handling, analysis and reporting.
• Ability to use scripting languages such as Python, PowerShell or Bash for automation and detection engineering.
• Familiarity with Singapore Government security frameworks including IM8, the Cybersecurity Act, and CSA's Cybersecurity Code of Practice would be advantageous. 
• Exposure to cloud environments (e.g. Azure, AWS or Government Commercial Cloud) and associated security tools would be advantageous. 
• Relevant certifications such as GCFA, GCFE, GCIA, GCED, CEH, or EDR/NDR certifications would be advantageous. 

The seniority of appointment and actual corporate job title will commensurate with individual work experiences.

Position is on a 2-year full-time contract directly under the payroll of CPF Board with potential for emplacement into a permanent position.

Social media today is no longer a supporting channel — it is where culture is made, influence is built, and travel decisions are shaped. For STB, this shift represents a significant opportunity to lead in destination marketing through sharp, insight-driven social strategy that is both creative and commercially grounded.

As the Social Strategist, you will be the resident expert on social strategy within STB's social department — developing the frameworks, playbooks, and strategic direction that the wider team builds upon. This is a role for someone who thinks deeply about where social is heading, translates that thinking into clear and actionable strategy, and is equally comfortable getting hands-on to deliver. You will work across the department and with key external partners to ensure STB's social presence is coherent, forward-looking, and effective.
jobResponsibilities:
Social Strategy Development & Oversight

You will develop, review, and own the overarching social strategy that guides the department's work. This means producing the strategic frameworks and playbooks that team members plug into as they develop strategies for their respective workstreams — ensuring that individual efforts are aligned, coherent, and laddering up to a unified social vision. You will regularly review and evolve the strategy in response to performance data, platform shifts, and broader marketing objectives, serving as the strategic backbone and thought partner for the team.

Performance Measurement & Reporting

You will own the performance for the Visit Singapore (VS) social channels. Working with the in-house social media manager, you will ensure monthly performance reports on VS channels are produced consistently and on time, and that the data is translated into clear insights and recommendations. Beyond the monthly cadence, you will lead quarterly and annual reviews — analysing performance trends, identifying what is working and what needs to change, and presenting findings to relevant stakeholders.

Channel Mix & Platform Planning

A core part of your remit is ensuring STB is investing in the right platforms at the right time. You will conduct yearly reviews of the social channel mix, assessing each platform's performance, audience fit, and strategic relevance — tracking cultural, platform, and algorithm shifts and translating them into a formal set of recommendations that shape how the department allocates its resources going forward.

Emerging Platforms, Experimentation & Prospecting

You will proactively scan for emerging channels, closed communities, and new social spaces that present strategic opportunities for STB. Critically, you will not just identify these opportunities — you will lead and run the pilots, developing go-to-market approaches, executing the test, and producing a clear assessment of viability and scalability. Where a pilot proves successful, you may continue to own and manage that channel as part of your portfolio. This requires a structured yet experimental mindset — knowing how to design a meaningful test, read the results honestly, and make a clear recommendation. You will also take the lead on horizon-scanning for the social department, synthesising signals from across the industry into actionable foresight that informs both near-term strategy and longer-term planning.

Campaign Delivery

You will be involved in developing key campaigns, driving the delivery of social strategy from planning through to execution. This means working across functions to ensure that the strategic intent of a campaign is preserved through to delivery and being hands-on where needed to make it happen.

Paid Social Oversight

Working closely with the Digital and Media team, you will oversee STB's paid social strategy, ensuring that paid efforts are meaningfully integrated with organic activity and aligned to campaign objectives.
