jobDescription:
We are looking for an experienced Senior QA Engineer / Software Test Analyst to take strong ownership of quality assurance for enterprise web applications operating in a dual-mode environment of production support and continuous feature delivery.
The role will independently plan, prepare, execute and drive testing activities end-to-end,   ensuring that system changes, production fixes, enhancements and integrations meet business requirements, quality standards and release-readiness expectations. The successful candidate must be hands-on, dependable and able to work with minimal supervision, while proactively identifying requirement gaps, edge cases, integration impacts and quality risks. The role requires the ability to test both conventional application functionality and AI-enabled capabilities, including workflows where outputs may be probabilistic or non-deterministic.
The role will also strengthen regression coverage and progressively implement appropriate test automation to improve testing efficiency, repeatability and confidence in releases.
jobResponsibilities:
Test Planning, Analysis and Preparation
•	Review and understand business requirements, functional specifications, user stories, acceptance criteria, solution changes and production fixes.
•	Independently determine test scope, approach, scenarios, dependencies, test data and areas of risk.
•	Develop, execute and maintain automated test scripts, and integrate appropriate automated tests into QA cycles and SHIP-HATS CI/CD pipelines to support continuous testing, regression assurance and release quality gates.
•	Perform impact analysis and ensure appropriate functional, integration and regression coverage for each change.
•	Proactively identify and challenge unclear, incomplete or inconsistent requirements, including edge cases, negative scenarios and downstream impacts, before they become release issues.
•	Work closely with Business Analysts, developers and business stakeholders to clarify expected system behaviour and testability.

Test Execution
•	Own and execute assigned testing activities independently with minimal supervision, from preparation through completion.
•	Perform functional, system, integration, API/interface, end-to-end and regression testing, where applicable.
•	Validate complex business rules, workflows, role-based access, data processing, interfaces and asynchronous/background processes across relevant systems.
•	Perform database and data validation using SQL or equivalent techniques where required.
•	Retest fixes and conduct risk-based regression testing to confirm that changes do not adversely affect existing functionality.
•	Maintain complete, accurate and auditable test evidence and test results.
•	Execute and analyse automated tests within SHIP-HATS CI/CD pipelines, investigate test and pipeline failures, and distinguish application defects from test-script, configuration, environment and deployment issues.
AI-Enabled Capability Testing
•	Plan and execute testing for AI-enabled capabilities and end-to-end workflows spanning application, integration and AI components.
•	Validate AI-assisted document ingestion, classification, extraction and processing across representative document types, formats and quality conditions, where applicable.
•	Evaluate AI-generated outputs against expected business outcomes and source evidence, including completeness, accuracy, consistency and traceability.
•	Design and maintain representative test datasets and expected outcomes to support repeatable evaluation and regression testing of AI-enabled capabilities.
•	Apply appropriate testing and evaluation approaches for probabilistic or non-deterministic outputs rather than relying solely on exact-output assertions.
•	Validate human-in-the-loop workflows, including user review, amendment, approval, rejection and appropriate recording of user actions.
•	Verify that relevant AI-generated outputs are traceable to supporting source information and that appropriate audit information is captured.
•	Test confidence thresholds, exception handling, fallback behaviour and escalation to human review where applicable.
•	Perform regression testing following changes to models, prompts, knowledge sources, business rules, configurations or other AI components that may affect system outcomes.
•	Work with Product Owners, business users, developers and relevant technical teams to define acceptance criteria, evaluation datasets and appropriate quality thresholds for AI-enabled capabilities.

Defect Management and Quality Risk
•	Identify, document and report defects clearly with sufficient reproduction steps, evidence and impact assessment for efficient investigation.
•	Drive defects through triage, prioritisation, investigation, resolution, retesting and closure, working closely with developers and relevant vendors.
•	Assess defect severity, business impact and regression risk, and escalate material quality concerns early.
•	Identify recurring defects, systemic quality issues or testing gaps and recommend preventive improvements.
•	Provide an objective, evidence-based view of residual quality risk and release readiness.

UAT, Production Support and Release Assurance
•	Support business users during UAT, including preparation of scenarios, test data and supporting materials where required.
•	Support defect triage and timely resolution during SIT/UAT and production-support cycles.
•	Provide clear and timely reporting on testing progress, coverage, outstanding defects, blockers, risks and recommended actions.
•	Support pre-release checks, deployment verification, production sanity testing and post-deployment verification where required.
•	Support release assurance through SHIP-HATS, including verification of automated test results, quality gates, deployment outcomes, smoke/sanity testing and relevant release evidence before production promotion.
•	Investigate production issues from a QA perspective and ensure relevant scenarios are incorporated into regression coverage.
•	Provide a clear recommendation on test completion and quality readiness before production release.

Test Automation and Continuous Improvement
•	Assess and recommend practical test automation approaches, tools and priorities based on delivery needs and return on effort.
•	Identify stable, repeatable and high-value regression scenarios suitable for automation.
•	Develop, execute and maintain automated test scripts and integrate them into QA cycles where appropriate.
•	Review automated test results, investigate failures and maintain scripts as the application evolves.
•	Continuously improve test coverage, QA standards, templates, traceability, evidence quality and testing efficiency.
•	Explore appropriate use of AI-enabled tools for test design, automation scripting, defect analysis and other QA activities, with proper validation of outputs.
Identify appropriate approaches for automating repeatable evaluation and regression testing of AI-enabled capabilities, recognising that probabilistic outputs may require different validation techniques from conventional deterministic test automation.
jobRequirements:
•	Preferably 5+ years of relevant experience in software testing / quality assurance for enterprise IT systems, with demonstrated ability to work independently and own testing outcomes.
•	Strong experience in preparing test strategies or plans, scenarios, test cases, test data and regression suites.
•	Strong functional and regression testing experience for web-based or enterprise applications with complex business workflows.
•	Experience testing APIs, interfaces or integrations between multiple systems, including end-to-end data flows.
•	Experience in defect management, including impact assessment, triage, retesting and closure.
•	Hands-on experience with test automation tools or frameworks and the ability to implement and maintain practical automation solutions.
•	Able to translate business and functional requirements into comprehensive test coverage and independently identify missing scenarios or requirements.
•	Strong analytical, problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with attention to detail and sound quality judgement.
•	Able to communicate defects, testing status, risks and release-readiness assessments clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
•	Able to work effectively with business users, Product Owners, Business Analysts, developers, technical teams and vendors in an Agile/Scrum delivery environment.
•	Familiarity with defect and work-management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps or equivalent.
•	Experience testing AI/ML-enabled, intelligent automation, document-processing or other systems involving probabilistic or non-deterministic behaviour; alternatively, demonstrated ability to understand and apply appropriate AI testing and evaluation techniques.
•	Able to design test scenarios and evaluation datasets for outputs that cannot always be validated through simple deterministic pass/fail assertions.
•	Able to validate end-to-end data and workflow behaviour across user interfaces, APIs, backend services, integrations and AI-enabled components.
•	Strong understanding of data quality, boundary conditions, negative testing, traceability and evidence-based validation.
•	Able to distinguish defects in application logic, integration, data, configuration and AI-generated behaviour, and work with the relevant technical teams to support root-cause investigation.

Good to Have

jobDescription:
The global Unmanned Systems sector has made quantum leaps and is expected to continue growing rapidly. This growth is encouraged by the interest in developing emerging technologies (such as Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) and electric-Vertical Take-Off and Landing (e-VTOL) aircraft) and innovative use-cases for both commercial and recreational use, arising from the benefits that Unmanned Systems bring across multiple industries.

To capture the potential and opportunities of the Unmanned Systems sector for Singapore, the Unmanned Systems Technology, Engineering and Planning (UTEP) Division develops strategies to assess, identify, and forge partnerships with the industry, other civil aviation authorities and research entities, to grow new business areas, initiate greenfield research and develop capabilities. The division also focuses on systems engineering, technology capabilities and strategic planning for the Unmanned Systems Group, in addition to integration, implementation and operational oversight of the maintenance of sensor and command and control (C2) systems.

As a member of the Technology and Strategic Planning section of the UTEP Division, you will develop the UAS ecosystem in Singapore to create a conducive and exciting environment for our UAS industry, while shaping the future of unmanned systems technology. You will work directly with stakeholders to grow the UAS sector, enabling new technologies and applications that will have transformative impact and potential social, economic, workforce, and environmental benefits. You will plan, strategise, coordinate, and implement initiatives to support our UAS industry, driving growth, capability and technology development, and public acceptance to enable the safe adoption of unmanned systems technology. You will also drive outreach and promotion initiatives to create a vibrant UAS ecosystem among recreational hobbyists, students, and other community stakeholders, through roadshows, workshops and educational programmes. You can expect to be involved in strategic decision-making contributing to CAAS' position as a thought leader, world-class regulator and enabler of new and emerging technologies.

If this role excites you, read on for details of the job responsibilities and requirements. We look forward to your application.
jobResponsibilities:
• Monitor and assess key emerging trends and developments in technologies and systems in the unmanned systems sector globally, conduct technical risk assessments on emerging technologies, identifying critical components/systems to focus R&D efforts on, and sense-make the implications for CAAS and Singapore.
  • Coordinate across multiple stakeholders, including other Singapore Government agencies, and drive CAAS’ strategic position and deliverables to create a vibrant UAS ecosystem in Singapore
  • Manage key accounts within the UAS industry to facilitate business development and operationalisation of new use cases, including through grant administrations, liaising on necessary regulatory requirements and providing networking opportunities.
  • Partner economic agencies (e.g. EDB) to engage foreign unmanned systems companies to anchor businesses in Singapore.
  • Partner workforce development agencies (e.g. WSG/SSG) to develop a manpower transformation map for the UAS industry in Singapore.
  • Partner educational institutes, research institutes and industry to drive innovation and technology development and build human capital in unmanned systems technologies in Singapore.
  • Engage other Singapore Government agencies, research institutes, schools, and community stakeholders to develop physical and digital infrastructure to enable recreational activities, commercial UAS operations and testbedding.

jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Research, Evaluation and Monitoring (REM) division, which drives the development of data-driven insights and analytics to inform health promotion strategies across HPB. The division focuses on translating cutting-edge research and emerging technologies into HPB programmes. By distilling learnings from diverse datasets, applied research, and innovative pilots, REM supports the translation of evidence into practice for delivery in national-scale platforms. The division also plays a key role in strengthening programme design, evaluation, and continuous improvement, ensuring that interventions are evidence-based, outcomes-driven, and relevant for real-world implementation.
jobResponsibilities:
As a member of the Analytics and Translation team in the Research, Evaluation and Monitoring division, you will work in a cross-functional, matrix team to contribute to high-impact projects in priority growth areas.


You will generate actionable insights through advanced analytics on diverse datasets (e.g. large longitudinal cohorts, sensors, and combined datasets), applying appropriate statistical and machine learning approaches to support risk prediction, population segmentation, and identification of behavioural patterns.


You will support the development and application of predictive models and segmentation approaches (e.g. clustering) to inform programme targeting, intervention design, and risk stratification, ensuring outputs are robust, interpretable, and relevant for real-world decision-making.


You will set up and support behavioural experiments and programme evaluations, including contributing to study design, data preparation, and analysis to distil research insights and evaluate suitability for translation into programme delivery.


You will develop compelling data-driven narratives for impactful storytelling to both internal and external stakeholders, translating technical findings into clear, concise, and actionable insights that inform programme and policy decisions.


You will work with cross-functional teams and external partners to support collaborations and analytics projects, contributing to delivery of strategic outcomes and facilitating knowledge sharing and learning across teams.


You will support the development of data pipelines, feature engineering, and preparation of datasets to enable efficient and scalable analytics, including working with relevant data platforms where required.
jobRequirements:
The ideal candidate will be a dynamic and self-motivated individual with a strong interest in advancing health promotion through data, research, and analytics. The candidate should be comfortable working at the intersection of data science and real-world application, and is motivated by translating insights into impact at scale.


The candidate should also possess:

  • Degree in statistics, data analytics, social sciences, life sciences, public health, or any related quantitative discipline
  • At least 2–6 years of practical experience working with data as an analyst or in a related role
  • Experience in applying statistical techniques and/or machine learning methods (e.g. regression, clustering, predictive modelling) to real-world datasets
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g. R, Python). Familiarity with Databricks, SparkR, PySpark or working with large datasets will be advantageous
  • Additional familiarity with statistical software (e.g. SPSS, STATA) will be a bonus

jobDescription:

The team's work spans both policy and operations – they identify and develop strategies to mitigate systemic vulnerabilities in Singapore's logistics sector and also develop and stress test activation plans. In an increasingly complex and uncertain environment, the team's work is central to ensuring that Singapore and the stakeholders they support can withstand, respond to, and recover from disruptions effectively.

You will work closely with colleagues across the public service and industry partners to stay up to date on expectations of- and the evolving state of Singapore's logistics sector. In this role, you will analyse complex and emerging risks that could disrupt the logistics ecosystem and translate them into clear, actionable policy recommendations. You will also design and run exercises, develop activation plans with defined triggers and coordination arrangements, and strengthen response readiness across logistics stakeholders and Whole-of-Government partners.

The portfolio is as varied as it is meaningful. No two days look the same, and the work you do will have a direct and tangible impact on Singapore's ability to navigate an increasingly uncertain world.

  • Map and develop capabilities required to bridge structural and emerging vulnerabilities in Singapore's logistics ecosystem

  • At least 2 years of relevant experience in logistics operations, supply chain management, risk management, crisis management, or public policy, with the ability to quickly develop deep sectoral knowledge
  • Strong analytical and research skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information from multiple sources, identify systemic risks, and translate findings into clear, actionable policy recommendations
  • Experience in stakeholder engagement and relationship management across both public and private sector organisations, with the ability to build trust and influence without direct authority
  • Familiarity with crisis management frameworks, business continuity planning, or emergency response planning, including the design and facilitation of tabletop or live exercises

jobDescription:
The Fiscal Policy Directorate in MOF is responsible for formulating and implementing fiscal strategies and frameworks to optimise the allocation of finite public resources, to maintain macroeconomic stability (e.g. through countercyclical fiscal policies), support economic growth, and promote social equity. This requires making difficult trade-offs across competing strategic priorities in the social, economic, security and infrastructure domains, while considering progressivity and inter-generational equity. Our work ensures that we can balance the budget and have sufficient resources to advance Singapore’s key priorities, for the benefit of Singaporean households and businesses. 

We ensure fiscal sustainability over the medium to long term by setting out plans for our revenue (e.g. taxes, returns on investment of reserves, Government fees), financing (e.g. use of bonds), expenditure, and public sector manpower priorities. This requires close collaboration with our colleagues across MOF, as well as other Government agencies.  

We are looking for a self-driven and highly motivated individual, with an interest in working with data, to join our dynamic and collaborative team. You will have the opportunity to gain a strategic overview of the government’s priorities, manage trade-offs among competing needs, and shape the public policy agenda. You will also have the opportunity to review and operationalise our budgetary policies (e.g. Block Budgets, Programme Budgets, Reinvestment Fund, Manpower Management Framework, debt management) to support our macro-allocation objectives. As a Fiscal Policy Associate, you will be required to consult widely at all levels, synthesise and analyse information effectively, generate robust policy options and exercise sound judgment over trade-offs.

Policymaking 
1.	Formulate, review and implement fiscal, budgeting, revenue, financing, debt management and public sector manpower policies to enable optimal allocation of resources across the Government and ensure fiscal sustainability 

Strategic Planning 
2.	Horizon scanning and research of future economic and social challenges/opportunities, and study the implications for Singapore 
3.	Formulate Singapore’s fiscal strategies and response to these key challenges and seed ideas for major public policy shifts 

Managing Stakeholders and Trade-offs 
4.	Work closely with stakeholders to shape the Government’s revenue and expenditure plans and ensure alignment and coherence with the Government’s strategic priorities 
5.	Analysis of fiscal impact of major policy changes and public spending programmes and manage the trade-offs across different sectors 

Data Analytics 
6.	Analyse fiscal and macroeconomic data to sense-make the impact of fiscal policies 
7.	Model and project our revenue and expenditure over the medium to long term

jobTitle: Senior Manager, (Internal Comms & Engagement), Strategic Communications
agency: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX)
agencyDescription: HTX is the world’s first Science and Technology agency that integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally-ready solutions for homeland security. As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. jobDescription:
HTX is Singapore's Science and Technology agency that brings together diverse scientific and engineering capabilities to develop transformative, operationally ready solutions for public safety. As a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower the Home Team with cutting-edge capabilities. Guided by our mission to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team's advantage, we are committed to keeping Singapore the safest place on planet Earth.

We are looking for a creative, hands-on communications professional to tell the stories of HTX’s culture and people. The role focuses on multimedia storytelling for internal channels and events, complemented by engagement activities that embody HTX’s value of Exuberance. You will also develop and refresh content for the HTX Gallery and HTX’s presence at the Home Team Gallery.
Working with the Organisational Communications & Engagement team, you will create multimedia content that achieves shared communications and engagement goals, informed by organisational priorities and audience insights.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Create multimedia content: Develop content that meets agreed communications goals, taking creative and hands-on ownership from concept to delivery.
•	Tell engaging stories: Turn fresh angles on HTX’s people and work into authentic stories, told through written pieces, social posts and events, and adapted for eDMs, Viva Engage, eXpresso! townhalls and digital screens.
•	Curate gallery content: Plan refreshes and develop and maintain narratives and creative assets for both galleries; operations, technical maintenance and installation are outside the remit.
•	Design engaging experiences: Develop concepts and coordinate activities that connect employees, encourage participation and bring the HTX value of Exuberance to life.
•	Learn and optimise: Use content performance, participation data and employee feedback to test new approaches and improve content and activities.
•	Collaborate and deliver: Share ideas, contribute creative expertise and work closely with teammates, leaders, subject-matter experts, agencies and creative partners to achieve shared communications and engagement outcomes.
jobRequirements:
•	Strategic and creative thinking: Turn communications needs, organisational priorities and audience insights into compelling ideas and narratives.
•	Hands-on multimedia capability: End-to-end production experience spanning concepts, scripts, storyboards, interviews, video, photography, editing and design, with strong visual and editorial judgement.
•	Audience engagement: A digital-first approach and experience creating social content and activities that capture attention, encourage participation and connect employees.
•	Delivery and learning: Strong project management and collaboration skills, with the ability to take ownership and contribute to shared goals in a fast-moving environment. Curiosity and enthusiasm for learning and creating engaging employee experiences are essential; familiarity with AI-assisted creative tools is an advantage.
•	Qualifications and experience: A recognised university degree and more than 10 years’ proven experience delivering communications and employee engagement outcomes. Journalism, communications, media or design degrees are an advantage.
•	Please include a portfolio or showreel demonstrating your creative thinking and multimedia storytelling.


All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement.

agencyDescription: We aim to build a cohesive and resilient society, deepening the sense of national identity and affinity for Singapore through strengthening community bonds, promoting of the arts and heritage, youth engagement, sports development, volunteerism and philanthropy.
jobDescription:
The Government Partnerships & Engagement Group (GPEG) contributes to the development of a collaborative government that empowers partnerships and engagement (PE) with citizens for a better Singapore. It does this through the development of public sector capabilities in partnerships and engagement, external partnerships and the design and organisation of Whole-of-Government (WOG) PE initiatives. 
Within GPEG, the Planning & Development team drives the development of public sector PE capabilities in the areas of PE policy, organisational capacity, workforce planning and development, and stakeholder management and engagement.
jobResponsibilities:
As an individual contributor within the Planning & Development team, you will bring HR expertise, particularly in talent management and workforce development, to drive PE sector development workstreams across the public service. You will work closely with teammates to build a professional pool of Partnerships and Engagement (PE) practitioners from officers to Directors. Working with GPEG colleagues, agencies and their HR teams, you will plan and implement talent development and progression pathways anchored in the PE Competency Framework, connecting officers with structured opportunities to develop their competencies, gain relevant experience and prepare for broader PE responsibilities. 
•	Develop and implement PE sector development plans, using workforce data and agency needs to identify capability gaps and prioritise development opportunities for PE officers and leaders across the public service. 
•	Develop and maintain the PE Competency Framework, PE Development Roadmap and PE job archetypes, translating them into clear development and progression pathways from officer to Director levels. 
•	Design and implement competency-linked development opportunities, including structured job rotations, talent attachment programmes and fireside chats with experienced PE practitioners and leaders. Define learning objectives and intended outcomes for different career stages, and connect these opportunities into coherent development pathways. 
•	Partner agency HR teams and PE leaders to identify development needs, match officers to suitable opportunities and secure host agencies for rotations and attachments. Establish programme arrangements and follow-through so that officers can apply their learning and prepare for subsequent PE roles. 
•	Develop indicators and evaluate the impact of sector and talent development initiatives using qualitative and quantitative methods, including competency development, application of learning and progression into PE roles. Use findings to address gaps and refine development pathways and programmes. 
•	Build networks of PE practitioners and leaders across WOG to support knowledge exchange, peer learning and the sharing of good practices, strengthening professional development and a culture of partnerships and engagement.
jobRequirements:
•	At least 3 – 5 years of HR experience, particularly in talent management, is essential. You should have relevant experience designing and implementing talent development initiatives, career and progression pathways, structured rotations or attachment programmes. 
•	Ability to translate competency frameworks into practical development pathways and opportunities for officers at different career stages, from officers to Directors. Experience in public service workforce or sector development, or familiarity with partnerships and engagement work, would be advantageous. 
•	Excellent writing, communication and interpersonal skills 
•	Strong analytical and critical thinking capabilities 
•	High level of initiative and willingness to learn

agencyDescription: Singapore Customs is a government agency under the Ministry of Finance. Re-constituted on 1 April 2003, Singapore Customs is the lead agency on trade facilitation and revenue enforcement matters. It is also responsible for the implementation of customs and trade enforcement measures including those related to Free Trade Agreements and strategic goods.
jobDescription:
[A Trade Facilitator, A Trade Regulator and A Law Enforcer]
 
Singapore Customs advances Singapore’s economic development by protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. We protect revenue – that is invested in the progress and well-being of our Singapore community, making Singapore a better place today and for tomorrow. We make trade easy, fair and secure by maintaining Singapore’s status as a global trading hub while ensuring the integrity of the trading system. As part of the OneCustoms team, you will have the opportunity to take on different roles during your career with us – a Trade Facilitator, a Trade Regulator, and a Law Enforcer. You can look forward to seamless advancement opportunities with our integrated grade structure under the Customs Unified Scheme of Service (CUS).
jobResponsibilities:
In Singapore Customs, we work, play, learn and grow together as OneCustoms team. With regular job rotations under our Open Posting System that offer many opportunities for competency and skills development, you will get to experience our Customs core functions in trade facilitation, regulation and compliance as well as enforcement during the foundational phase. 
 
You lead and guide a team of officers who share a common objective of protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. 
· Trade Facilitator: You facilitate customs connectivity across borders for a seamless and resilient end-to-end international supply chain, and work closely with local and international partners to advance Singapore’s economy. 
· Trade Regulator: You safeguard Singapore’s reputation as a global trade hub by upholding the rules of trade and tariffs, and keeping a close watch on strategic goods and technologies to maintain an effective and robust regulatory regime. 
· Law Enforcer: You protect Singapore’s revenue by adopting a whole-of-government approach, and working closely with other enforcement agencies to enforce against revenue-related and trade offences. 
 
No matter what your role is or how you spend your time, the impact of your contributions count. 
 
[Sign-on Bonus] Eligible officers who are newly appointed to the Public Service and Singapore Customs will receive a sign-on bonus of $8,000 paid in two tranches. 
 
[Retention Bonus] You will receive attractive retention pay-outs in your 4th, 7th, and 10th in Customs scheme of service. 

[Starting Salary] ·  $4,398-$5,196*
 
*Starting monthly salary may vary based on a holistic assessment of academic qualifications, relevant work experience and completion of full-time National Service.
jobRequirements:
You can be a part of the OneCustoms team to protect the revenue to be invested in the progress and well-being of our Singapore community and to contribute to maintaining Singapore’s status as a global trading hub! The role is open to applicants from all disciplines who are keen on the opportunity to take on different roles in Customs through the regular job rotations under our Open Posting System – a Trade Facilitator, a Trade Regulator, and a Law Enforcer. We have a structured career development roadmap to nurture you as a professional Customs officer. We put our traders, travellers and our people at the heart of everything we do. We serve with commitment and purpose yet being able to deliver decisively at the same time. 
 
As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. Find out more about careers with Customs here ( https://www.customs.gov.sg/about-us/careers/)

jobTitle: Assistant Director / Senior Assistant Director, Business Advisory
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. jobDescription:
At MSF, our work makes a difference to individuals, families and society. Delivering that mission well requires leaders who can make sound workforce and people decisions, supported by HR professionals who understand both the business context and the people implications.

Our Human Resource Division is transforming how we partner MSF and our people, moving beyond traditional HR delivery to become trusted advisers, strategic partners and future enablers. The Business Advisory pillar is at the heart of this shift, providing dedicated HR consultancy and advisory support to leaders on people, talent and workforce decisions.

As Assistant Director / Senior Assistant Director, Business Advisory, you will lead strategic people and workforce advisory for an assigned portfolio. You will lead the delivery of integrated advisory across workforce planning and deployment, talent and succession, performance management, conduct and employee relations to help leaders make effective people decisions and strengthen organisational outcomes.

You will provide professional leadership for Business Advisory within an assigned portfolio and lead or guide Business Partners supporting leaders and divisions on complex workforce, organisation, talent and people matters.

Working closely with senior leaders, you will bring together business context, workforce insights and HR expertise to shape practical and integrated solutions. You will mobilise expertise across the Division where broader support is required and ensure that people advice is coherent, responsive and grounded in sound professional judgement.

Beyond individual divisional matters, you will identify patterns, risks and emerging workforce concerns across your portfolio, and contribute these insights to the development of organisation-wide people strategies, policies and interventions.

A key part of your role will be to strengthen Business Advisory professional capability, developing Business Partners into trusted consultants who can diagnose issues, constructively challenge leaders and translate MSF’s people strategies into effective business decisions.
jobResponsibilities:
Shape workforce solutions that enable the business
- Build trusted partnerships with senior leaders and develop a deep understanding of divisional priorities, operating requirements and emerging workforce challenges.

- Lead or guide the diagnosis of organisation and workforce issues and the development of integrated solutions across manpower planning, workforce deployment, organisation changes and workforce transitions. Help leaders balance immediate business requirements with longer-term workforce sustainability.

Strengthen talent, succession and workforce mobility
- Partner leaders on talent identification, succession planning and critical workforce-pipeline needs, helping divisions build sustainable pipelines for leadership and critical roles.

- Guide talent discussions and translate them into meaningful development, deployment and career actions. Facilitate cross-divisional mobility and connect identified needs with relevant leadership, capability and career interventions.

Strengthen performance, accountability and sound people management
- Guide leaders and Business Partners on performance management, including complex performance and underperformance matters, and strengthen the quality of performance conversations and decisions.

- Provide professional oversight of complex employee-relations, workplace-conflict, grievance, conduct and disciplinary matters. Exercise sound judgement in balancing policy intent, precedent, organisational requirements, fairness, employee circumstances and risk.

Enable leaders and divisions to navigate workforce and organisational change
- Partner divisions through restructuring, leadership transitions, changing operating models and other significant organisational developments.

- Assess the workforce and employee implications of change, recommend appropriate people interventions and mobilise relevant expertise across the Division to support implementation. Bring implementation insights back to the relevant strategy, policy, organisation-development and capability teams.

Build a high-performing Business Advisory team
- Lead, develop and coach Business Partners within the assigned portfolio, strengthening capability in consulting, workforce advisory, talent, performance management, employee relations and professional judgement.

- Set team priorities and deploy resources according to organisational need, complexity and risk. Strengthen advisory quality, calibration and knowledge-sharing within the team, while contributing to consistent professional practice across Business Advisory.

- Lead or contribute to selected cross-cutting Business Advisory portfolios, depending on appointment level and organisational needs.
jobRequirements:
Experience & Professional Expertise
•	Tertiary qualification in Human Resource Management, Business, Psychology, Social Sciences or a related discipline. Relevant professional HR certification would be advantageous.
•	At least 7 years of relevant HR experience, with depth across two or more of the following areas: HR business partnering, workforce advisory, talent and succession management, performance management, employee relations, conduct and discipline, workforce planning, deployment or organisational change.
•	Experience partnering senior leaders on complex workforce, people and organisational matters.
•	Strong professional expertise in strategic HR business partnering and consultancy, with good knowledge across talent and succession, performance management and employee relations.
•	Good understanding of workforce planning, manpower management, deployment, organisational change and HR policy interpretation.
•	Ability to use workforce data and organisational insights to diagnose issues and develop practical, context-sensitive recommendations.
•	For appointment at Senior Assistant Director level, candidates should bring greater depth of experience leading teams and advising senior leaders on complex, sensitive or organisation-wide workforce and people matters.

Leadership & Personal Attributes
•	Strong organisational and business acumen, with the ability to understand divisional priorities, operating contexts and their workforce and people implications.
•	Strategic and systems thinker, able to connect individual and divisional issues to broader workforce and organisational considerations and develop integrated solutions.
•	Trusted adviser and influential partner, able to establish credibility with senior leaders, constructively challenge perspectives and navigate competing interests.
•	Sound professional judgement, particularly when managing sensitive, ambiguous or complex workforce, performance and employee matters.
•	Collaborative and integrative, able to mobilise expertise across the Division and build shared ownership with leaders and stakeholders.
•	Strong people leader, able to coach and develop Business Partners into credible, confident and effective HR consultants.
•	Empathetic and principled, able to balance organisational and employee considerations while maintaining fairness, professional objectivity and integrity.
•	Adaptable and resilient, comfortable navigating ambiguity, complexity and competing priorities while maintaining focus on outcomes.

Appointment at AD / SAD Level
Appointment at Assistant Director or Senior Assistant Director level will take into account the candidate’s experience and demonstrated ability to operate at the required level of portfolio complexity, professional judgement, stakeholder engagement and leadership.

Portfolio scope: At AD level, lead an assigned portfolio of divisions and workforce matters. At SAD level, lead a larger, more complex or higher-impact portfolio.

Stakeholder and issue complexity: At AD level, partner divisional leaders and senior stakeholders on complex matters. At SAD level, advise on more sensitive, ambiguous, cross-divisional or higher-impact matters.

Professional judgement: At AD level, independently handle complex matters within established frameworks and escalate novel or high-risk issues. At SAD level, exercise significant judgement on ambiguous, high-risk or precedent-setting matters and shape intervention options.

People and professional leadership: At AD level, lead and develop Business Partners and manage advisory delivery within the portfolio. At SAD level, provide stronger professional leadership across the team and may lead other senior practitioners.

Enterprise contribution: At AD level, contribute insights and participate in cross-cutting Business Advisory work. At SAD level, lead selected cross-cutting portfolios and influence professional practice across Business Advisory.

But you'll do more than manage projects. Working across engineering, planning, regulation and research, you'll help shape how Singapore plans and develops its underground space. Few people here have hands-on experience in this field, and the playbook is still being written.

  • Plan caverns and supporting infrastructure, covering geological assessment, rock engineering, blast design, fire-fighting provisions and M&E systems.
  • Lead the procurement and appointment of consultants, insurers and contractors.
  • Steer multi-disciplinary teams to deliver rock cavern projects safely, cost-effectively and innovatively.

2. Shaping a new sector

  • Partner government agencies to plan and develop Singapore's underground space.
  • Help streamline regulations and establish standards for future underground developments.

3. Capability building and innovation

  • Work with institutes of higher learning (IHLs) and industry partners to turn research into practice.
  • Lead capability-building programmes, international conferences, overseas study trips and other initiatives that grow Singapore's expertise in underground development.

4. Building partnerships

  • Collaborate with government agencies, consultants, contractors, IHLs and international experts on caverns developments.
  • Represent JTC at inter-agency, industry and international platforms, while building a strong professional network in this specialised field.
jobRequirements:
• Background in Civil or Geotechnical Engineering, Rock Mechanics, Engineering Geology or a related field.
  • Preferably 5 or more years of experience in underground, tunnelling or geotechnical projects. Experience with rock caverns or drill-and-blast works is a strong plus.
  • Strong project management, stakeholder management, interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Confidence to lead multi-disciplinary teams and manage multiple projects concurrently.
  • A strong technical foundation; familiarity with geological or numerical modelling tools is an advantage.
  • Curiosity and an interest in new ideas and technology.

Why join us

  • Rare expertise: Few engineers and project managers in Singapore get to work on deep rock caverns.
  • End-to-end ownership: You'll see projects through from the first study to delivery.
  • Wide exposure: You'll work across engineering, regulation, research and international practice.
  • Strong network: You'll build connections across the public sector, industry, academia and the international underground-development community.

The Inter-Generational Support Division (IGS) sits within FLG and focuses on three areas: encouraging pre-planning through the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA); protecting the dignity and interests of vulnerable persons who lack mental capacity under the Mental Capacity Act (MCA); and supporting the resolution of maintenance disputes between parents and their children through the Tribunal for the Maintenance of Parents (TMP) under the Maintenance of Parents Act (MPA).
jobResponsibilities:
As a Litigation Officer in the IGS Investigation and Litigation Unit, you will play a critical role in safeguarding vulnerable persons who may lack mental capacity. You will provide legal support on matters under the MCA to the Public Guardian, manage court proceedings that arise from the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG)'s investigations and/or other matters involving the MCA or persons who lack capacity. You may also be involved in policy and legislative reviews or in projects that contribute towards strengthening the legal and operational frameworks that protect vulnerable persons. You will:

• Provide legal advice and support to IGS on matters involving the MCA and MPA, including the LPA and deputyship frameworks, investigations and the exercise of statutory powers.
• Assess complex cases and investigation findings, identify legal, evidential and procedural issues, and recommend appropriate legal action.
• Work closely with IGS Investigation Officers, MSF’s Legal Services Unit and the Attorney-General’s Chambers to manage court proceedings involving LPA Donees, court-appointed Deputies and persons who lack capacity, including applications relating to the suspension and revocation of LPAs and deputyship orders.
• Prepare and coordinate court applications and supporting materials, including affidavits, submissions and evidence, and handle other applications for the Court’s determination or directions under the MCA.
• Engage relevant stakeholders, including professional deputies, MSF’s Protective Service, the Office of the Director-General of Social Welfare, the Public Trustee’s Office, the Family Justice Courts, healthcare and social service professionals, and other government agencies, where required.
• Contribute to legislative, policy and operational reviews arising from litigation, investigations, legal developments and emerging issues to strengthen the mental capacity and safeguarding frameworks.
• Contribute to building the legal capabilities of IGS officers including the development of legal curriculum, guides and manuals.
• Enhance litigation processes, SOPs, legal resources and case management practices, including the appropriate use of digital, data and AI tools to improve efficiency, consistency and quality.
• Monitor developments in legislation, case law and practice relating to mental capacity, LPAs, deputyships and safeguarding, and translate these into practical guidance for IGS’ operations.

• Experience in civil litigation, family law, public or administrative law, regulatory work, or related areas will be an advantage.
• Strong legal analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to assess complex facts and evidence, interpret legislation, identify legal risks and exercise sound judgement.

jobDescription: The job requirements for Executive Engineer/Senior Engineer (Process and Civil) for Changi Water Reclamation Plant (WRP) Construction are as follows:
jobResponsibilities:
Civil Works and Process Management

Team and construction oversight:

  • Work with the consultant’s site supervision team to ensure that the project is delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with the approved design.

Design and technical review:

  • Review civil and structural drawings to ensure that piling, foundation, and permanent concrete works comply with the relevant specifications.
  • Review process designs with MEICA counterparts to ensure compliance with the design requirements and specifications.
  • Assess design deviations arising from site constraints or specification requirements.

Site interfaces and operational requirements:

  • Review site-access arrangements and interfaces between contractors to streamline the works and minimise site conflicts.
  • Develop mitigation measures and liaise with plant staff and HSS to safeguard security and safety during interface works that integrate new plants and facilities with the existing plant.
  • Review with the MEICA counterpart requests from the Plant for additional process or equipment requirements to confirm that they are necessary to support future operations and maintenance or address potential safety concerns.

Commissioning and handover:

  • Work with consultants and contractors to develop testing and commissioning plans.
  • Work with consultants to obtain the Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) and Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC) for completed facilities.
  • Coordinate with the consultants and contractors in preparing completed facilities for handover, including inspections, punch-list closure, training, documentation, and regulatory clearances. Liaise with Changi WRP to complete the handover with all required records and approvals.

Contract Management

Progress and resource management:

  • Monitor contractors’ progress against the project schedule through regular weekly and monthly meetings and reviews of actual site progress.
  • Identify and escalate any shortfall in contractor or consultant manpower that may affect timely project completion.

Contract administration:

  • Manage contractual matters, including project schedules, contractors’ claims for extensions of time (EOT), and variation works.
  • Manage the issuance of the Certificate of Substantial Completion (CSC) to the contractor as the contract approaches completion.
  • Work with contractors and consultants to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and advisories.

Payments and financial administration:

  • Manage monthly progress payments for consultancy service contracts, ensuring that claims are accurate and paid in accordance with the contract provisions.
  • Manage monthly progress payments for the respective construction contracts, ensuring that payments comply with the contract provisions.
  • Prepare five-year project budget forecasts and annual budgets and monitor achievement of the required utilisation rate.
  • Arrange virements to ensure that sufficient funds are available to pay for completed works under each contract.

Governance and assurance:

  • Coordinate with the Procurement and Contracts Department (PCD) and Centralised Services Department on directives and matters relating to contract administration and construction safety.
  • Manage and address internal and external audits relating to contract calling, evaluation, and management.

Project Cost and Schedule Control

Cost control:

  • Monitor contract expenditure against the approved contract sum and contingency sum. Prepare and submit project papers promptly when projected expenditure is expected to exceed the available contingency.
  • Monitor each project’s overall plan cost against committed expenditure across the contracts under that plan. Prepare and submit plan-cost papers promptly to seek an increase in the approved cost where additional funding is required to complete the project.

Schedule and resource control:

  • Monitor contractors’ progress against the project schedule through regular monthly meetings and reviews of actual site progress.
  • Identify and escalate any shortfall in contractor or consultant manpower that may affect timely project completion.

Variations and claims:

  • Evaluate proposed variation works to confirm that the additional scope and costs are necessary to meet organisational needs.
  • Verify monthly progress claims for civil, structural, and process works, ensuring that each claim is valid and reflects the actual progress of completed works.

Testing and Commissioning (T&C)

Planning and coordination:

  • Work with consultants, contractors, and stakeholders to develop testing and commissioning plans.
  • Coordinate with all stakeholders, particularly existing Plant personnel, to ensure smooth integration with existing systems.

Execution and performance verification:

  • Manage T&C activities, including dry and wet tests, automatic sequence tests, redundancy tests, fault-scenario tests, the sampling regime, and Plant Proving.
  • Manage each stage of T&C and evaluate performance against contractual requirements before proceeding to the next stage. Give particular attention to Plant Proving, which is the critical milestone for certifying completion of the new facility.

Completion and documentation:

  • Work with the consultant to certify completion of T&C and ensure that all required documentation is submitted in accordance with the contract specifications.

Safety Management

Safety assurance:

  • Conduct safety audits and review risk assessments, method statements, and safe work procedures to verify contractors’ compliance with safety requirements.

Site inspections:

  • Conduct random safety inspections with the consultant’s safety team to verify compliance with safe work procedures and standard operating procedures.

Incident Management:

  • Coordinate with consultants and contractors to ensure that incidents are reported to senior management within the required four-hour timeframe.
  • Conduct incident investigations with consultants and contractors to identify root causes in accordance with the investigation framework and prepare and submit the incident investigation report.

Leadership engagement:

  • Engage contractors’ senior management to reinforce their commitment to construction safety and the implementation of site initiatives that enhance worker safety.

jobTitle: Senior Assistant Director, Organisation & Capability Development
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. jobDescription:
Help shape the organisation, capabilities and culture MSF needs for the future!

At MSF, our work makes a difference to individuals, families, and society.  Delivering that mission well requires an organisation and workforce that can continue to grow, adapt and respond to changing needs.

Our Human Resource Division is transforming how we support MSF and our people, moving beyond traditional HR delivery to become trusted advisers, strategic partners, and future-enablers.  We are strengthening how we build workforce capabilities, develop leaders, enable meaningful careers, shape culture and organisational effectiveness to create an engaging workplace and supportive employee experience.

About the Role

As Senior Assistant Director, Organisation & Capability Development, you will play a key role in the Division’s transformation, leading an integrated portfolio that strengthens MSF’s organisational effectiveness and prepares our leaders and workforce for evolving needs. 

You will provide professional leadership across organisation development (OD), capability building, learning and leadership development, career development, culture, employee engagement and well-being.  

Working with senior leaders, divisions and HR partners, you will diagnose organisational and workforce needs, shape evidence-informed interventions, mobilise stakeholders and build capability across MSF to sustain change. You will also lead in building partnerships and networks needed to deliver organisation-wide outcomes.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Shape future workforce capabilities: Partner divisions and functional leads to identify the capabilities MSF needs for its evolving work and operating demands. Translate competency assessments and workforce insights into targeted capability-building priorities, integrate competencies into relevant learning, career and workforce processes, and evaluate the effectiveness of capability development interventions.

•	Develop leaders and enable meaningful careers: Oversee learning and leadership development interventions aligned to the needs of different workforce and leadership segments.  Work with functional leads to develop learning and leadership frameworks and roadmaps, and drive career development frameworks, tools and programmes that help officers build skills, broaden experience and prepare for current and future roles.

•	Strengthen organisational effectiveness, culture and change management: Lead organisational diagnosis using organisation development (OD) methodologies, data and stakeholder insights. Shape and oversee organisation-wide OD, culture and change interventions, partnering divisions to adapt approaches to different business contexts and needs.

•	Translate MSF's desired culture, values and behaviours into practical leadership, team and workplace practices: Build OD and change capability across MSF so key stakeholders can continue to drive and sustain outcomes within their areas.

•	Build an engaged, connected and resilient workforce: Identify emerging employee-engagement and well-being needs and translate insights into relevant priorities and interventions. Oversee MSF's internal communications approach and employee-listening channels, including surveys and feedback exercises, and guide analysis of workforce sentiments, well-being indicators and emerging concerns to inform organisation-wide and division-level actions. 

Build capability and provide guidance to leaders and stakeholders to strengthen employee engagement, well-being and employee-support practices, and review the reach and effectiveness of interventions to ensure that they remain relevant and sustainable.

•	Lead through partnership and influence: Lead, develop and coach a professional team and build strong partnerships with leaders and stakeholders across MSF. 

Exercise professional judgement in determining the appropriate level, approach and stakeholders for organisation and workforce interventions, balancing Ministry-wide priorities with diverse divisional needs, available evidence, implementation feasibility and resources.

Build shared ownership for organisation and people outcomes, recognising that sustainable change is achieved not through HR acting alone, but by enabling leaders, divisions and stakeholders across MSF to play their part.
jobRequirements:

•	Tertiary qualification in Human Resource Management, Organisation Development, Psychology, Business, Social Sciences or a related discipline. Professional certification in HR, Organisation Development, Change Management or Learning & Development is an advantage.
•	At least 8 years of relevant experience across two or more of the following areas: organisation development, change management, capability development, learning and leadership development, employee engagement, culture transformation, career development or other strategic people-development functions.
•	At least 5 years of experience leading and developing a team. Experience partnering senior leaders and stakeholders on organisation-wide people and organisational initiatives is advantageous.
•	Strong expertise in organisation development and change management, learning and leadership development, workforce capability development, and employee engagement and experience.
•	Sound knowledge of career development and the development and application of competency frameworks.

Generic Competencies
•	Strategic and systems thinker, able to diagnose complex organisational and workforce issues, translate strategic intent into practical and scalable solutions, and balance Ministry-wide priorities with diverse divisional needs.
•	Strong organisational acumen, with a good understanding of how organisational policies, operations, people and workplace dynamics intersect.
•	Strong stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, with the ability to build shared ownership, align diverse stakeholders, and mobilise networks and partnerships across the organisation.
•	Able to manage a diverse portfolio of organisation and workforce initiatives while maintaining strategic focus and attention to implementation quality.
•	Strong people leader, with the ability to lead, develop and coach a professional team.
•	Adaptable and resilient, comfortable navigating ambiguity, complexity and competing priorities while maintaining focus on outcomes.

agencyDescription:

Many opportunities & challenges await those who are keen on an exciting career to realise our commitment to envision & implement an integrated transport system.
jobDescription: LEAD / PRINCIPAL / SENIOR CYBER THREAT INTEL ANALYST
jobResponsibilities:
The Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst will be responsible for identifying, tracking, and analysing emerging cyber threats, with a focus on protecting critical IT/OT systems in the land transportation sector. This role goes beyond passive news consumption and emphasises active threat research, transforming global threat data into localised, actionable monitoring strategies and detection logic.

Key Responsibilities

· Intelligence Programme Development: Lead the development and continuous improvement of the Threat Intelligence (TI) function, including the implementation of of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and CTI solution for intelligence collection, analysis, and dissemination.

· Threat Research & Actor Tracking : Conduct proactive research into the Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) of threat actors, with particular focus on the Asia‑Pacific region and Industrial Control Systems (ICS).

· Monitoring List Management : Curate, validate, and maintain high‑fidelity monitoring lists, including Indicators of Compromise (IOCs), for ingestion into SIEM, EDR, and Network Traffic Analysis tools.

· Detection Engineering Support : Translate research findings into technical detection artefacts, such as YARA, Sigma, or Snort rules, to strengthen proactive threat hunting and detection capabilities.

· Incident Response Integration : Act as the Tier- 3 intelligence lead during critical incidents, providing real‑time threat context, infrastructure pivoting, and attribution support to the CERT team.

· Vulnerability Intelligence : Monitor and prioritise newly disclosed CVEs based on the organisation’s technology stack, providing actionable, risk‑based assessments to patching and infrastructure teams.

· TTP Mapping : Map observed adversary behaviours to the MITRE ATT&CK framework to identify visibility gaps and areas for improvement in existing security controls.

· Stakeholder Reporting : Produce high‑quality intelligence report/ update (including Flash Alerts) for emerging or imminent threats and monthly strategic summaries for management and public transport operators.

Technical Skills & Competencies

· OSINT & Investigation - Strong capability in conducting open‑source investigations across surface, deep, and dark web sources, including forums, code repositories, and social media, to identify leaked credentials or planned threat campaigns.

· Automation - Proficiency in scripting to build custom scrapers, automate Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) workflows, and manage large‑scale intelligence datasets.

· Log Analysis - Ability to correlate threat intelligence with internal telemetry (e.g. proxy, firewall, EDR logs) to validate malicious activity and identify early indicators of compromise.

· Framework Knowledge - Strong understanding of MITRE ATT&CK, Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis, and Cyber Kill Chain.
jobRequirements:
· Knowledge in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related discipline.

· At least 8 years of experience in cybersecurity, with at least 4 years in Threat Intelligence, Advanced SOC Operations, or Incident Response roles.

· Professional Certifications - GIAC Cyber Threat Intelligence (GCTI) or Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)

· Desired Technical Certifications - Relevant technical certifications such as GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH), GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA) or GIAC Reverse Engineering Malware (GREM) would be advantageous.

Key Competencies

· Demonstrated track record in mentoring junior analysts and uplifting SOC/CERT capabilities.

· Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to brief senior leadership and executive stakeholders on complex cyber risk matters.

· Ability to operate effectively in a cross‑matrix environment, as well as independently and decisively in a fast‑paced, high‑impact operational setting.

· Technical leadership: Set technical direction for significant product areas or complex initiatives; turn ambiguous needs into coherent designs and execution plans, and make sound engineering trade-offs.

jobRequirements:

The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), a government agency under the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI), is responsible for strategies that enhance Singapore’s position as a global centre for business, innovation and talent. The Innovation Strategy & Partnerships division in EDB charts the agency’s vision towards an innovation-led economy by developing strategies to enhance the innovation ecosystem for foreign companies to create new products, services and businesses in Singapore.   • Develop value propositions and co-create solutions to strengthen Singapore as an innovation economy, in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders (e.g. industry groups in EDB, other government agencies and industry partners)

agencyDescription: The Public Sector Science and Technology Policy and Plans Office (S&TPPO) is a department under the Prime Minister’s Office and serves as the functional leader for the Science, Technology and Engineering (STE) domain in public sector. S&TPPO also aims to develop and implement HR strategies and levers to strengthen capability development and career value proposition of STE professionals in the Singapore Public Service.
jobDescription:
Science, Technology, and Engineering (STE) are pivotal in modernising public service delivery, driving innovation and efficiency across the public sector. As the challenges facing Singapore grow more complex and cross-cutting, the public sector must harness STE capabilities in a coordinated and sustained way — building on agencies' efforts, catalysing collaboration, and ensuring that innovation translates into real-world impact.
S&TPPO plays a key role in advancing WOG STE capabilities, working across agencies to identify opportunities, develop solutions, and build the foundations for scalable and sustainable adoption. In particular, S&TPPO will focus in these areas in the next few years: (i) driving Transformative STE Initiatives (TSIs) that tackle complex national challenges at the system-of-systems level; and (ii) developing Innovation and Ops-Tech Enablers that help agencies adopt frontier technologies and build new Ops-Tech capabilities.
jobResponsibilities:
The officer will play a key role in enabling agencies to apply innovation towards addressing WOG and cross-sectoral challenges.

Innovation Partnerships
• Engage regularly with agency partners, senior leadership, and external stakeholders to surface STE problem statements, gather insights to inform Public Sector STE workstreams, and channel expertise to agencies where needed.

• Build and sustain a network of external technical experts and partners, including Public Sector STE alumni, researchers, and industry practitioners, and establish the formal mechanisms to sustain this network.

Innovation Management
• Drive the end-to-end programme management of S&TPPO's key innovation initiatives, including the STE Innovation Challenge, STE Innovation Catalyst, and Ops-Tech-as-a-Service engagements, from concept scoping through to delivery and handover.

We develop core capabilities across quadrupeds, humanoids, and Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) platforms, specializing in in-house stacks for navigation, locomotion, manipulation, and whole-body control.

jobResponsibilities:
Architect, develop, and integrate cutting edge robotics capabilities—spanning navigation, locomotion, manipulation, and whole-body control (WBC) —for individual platforms and multi-agent system-of-systems operations.
Drive research and software stack development in edge sensing, real-time decision-making, multi-robot coordination, and operational artificial intelligence (e.g., VLM, VLA etc.) tailored for mission-critical applications.
Integrate heterogeneous robotic platforms (quadrupeds, humanoids, and traditional AMRs) with specialized sensors, edge compute, dexterous manipulation capabilities, mission payload transportation and facility infrastructure into unified, resilient field solutions.
Develop, benchmark, and optimize modular robotics middleware (e.g., ROS 2) and open communication standards to ensure seamless interoperability and low-latency control across diverse platform fleets.
Support product manager in rapid prototyping, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation, and rigorous stress-testing to validate safety, autonomy, and robustness under challenging environmental conditions.
Support end-to-end capability transition by planning and executing operational field trials, ensuring prototypes meet the reliability and readiness standards required for front-line Home Team deployment.

Tertiary education in Robotics, Computer Science, Mechatronics, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related STEM discipline.
A post-graduate degree in Robotics, Autonomous Systems, or Embodied AI would be an advantage.
Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience (or equivalent track record) in robotics software development, autonomous systems engineering, or applied R&D.
Core Robotics Stacks: Hands-on experience developing or integrating modules across at least one key domain (in order of preference):
i) Manipulation & Perception (VLA arm trajectory planning, multi-modal sensing, sensor fusion).
ii) Locomotion & Control (whole-body control (WBC), quadruped/humanoid gait planning, MPC).
iii) Navigation & SLAM (GPS-denied mapping, open-vocabulary ObjectNav, path planning).

Strong analytical, technical writing and problem-solving skills.
Excellent team player with strong stakeholder engagement and collaboration skills.
Self-motivated and committed with a sense of urgency to deliver desired outcomes.

jobDescription:

A key area of responsibility will be supporting the ground operations and deployment of APS across parks and Park Connector Networks (PCNs), including coordinating with service providers, tracking operational readiness and resolving ground-level issues. Through this work, you will contribute to the sustainable scaling of autonomous cleaning operations in Singapore’s public parks while gaining exposure to ground operations, stakeholder coordination, trials and operational transformation.

You will work closely with internal divisions, government agencies, service providers and technology vendors to translate operational requirements into practical technology adoption, conduct trials and support the implementation and operationalisation of autonomous cleaning technologies.
jobResponsibilities:

  • Conduct site and feasibility assessments to identify suitable parks and infrastructure locations, taking into account operational, technical and safety considerations.
  • Coordinate with service providers, LTA, NParks and other relevant counterparts on APS deployment, operational integration, and regulatory requirements.
  • Coordinate and track regulatory/agency approvals and infrastructure readiness required for APS deployment.

  • Support asset tracking and verification, where applicable.

  • Ability to analyse operational data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Strong written, verbal and interpersonal skills, including the ability to engage diverse stakeholders and present recommendations to management.
  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and drive issues to resolution.
  • A proactive, resourceful and solution-oriented mindset, with a keen eye for ground-level operational details.

About the EDB Summer Internship Programme
Each summer, EDB welcomes students from diverse academic backgrounds who are passionate about Singapore's economic development and eager to gain real-world experience. Our internship programme offers a unique learning opportunity to understand how strategy and policy come together to shape economic outcomes.

Our 2027 Summer Internship Programme runs from 10 May to 30 July 2027*. The programme includes networking events with our senior leaders and officers to give you behind-the-scenes insights into the organisation and our role in economy and nation building.

*We understand that academic schedules vary, so if these dates do not align with your availability, we still welcome your application. Just include a note in your resume with your preferred 12-week period and we will work to accommodate where possible.

What the internship entails

You will be attached to a division within EDB where you will work with experienced mentors on meaningful projects that address real-world business and industry challenges. Over 12 weeks, you will own and drive your internship project. This could be a new opportunity, challenge or problem statement that your division is working on. To mark the end of your internship, you will present your insights, analysis and recommendations to your division.

Your key responsibilities:

  • Conduct in-depth research and analysis. This could include understanding market dynamics, competitive landscapes, underlying issues and emerging trends for your assigned industry sector or policy area.
  • Engage key internal and external stakeholders (e.g. MNCs, industry associations, government agencies) to gather firsthand perspectives and validate your research findings.
  • Collaborate closely with EDB officers to draw insights from their experience, bounce ideas and discuss challenges as you work through your project.
  • Based on your research and analysis, develop practical recommendations which are actionable and grounded in real market conditions and policy considerations.

We are seeking individuals who are curious, adaptable and eager to contribute to Singapore’s economic development.

  • A penultimate undergraduate or current master's student at a recognised local or overseas university
  • Pursuing a degree in any discipline (No, you don’t need to have an economics background. We welcome all backgrounds, including STEM students!)

Applications for the EDB Summer Internship 2027 are open from November 2026 to March 2027. Interviews will be conducted from December 2026 onwards and on a rolling basis.

agencyDescription: The Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) is the national authority that registers and is responsible for the administration of IP rights in Singapore. jobDescription:
Great ideas do not discriminate — anyone can have them. With the right protection and support, a great idea can become a trusted brand, a transformative technology, an innovative process or design, or even a song or story that inspires one’s soul.
