We leverage on our deep technical, legal and business expertise to help innovative enterprises grow, through their intangible assets, including IP, from Singapore, through Singapore. We catalyse the ideas today, into assets tomorrow.

A trade mark can be any word, name, letter, numeral, device, shape, colour, aspect of packaging, or a combination of such elements. In some cases, even sounds or holograms may qualify. From the Singapore Airlines bird logo to the DBS quatrefoil, trade marks help businesses build distinctive brands and protect their reputation.

We are currently seeking Associate Trade Mark Examiners to join the Registry of Trade Marks. In this role, you will work closely with fellow examiners to assess trade mark applications and ensure they comply with the legal requirements for registration. You may also contribute to the formulation and implementation of national trade mark policies, supporting Singapore’s position as a global hub for intellectual property and intangible assets.

The role includes an initial structured training period of approximately 18 months, during which successful candidates will progressively develop the legal, analytical and professional judgment required for independent trade mark examination. This training combines on-the-job learning, with mentoring and formal instruction provided, and requires sustained commitment and dedication from the job holder.
jobResponsibilities:
Examining a trade mark application requires a combination of sound thinking, good judgment, strong analytical skills, and some understanding of, or an interest in how businesses brand, market and identify themselves.

As a Trade Mark Examiner, you will:

1. Assess distinctiveness Determine whether a proposed trade mark is capable of distinguishing the trade origin of the relevant goods or services.
2. Conduct searches for conflicting marks Identify earlier trade marks on the Singapore trade mark register that may conflict with the application.
3. Review specifications of goods and services Examine the description of goods and services applied for, with reference to international classification standards.
4. Communicate examination outcomes and provide guidance
Correspond with applicants or their legal representatives on examination outcomes, including raising objections where necessary, and assessing responses received. Provide guidance and assistance to members of the public who have queries on trade mark-related matters.

Beyond examination work, Trade Mark Examiners may take on administrative and project-based responsibilities that support the effective functioning of the Registry and the broader objectives of IPOS.

As you gain experience and seniority, your role will broaden to include mentoring, training and supervisory responsibilities, contributing to the professional development of junior colleagues.

The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is a statutory board under Ministry of Transport that spearheads land transport developments in Singapore. We are seeking dynamic, energetic, highly motivated, passionate and qualified professionals to join us.

Many opportunities & challenges await those who are keen on an exciting career to realise our commitment to envision & implement an integrated transport system.
jobDescription:
The Learning Strategy and Planning Team is part of LTA’s Learning Office, and you will be at the forefront of driving a systemic shift in how the organisation approaches learning and capability development. We are moving beyond traditional learning and development to embed continuous organisational learning in LTA.

In this role, you will be instrumental in addressing key organisational challenges, including consolidating our learning landscape, strengthening a vibrant learning culture, and enhancing our agility to respond to emerging needs and transformation areas. You will take a systems view of learning, ensuring that capability gaps and opportunities, are systematically reviewed and that learning interventions drive measurable impact. Your scope of work will encompass four key pillars:

• Conduct Capability Diagnostics and Pulse on Learning. You will either lead or be involved in developing and deploying frequent dipsticks to gather learning-related data across the organisation. This includes measuring and analysing skills and performance gaps against desired organisational outcomes, and establishing a consolidated view of the LTA learning landscape (what, who, where, how, when).

• Design Learning Interventions and Approaches. You will either lead or be involved as a workplace learning partner to close identified capability gaps, and to design nimble and contextualised solutions, such as curating learning playlists and establishing action-learning project teams. The team would also need to respond rapidly to emerging needs and support LTA-wide transformation areas.

• Measure Learning Outcomes. You will either lead or be involved in defining clear behavioural and performance metrics to evaluate the impact of learning interventions, track the speed of upskilling across the organisation, and establish systematic reviews of performance gaps and the effectiveness of deployed solutions.

• Strengthen Learning Culture and Vibrancy. You will either lead or be involved in applying a systems lens to cultivate a healthy organisational learning culture, and implement strategies that target individual motivation, foster supportive team environments, and build organisational enablers.
jobResponsibilities: This role also involves direct partnering with LTA senior management and engaging of Groups, Divisions and colleagues very closely. To be part of our team, you should enjoy working with diverse groups of leaders and people to forge deep understanding of their operations and help create meaningful change within the organisation. You would need to be comfortable with creating communication materials and coming up with systematic processes, synthesizing information and data from diverse sources, and have strong communication skills to engage management and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Organisational Psychology, Organisational Development preferred
  • Strong advocate of and familiarity in AI tools utilisation and adoption
  • Familiarity with workplace learning methodologies, performance measurement frameworks, and diverse learning solutions
  • Currency on the latest learning trends and shifts in developmental approaches
  • Adaptable, creative, open to new ideas and able to execute effectively
  • Analytical and excellent writing and presentation skills
  • Comfortable in engaging people of different levels
  • For deputy manager applicants, 3 to 5 years of experience in learning and development
  • For manager applicants, more than 7 years of experience in learning and development and professional certifications in Learning and Development (e.g., CIPD, ATD CPTD, or similar)

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment.

At MSF, our work makes a difference to individuals, families and society. Delivering that mission well requires a workforce that is appropriately structured, resourced and equipped to respond to changing organisational and workforce needs.

Our Human Resource Division is transforming how we support MSF and our people, moving beyond traditional HR delivery to become trusted advisers, strategic partners and future enablers. Within the Strategy & Development pillar, we bring together workforce strategy and planning, HR policy, organisation and capability development, culture and employee experience to help MSF remain future-ready.

As Manager / Senior Manager, HR Policy & Planning, you will help shape MSF’s  workforce strategies and HR policies using a data-driven approach. You will translate organisational priorities, workforce trends and Whole-of-Government directions into practical policies, plans and recommendations that support MSF’s current and future workforce needs.

About the Role
You will work at the intersection of workforce strategy, HR policy and workforce analytics, helping MSF understand its future workforce needs and how our policies and workforce approaches should evolve to support them.

Working with leaders, divisions and HR colleagues, you will analyse workforce trends and organisational needs, develop policy and planning recommendations, and translate broader Public Service directions into practical approaches for MSF.

You will combine research, workforce data, policy thinking and stakeholder perspectives to identify emerging workforce issues, evaluate options and support evidence-informed decisions on manpower, HR policy and workforce transformation.

Depending on your experience and appointment level, you may independently lead policy reviews, strategic workforce-planning workstreams, analytical projects or other cross-cutting workforce initiatives.
jobResponsibilities:
Shape relevant and future-oriented HR policies
•	Develop, review and implement HR policies and frameworks that support MSF’s organisational priorities, workforce needs and transformation agenda.
•	Assess policy intent, workforce implications, implementation considerations and stakeholder needs, and translate Whole-of-Government directions into practical approaches for MSF.
•	Lead or support the rollout of new and revised policies, engaging stakeholders, managing implementation issues and using feedback to improve policy design and application.

Turn workforce data and trends into actionable insights
•	Conduct workforce research, environmental scanning and benchmarking, and analyse workforce data and trends to identify emerging risks, gaps and opportunities.
•	Develop workforce dashboards and analytical approaches that translate data into meaningful insights for workforce planning, policy and management decisions.
•	Bring together quantitative data and organisational context to develop clear recommendations and workforce metrics.

Help shape MSF’s future workforce
•	Drive and support strategic workforce-planning exercises to identify MSF’s current and future manpower, workforce and capability requirements.
•	Partner leaders, divisions and other planning functions to understand future work, identify workforce gaps and translate organisational priorities into workforce strategies and transformation plans.
•	Monitor manpower establishment and workforce movements, and provide analysis and recommendations that support sustainable management of MSF’s manpower resources.

Translate policy and workforce strategy into practice
•	Provide professional advice to leaders, managers and HR colleagues on policy interpretation and application, helping stakeholders understand policy intent and apply policies consistently and appropriately.
•	Identify recurring implementation issues, workforce concerns and stakeholder feedback, and bring these insights back into policy reviews, workforce-planning work and broader HR strategies.
•	Lead or contribute to cross-cutting HR and workforce projects, management committees and strategic planning exercises where policy, workforce insights and organisational considerations need to come together.
jobRequirements:
Experience & Professional Expertise
•	Tertiary qualification in Human Resource Management, Business, Economics, Public Policy, Social Sciences or a related discipline.
•	At least 4 years of relevant experience in one or more areas such as HR policy, strategic workforce planning, workforce analytics, manpower planning, strategic HR business partnering or related strategy and planning work.
•	Strong analytical and policy-thinking capabilities, with the ability to synthesise workforce data, research, stakeholder perspectives and organisational considerations into sound recommendations.
•	Good understanding of workforce planning and policy development. Knowledge of Singapore Public Service HR policies and operating context would be advantageous.
•	Proficiency in analysing and presenting workforce information. Experience with Microsoft Power BI, Tableau or comparable data-visualisation tools would be useful.
•	Experience using HR systems and workforce data, including SAP-based HR systems where relevant, would be useful.

Leadership & Personal Attributes
•	Strategic and analytical thinker, able to analyse complex information, question assumptions, evaluate different perspectives and translate insights into practical recommendations.
•	Strong organisational acumen, with an appreciation of how workforce, policy and people considerations connect to broader organisational priorities.
•	Clear and persuasive communicator, able to distil complex policy and workforce issues into clear, compelling narratives that build understanding and support among diverse audiences.
•	Strong stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, able to build constructive relationships, navigate different perspectives and develop shared understanding.
•	Collaborative and self-driven, with a strong sense of ownership and willingness to work across teams and professional boundaries.
•	Adaptable and detail-oriented, able to adjust to changing circumstances and shifting priorities while maintaining quality, rigour and attention to implementation.

jobTitle: [LTA-RAOM] SNR / EXEC / ENGINEER, ASSET MGMT (SYSTEMS & PLANNING)
agencyDescription:

jobDescription: [LTA-RAOM] SNR / EXEC / ENGINEER, ASSET MGMT (SYSTEMS & PLANNING)

jobTitle: Senior Manager / Manager (Acute and Crisis Care)
agencyDescription:

MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.

jobTitle: Assistant Manager / Manager (Casework - Youth Homes), RPG/PRGS
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription:
Description of Division: 
The Probation, Reintegration and Gambling Safeguards (PRGS) Division works with offenders on community-based orders and youths in residential care through targeted interventions delivered in collaboration with families and community partners. The role encompasses case management across diverse profiles, from youth to adults, focusing on enhancing their socio-emotional development, building 
social networks, and facilitating successful reintegration into the community. In addition, PRGS oversees gambling related social safeguards, funds support programmes for problem gamblers and their families, and serves as the secretariat to the National Council on Problem Gambling (NCPG).
jobResponsibilities:
Brief description of Job Scope: 
As part of the Casework (Youth Homes) team, you will be responsible for the rehabilitation, protection and reintegration of youth placed in secure care at the Singapore Boys’ Home (SBH) and Singapore Girls’ Home (SGH). You will work with these youths and their family to strengthen their socio-emotional development and social networks and prepare them for reintegration into the community. 

Responsibilities: 
Your work includes the following: 
• Case management: formulating and implementing care plans for youths under your charge. 
• Conduct intervention programmes with youths and their caregivers in both individual and group settings. 
• Work closely with stakeholders such as caregivers, school authorities, employers and community partners to address risks and needs identified.

agencyDescription: At the National Parks Board (NParks), we take pride in conserving our natural heritage and enhancing green spaces for all to enjoy in our City in Nature. agencyDescription:

We enable employers to build a skilled, future-ready workforce, design quality jobs, and adopt skills recognition practices. Together with our partners, we build a trusted, high-quality, industry-relevant, and innovative ecosystem that meets the evolving workforce needs of both businesses and workers.   

Guided by our vision of a Singapore where everyone can grow in fulfilling careers, we live our promise of Building Skills, Growing Careers by nurturing lifelong learning, strengthening employability and enabling career growth for all, including our own officers, through a continuous learning culture and a supportive, flexible, inclusive working environment that fosters innovation, collaboration, and well-being.

So, join us to be part of a dynamic team driving the national SkillsFuture movement and building a strong Singaporean core. Together, we create opportunities, transform lives, and shape the future of work.
jobDescription: You will support SWDA’s efforts to deepen strategic partnerships, develop programmes and pilots, and manage grants and funding arrangements that support initiatives related to career planning and development, employment services, and capability building within the Careers and Employment Services (CES) sector.
jobResponsibilities:

• Develop and implement partnership and engagement plans with priority stakeholders, including training providers, institutes of higher learning (IHLs), employers, industry associations, sector agencies and community partners.

• Build and sustain strategic partnerships across the public, private and people sectors, translating these relationships into co-created initiatives that expand career planning support and CES sector capability-building.

• Lead the conceptualisation, design, implementation and review of programmes, pilots and innovation projects, including objectives, operating model, delivery modality, governance structure, funding model and success indicators.

• Translate inputs, feedback, observations and data into actionable proposals, budget requests, and implementation and evaluation plans.

• Oversee grant administration and funding-related matters, including eligibility, claims, disbursements, budget utilisation, performance monitoring, compliance requirements, risk management and audit readiness.

• Work closely with internal teams to ensure initiatives are well-governed, properly resourced and aligned with organisational priorities.

• Evaluate partnership and grant-funded initiatives to determine what should be refined, scaled, handed over or discontinued.

• Identify new partnership models, technology-enabled approaches, service delivery formats and process improvements that can improve accessibility, quality or impact.

• Prepare and present clear updates, management papers, briefing decks and recommendations to internal and external stakeholders, including senior management.

Successful candidates will be offered a contract in the first instance and may be considered for an extension or be placed on a permanent tenure.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities

The future of Singapore’s energy landscape depends on our ability to harness four switches – natural gas, solar, electricity imports, and low-carbon solutions We are exploring the potential of hydrogen, ammonia, carbon capture and storage, bioenergy, advanced geothermal and advanced nuclear, as well as other promising low-carbon technologies.

Singaporeans are at the heart of what we do. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) empowers our people and fosters a thriving, inclusive workforce that drives Singapore's growth and prosperity. By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore. 

As an MOM officer, you will be part of this meaningful mission, contributing across diverse and impactful areas - from shaping forward-looking and effective manpower policies and strengthening industrial relations, to enhancing workplace safety standards and ensuring balanced local and foreign workforce regulations. Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobDescription:
The Income Security Policy Division (ISPD) shapes policies that help Singaporeans achieve greater financial security in retirement. 

As a part of the Strategy & Planning team, you will help chart the future direction of CPF and retirement adequacy policy.
jobResponsibilities:
You will use data, research and policy analysis to understand how Singaporeans’ retirement needs are changing, identify emerging gaps, and develop strategies to address them.

Your work will span the full spectrum of policy making, from policy design to scheme implementation and public communications. You will frame complex questions, analyse large datasets, develop projections and recommendations, and work closely with stakeholders to translate evidence into implementable policy. You will also collaborate closely with Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board, Ministry of Finance (MOF), Ministry of Health (MOH), Ministry of National Development (MND) and other key stakeholders on issues that cut across retirement, housing and healthcare.

You will have the opportunity to work on areas such as:
a.	Reviewing the strategic direction and next bound of CPF policy 
b.	Assessing the current and future state of retirement adequacy 
c.	Identifying emerging gaps and developing policy responses to these
d.	Reviewing key policy benchmarks and retirement adequacy indicators, including the Basic Retirement Sum; and
e.	Evaluating trade-offs across retirement, housing, healthcare and other policy objectives

This role will suit someone who enjoys making sense of complex problems, working with evidence and helping to shape long-term policy. You will join a collaborative team, with experienced supervisors supporting your professional development and giving you opportunities to take ownership of substantive work.
jobRequirements:
•	Strong interest in social and economic policy. 
•	Ability to structure ambiguous problems, think strategically and exercise sound judgement. 
•	Strong analytical and writing skills, including the ability to explain complex findings clearly. 
•	Experience using programming or analytical tools to analyse and manipulate large datasets, such as Python, Tableau, R, SQL or equivalent tools. 
•	Intellectual curiosity, attention to detail and a willingness to test assumptions against evidence. 
•	Ability to take initiative, work independently and collaborate across agencies and disciplines. 
•	Good interpersonal and communication skills. 
•	Two to three years of relevant experience would be useful, although we welcome candidates with strong transferable skills from policy, research, economics, data analysis or related fields.

jobDescription:
The Income Security Policy Division (ISPD) shapes policies that help Singaporeans achieve greater financial security in retirement. 

In the Accumulation & Decumulation team, you will work on the core policy levers that determine how Singaporeans build, grow and draw down their CPF savings.
jobResponsibilities:
You will need to consider a multitude of interdependent issues involving fairness across generations, financial sustainability, individual choice and the provision of adequate and lasting retirement income.

You will analyse policy and financial questions, develop recommendations, and work through their implementation and public communications. You will work closely with the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board, Ministry of Finance (MOF) and other key stakeholders to ensure that the policies are sound in design and workable in practice.

You will have the opportunity to work on areas such as: 
a.	How CPF contribution rates and wage ceilings should evolve to support retirement adequacy;
b.	How CPF interest rates should be set to provide fair and sustainable returns; 
c.	How members can invest their CPF savings for potentially higher returns while managing risks; and
d.	How retirement savings should be drawn to provide adequate and sustainable lifelong income.

This role will suit someone who enjoys combining policy judgement with quantitative and financial analysis. You will join a collaborative team, with experienced supervisors supporting your professional development and giving you opportunities to take ownership of substantive policy work.
jobRequirements:
•	Strong interest in social and economic policy. 
•	Ability to understand complex policy choices, assess trade-offs and develop practical recommendations. 
•	Strong analytical, data analysis and writing skills. 
•	Comfort with quantitative and financial concepts, including interest rates, investment risk, modelling and sustainable retirement income. 
•	Ability to explain technically complex issues clearly to non-specialist audiences. 
•	Ability to take initiative, sound judgement and attention to detail. 
•	Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across agencies and with diverse stakeholders. 
•	Two to three years of relevant experience would be useful. Experience in public policy, economics, finance or quantitative analysis would be an advantage, but is not essential.

Responsibilities

You will be part of the team to drive greater design standardisation and industrialised construction to improve productivity, manufacturability and scalability across the built environment sector. The role involves working closely with public agencies and industry stakeholders to develop and implement a comprehensive design standardisation strategy. Key responsibilities include:

agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
Looking for a job that actually makes a difference?

Join us at the Forefront of Shaping Healthier Lives!

The Health Promotion Board (HPB) is seeking a highly motivated, innovative and dynamic candidate to advance health promotion through the translation of research to practice.

The job holder will play an important role in shaping the next generation of health promotion by distilling learnings and insights research, rich data and novel technologies, and translating these into actionable recommendations that inform the development of population‑scale digital health interventions. This includes leading the research and development of health interventions that integrate behavioural science, emerging technologies (including generative AI), and population‑scale digital platforms.
jobResponsibilities:
The jobholder will drive and manage high impact projects in priority growth areas by:

  • Distilling complexity across data, behavioural insights, user research and implementation constraints into clear, decision‑ready narratives (in writing and slides) for diverse stakeholders

  • Incorporating behavioural insights in the setup, design, testing and review of human-centric user experiences and digital health interventions

  • Managing the digital product cycle, including ideation, design and execution of feasibility trials, outcome evaluation, and translation of learnings into deployment‑ready insights and recommendations. This includes leading and coordinating a multidisciplinary tech squad (product, engineering, data, design) to support rapid experimentation, prototyping and evaluation of generative AI‑enabled coaching and personalisation concepts.

  • Working with cross-functional teams comprising subject matter experts, data scientists, deployment teams and practitioners to develop innovative and practicable solutions

  • Demonstrating value to citizens in developed solution through quantifiable outputs and outcomes, and developing compelling narratives to convince and secure buy-in from internal and external stakeholders

Required Skills and Competencies:

  • Ability to adopt big picture thinking and distil clarity from complex problems

  • Ability to synthesise insights across multiple, partially‑formed research and product workstreams into coherent decision narratives

  • Ability to connect disparate signals across policy, technology, behavioural science and on‑the‑ground implementation for convergence into solutioning and problem solving

  • Comfortable acting as an integrator across research, technology and policy rather than a depth specialist in a single domain

  • Familiarity with behavioural insights and design thinking

  • Comfortable managing complexity and ambiguity in a fast-paced environment

  • Strong sense of intellectual curiosity and openness to new ideas

  • Demonstrated ability to quickly build working knowledge in new and emerging health or technology domains

  • Strong project management skills to support research, experimentation and cross‑functional coordination

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with ability to engage a wide range of audience

  • Comfortable as an individual contributor or leading a team
jobRequirements:
• Good degree in any discipline
  • At least 8 years of total relevant working experience with 5 years of practical experience overseeing and/or managing end-to-end projects including stakeholder management and 3 years of experience leading cross-functional or multidisciplinary teams to oversee development and implementation of end-to-end product cycles or multi-year projects
  • Practical ground experience and proven track record in applying behavioural insights, with familiarity in design thinking approaches to inform intervention design and testing
  • Prior experience working in the field of public health, health care, health sciences, research or quantitative domains will be an added bonus
  • Experience working with AI‑enabled or data‑driven digital products (including generative AI) is a strong advantage

While this role works closely with AI technologies and tech teams, it remains fundamentally a research‑ and insight‑driven role focused on learning, synthesis and translation, with deployment as an outcome of evidence rather than a starting point.


Successful candidates will be offered a 1-year contract.

jobTitle: Senior System Product Manager (Payments & Monetary Management) (Contract)
agencyDescription: MAS is the central bank of Singapore. Our mission is to promote sustained non-inflationary economic growth, and a sound and progressive financial centre.
jobDescription:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator. MEPS+ (Central Banking & Devt Platforms Division) is responsible for the MAS Electronic Payment System — a mission-critical system supporting interbank payments, government securities management, and domestic market infrastructure. MEPS+ serves the entire Singapore financial sector and requires 24/7 operational reliability, strict compliance with government regulatory frameworks, and close coordination with financial institutions and government agencies.

As System Manager, you are the operational and delivery owner for MEPS+ and related systems. You own the outcomes, and coordinate across software engineers, product owners, compliance teams, and external vendors to ensure system reliability, regulatory compliance, and successful delivery of enhancements and patches.
jobResponsibilities:
Operational Delivery & Application Portfolio Management

  • Own operational delivery outcomes for the MEPS+ application portfolio across interbank payments, government securities management, and domestic market infrastructures. Make and recommend strategic decisions on application rationalisation, consolidation, or decommissioning to optimise portfolio efficiency.
  • Coordinate release management and delivery cycles with product owners, ensuring timely and quality deployment of enhancements, patches, and security updates across major (semi-annual) and monthly patch cycles.
  • Own Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for applications under management. Review SLI and SLO performance reports produced by the SRE team, identify trends and deviations, and escalate or drive remediation as appropriate. Set requirements for monitoring coverage and alert quality; hold the SRE team accountable for outcomes.
  • Coordinate verification of monthly and quarterly system patching with the SRE team. Ensure patch outcomes are documented and meet compliance requirements.

Tech Delivery Manager Responsibilities (During Release Cycles)

  • Lead release planning and delivery activities during major enhancement releases (semi-annual). Coordinate with product owners, development teams, testing teams, and vendors to establish release scope, timelines, and deployment readiness criteria.
  • Manage release communication to all stakeholders. Provide status updates, escalate blockers, and maintain stakeholder alignment on release objectives and timelines throughout the cycle.
  • Own release governance and quality standards for MEPS+. Define the release readiness criteria and test governance framework that the Software Engineer executes against. Review and sign off on test outcomes, patch verification results, and release readiness reports before production deployment.

Incident Management

  • Own the incident management framework for MEPS+. Define and maintain incident escalation paths, SLO targets (P1, P2, P3), and communication protocols. During major incidents, lead stakeholder communication and coordinate the response — software engineers provide technical investigation and resolution support.
  • Drive root cause analysis and post-mortems following significant incidents. Own the documentation of lessons learned and track implementation of preventive measures to reduce recurrence.

Vendor Coordination & Procurement

  • Own vendor governance for outsourced components and services. Chair vendor performance reviews, monitor SLA compliance, and make escalation decisions when vendor performance falls short. Coordinate with software engineers for detailed technical review of vendor-delivered code and fixes.
  • Lead MAS's participation in procurement activities for outsourced services, including defining tender specifications, evaluating vendor proposals, and contributing to contract negotiations.

Compliance, Governance & Risk Management

  • Coordinate RFI responses across the team, ensuring accurate and timely submission of supporting documentation.
  • Plan and lead resiliency exercises including Disaster Recovery drills, manual contingency procedures, and CyberEx participation. Validate system failover and recovery capabilities. Maintain compliance with ICT Governance policies and standards specific to government financial infrastructure.
jobRequirements:
Essential Criteria

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in managing, operating, or delivering complex mission-critical systems. Minimum 3–4 years in a delivery management, operations management, or technical programme management role with clear accountability for system reliability or release outcomes. Experience with payment systems, securities settlement, or financial infrastructure is advantageous but not required.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead incident response at an organisational level — owning stakeholder communication, driving post-mortems, and implementing systemic improvements. Track record of managing high-stakes operational environments.
  • Proven experience managing vendor relationships, chairing performance reviews, and holding vendors accountable to SLAs. Experience contributing to procurement or contract management activities.
  • Strong experience coordinating release cycles across multiple teams — development, testing, operations, and compliance — with accountability for release readiness decisions.
  • Excellent communication skills. Able to explain technical risks, operational decisions, and compliance requirements clearly to senior leadership, business stakeholders, and regulators. Strong written communication for incident reports, post-mortems, audit RFI responses, and governance documentation.
  • Comfortable working across technical domains without requiring deep hands-on expertise in every platform. Able to engage credibly with software engineers and SRE colleagues, ask the right questions, and make informed decisions based on their input.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams — incident response, release coordination, compliance activities, vendor management — without losing attention to detail or governance rigour.

Desirable Criteria

  • Familiarity with Java/J2EE application environments, Linux/RHEL systems, or SQL — sufficient to engage meaningfully with engineering teams and understand technical risk, without necessarily being a hands-on practitioner.
  • Experience with containerisation technologies (Docker, Kubernetes) or cloud platforms (OpenShift, OpenStack) at a conceptual or governance level.
  • Experience with CICD pipelines, release automation, and test management frameworks.
  • Familiarity with observability and monitoring platforms (e.g. Grafana, ELK stack) from an operational governance perspective.
  • Familiarity with government IT environments and regulatory compliance frameworks (CCoP, CSP, AGO, IM8).
  • Agile delivery experience and comfort collaborating with product teams and development teams.
  • Relevant certifications (e.g. ITIL, PMP, AWS Solutions Architect, or equivalent).

This is a contract role until December 2028. All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

jobDescription: You will be responsible for the end-to-end personnel management and engagement of SAF Volunteer Corps Volunteers (SVs), covering deployment fulfilment, personnel assessment, development and role progression, welfare, recognition and continued service.

jobDescription:
Description of Group:
Looking for a workplace with passion and commitment to empower and restore lives of the vulnerable population in Singapore? Join the Rehabilitation and Protection Group (RPG)! RPG undertakes the statutory functions in the rehabilitation of adult and youth offenders, and the protection of children and families. Our mission is to empower individuals and families to break cycles of abuse, neglect and offending. You influence and shape lives, and in the process, the future of the rehabilitation and protection landscape in Singapore. To support your professional development, you will receive comprehensive training and develop foundational capabilities and knowledge on rehabilitation and protection work. You will also be given the opportunities to rotate to different exciting roles within RPG and broaden your perspectives, skills and experiences.

Description of Division:
As part of the RPG family, the Protective Service (PSV)/Operations (OPS) Division is dedicated to safeguarding the safety and well-being of individuals vulnerable to abuse, neglect, or exploitation—including children, vulnerable adults, and families affected by domestic violence. We provide statutory interventions and supportive services for those who have been seriously harmed or are at high risk of serious harm, ensuring timely, coordinated responses to meet their needs and uphold their protection.

Additionally, PSV/OPS plays a key role in facilitating the child adoption process, ensuring the welfare of both the child and adoptive family. PSV/OPS adopts a holistic approach through early intervention, comprehensive assessments, case management, and crisis response. Our team works in close collaboration with social service agencies, healthcare professionals, law enforcement, and community partners to identify risks, develop safety plans and provide ongoing support.
jobResponsibilities:
Responsibilities:
Reporting to the Assistant Director / Senior Assistant Director, your role is to lead a team of protection officers to safeguard children’s / Vulnerable Adults’ (VAs) safety and wellbeing by providing triages/investigation, supervision and guidance to them in assessing, putting in safety and intervention plans and decision-making for the cases. 

As a Manager (Team Lead) / Senior Manager, you will: 
•	Lead a team of protection officers undertaking triage/investigation, safety planning, guide assessments to put in place appropriate intervention plans and right-siting of referrals or cases to work with families and professionals to ensure continued safety and well-being of children, VAs experiencing abuse, neglect or self-neglect, and egregious cases of Family Violence with imminent danger. 
•	Assist to oversee day to day operations of the team which includes regular reviews of cases, operational processes; 
•	Support and contribute to the development, implementation, and reviews of operational policies and processes to improve effectiveness and efficiency of Ops’s function; and 
•	Work closely with the public and people sectors to offer statutory guidance, care and protection for children who have been abused or neglected, and VAs experiencing abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.

jobDescription: The Built Environment (BE) sector is integral to the design, construction and maintenance of Singapore’s cityscape and infrastructure. However, the sector will need to confront the existential challenges of global climate change, energy and manpower constraints, changing demographics and values, and ageing infrastructure in the coming years. Addressing these challenges requires the ability to manage the trade-offs between the desired outcomes of greater safety, resiliency, quality, sustainability, liveability and as well as to strike a balance between industry regulation and development/promotion.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of a passionate policy team in MND’s Infrastructure Division which serves as an advocate for businesses within the Built Environment (BE) sector, seeking and acting on suggestions on how rules and regulations imposed on the industry can be improved, saving businesses time, effort and money, while creating a nimble, forward looking and agile regulatory regime. 

You will champion regulatory innovation by steering rules review efforts across the BE sector. This includes staffing our Political Office Holders for the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review which reviews cross-cutting regulatory issues across the Whole-of-Government and reduces compliance burden for businesses.  You will also support regulatory reviews to improve productivity across the BE sector, including through the Action Team to Improve Built Environment Productivity chaired by the Minister for National Development. This will involve working with agencies and industry stakeholders to identify regulatory, process and implementation issues that may affect productivity, and propose practical measures to streamline requirements, strengthen coordination and support sector-wide transformation.

Further, you will lead the transformation of the sector through various initiatives, including encouraging digitalisation and adoption of regulatory technologies across the sector.  In your capacity as Secretariat for the BE Rules Review Panel (RRP) chaired by PS/ND, you will work across 11 public agencies that perform regulatory functions in the BE sector.  You will also serve as the deskhead for the Professional Engineers Board, giving you direct exposure to professional development and sector governance. 

Through your work, you will have the exciting opportunity to translate strategic intent and objectives to policy moves and programmes, and work closely with ministries and agencies across the Whole-of-Government.  Depending on your level of seniority and experience, you may be given the opportunity to lead a small team.

• Strong interpersonal, analytical and problem-solving skills 
• A sense of initiative and dynamism

jobDescription:
READY TO DIG DEEPER THAN HEADLINES?

Love connecting dots that others miss? Fascinated by issues and developments that affect Singapore? At Security and Intelligence Division (SID), we’re on a mission to protect Singapore in an increasingly unpredictable world. 

As a Target Analyst, you will conduct deep investigations into entities and networks to identify emerging threats and operational opportunities on issues and developments that shape national interests. You will use multi-source intelligence and data analytics to synthesise information into actionable insights that drive high-stakes decisions. Translation? You won't just be reading news tickers. You'll be uncovering the stories hidden beneath the surface. It's part detective work, part strategy play, and 100% real-world impact. In this role, your analysis protects Singaporeans and safeguards our national interests.

Whether you're a fresh graduate hungry to master specialised analytical tradecraft or a mid-career professional looking to pivot for a greater purpose, this is your chance to contribute to Singapore’s national interests.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Integrate Fragmented Data: Combine data from diverse sources— OSINT, technical metadata, and specialised feeds
•	Separate Signal from Noise: Filter through large volumes of messy, conflicting information by asking the right questions, and discerning the relevant picture from unrelated noise
•	Map Networks: Map out complex networks of entities and operational infrastructures, and create clear pictures from a large web of disparate clues
•	Tell the Story Behind the Data: Translate complex technical data and convoluted investigative trails into clear and concise executive briefs to provide early warning and strategic support for Singapore's policymakers
•	Build & Innovate: Develop new investigative tools, and refine analytical workflows to keep our team ahead of emerging risks

What you will gain
•	Unmatched Purpose: Contribute directly to the safety, stability, and sovereignty of Singapore
•	Culture of Continuous Learning: We invest heavily in professional training, including advanced OSINT, data analytics, foreign languages, and cutting-edge investigative methods
•	High-Calibre Teams: Work alongside passionate, like-minded analysts, data experts, and domain experts who love what they do
jobRequirements:
•	Singapore Citizens only

We are looking for individuals with an investigative mindset who are able to find clarity in ambiguity and turn fragmented data into clear answers. You would possess the creativity to:
•	Hunt for missing pieces: Develop mastery of the information landscape and know where to find additional data sources when the current picture is incomplete
•	Slice and dice data: Approach data with clear questions to ensure your analysis is relevant, looking for patterns that others miss
•	Connect the dots: Turn disjointed or weak signals into a coherent narrative of “how things fit together”

We will provide the tradecraft training; you bring the curiosity. Your job isn’t to know all the answers today, but to have the drive to uncover them. Desired qualities and attributes include:
•	Keen interest in geopolitical, threat or security-related developments
•	Strong investigative, analytical, and problem-solving skills
•	Willingness to apply new tools and technologies to derive insights from information
•	Interest in mastering a foreign language and culture
•	Both detail-oriented and able to zoom out to see the big picture
•	Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
•	Strong communication skills
•	Motivated team player and an independent self-starter

We actively welcome candidates from adjacent backgrounds such as (but not limited to):
•	Geopolitical Risk Researchers: Analysts skilled in open-source research (OSINT), digital forensics, or regional threat monitoring
•	Trust & Safety / Risk Operations: Investigators who identify bad actors, coordinated abuse, or platform manipulation at scale
•	Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI): Analysts who track threat actors, malware campaigns, or digital indicators
•	Financial Crime & Fraud Investigations: Specialists who follow paper trails, map suspicious transactions, and uncover hidden entity relationships

Beyond these professions, candidates with the following foundational skills will hit the ground running:
•	Investigative & OSINT Methodologies: Advanced search techniques, digital footprinting, domain/IP pivoting, social network analysis, and online investigation frameworks
•	Link Analysis & Visualisation: Practical experience with network visualization platforms (e.g., graph analysis tools)
•	Domain Expertise: Familiarity with regional or international geopolitical, threat or security issues
•	Language Expertise: Mastery of a foreign language

We hire at various levels. Junior analysts focus on execution and tradecraft mastery, while experienced hires will lead complex investigations and mentor teams.

jobResponsibilities:
The Rail Digitalisation Division is a cross-functional and multi-disciplinary team set up to drive and deliver LTA’s Railway Common Data Platform (CDP), which includes data analytics and artificial intelligence capabilities to support rail performance and operational/maintenance enhancements. You will be responsible for building the "intelligence layer" of the CDP, developing systems that not only detect anomalies in complex railway time-series data but also reason about them to provide clear, actionable outcomes for maintenance and operations.

We are seeking a Data Scientist / Senior Data Scientist who excels at converting use cases into a data problem and analyzing data to generate value to support decision making. You should have a proven track record of delivering end-to-end machine learning solutions—from data discovery and feature engineering to model deployment and monitoring. The ideal candidate balances deep technical expertise with a value-driven mindset, ensuring that analytical outputs directly translate to better cost efficiency and improved commuter experience. A degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field is required.

Technical Skills

  • Modeling & Time-Series Analysis: Expert proficiency in Python and SQL. Deep experience in time-series forecasting and anomaly detection (e.g., Z-score, growth rate analysis, and statistical thresholds).

  • Data Engineering Synergy: Competence with modern data stacks (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks) and real-time data ingestion via APIs to build scalable, production-ready pipelines.

  • MLOps & Automation: Experience in managing the full ML lifecycle, focusing on "operational AI" that triggers automated workflows or maintenance alerts.

  • Visualization & UI Collaboration: Ability to translate complex model outputs into requirements for UI/UX designers to create intuitive, data-rich enterprise dashboards.

  • Decision Intelligence: Proven ability to build autonomous systems that go beyond simple detection, including experience with AI agents that combine statistical triggers with LLM-based reasoning to automatically categorise, prioritise, and/or escalate operational issues.

Key Attributes

  • Analytical Problem Solver: Strong ability to take vague operational "pain points" and structure them into rigorous analytical frameworks that drive ROI.

  • Stakeholder Management: Exceptional communication skills to explain algorithmic logic and "uncertainty" to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Proactive Learner: A self-starter who stays updated on the latest in Agentic AI and can independently drive design initiatives end-to-end.

  • Collaborative: High comfort level working in a "squad" format alongside UI/UX designers, Product Managers, and Railway Engineers.
jobRequirements:

  • At least 2 years of proven relevant experience in data science, preferably with data-heavy industrial or enterprise products.

  • Experience in transportation, IoT, or large-scale condition-monitoring systems with AI agents is advantageous.

  • Those without working experience but has strong interest in quantitative fields are welcome to apply

jobDescription: You will be part of the Law Publishing Unit in the Legislation Division of the AGC. Requirements:

jobDescription:
You will be part of the Law Editing and Revision Unit in the Legislation Division of the Attorney-General’s Chambers, and will be responsible for providing —
 
•	editorial services for the drafting of legislation, including checking of house-styles, formatting and language checks, fact checking, conducting policy and legal research, and legal checks, establishing and maintaining standard provisions, to ensure consistency and quality control across the Singapore Statute Book,
 
•	simple legislative drafting and legislative advisory services to the Government and statutory authorities, and
 
•	support in preparing revised editions for both Acts and subsidiary legislation.
 
This role also involves organising the timely and efficient proofing of Bills, subsidiary legislation and revised editions, coordinating and liaising between Government Ministries and statutory authorities, the law drafters, editors and publishers within the Division, Parliament Secretariat and the Government Printer to ensure timely and accurate publication in the Gazette and synchronised publication on the online legislation database.
jobResponsibilities:
Your main job responsibilities as an editor include:
 
1.	Providing legislative editorial services and drafting assistance to law drafters, including making editorial amendments for grammar, punctuation, spelling, consistency and compliance with house-styles and drafting directives, as well as simplifying the language of draft legislation, to ensure that legislation to be presented to Parliament or enacted by publication in the Gazette are accurate and error free.
 
2.	Providing advisory services to Government Ministries and statutory authorities on Parliamentary procedures and practices, less complex legal issues and established legislative procedures and processes, publication processes, and drafting approaches.
 
3.	Drafting and vetting less complex subsidiary legislation and Gazette notifications in accordance with the policies of Government Ministries and statutory authorities and in compliance with house-styles and drafting directives, and established precedents.
 
4.	Preparing accurate and error-free revised editions of Acts and subsidiary legislation for publication, including editing to simplify the language (with no change in meaning) and in a way that is consistent with house-styles and drafting directives.
 
5.	Conducting simple legal research.
 
6.	Developing a working knowledge of legislation, legislative processes, house-styles, drafting directives, editing and publishing software, and publication processes, in order to draft, edit and produce high quality work in a short time frame.
 
7.	Proofreading, and performing editorial and stylistic checks of legislation and revised edition proofs before dispatch to Government Ministries and statutory authorities, and before publication.
 
8.	Planning publication schedules for legislation and revised edition projects, including working out resource allocations, timelines and budget (if any).
 
9.	Drafting and vetting minutes of meetings and policy papers for decision/approval.
 
Additionally, you will also be required, from time to time, to provide administrative and legal support services to the Division by undertaking a wide range of administrative projects, committee work and activities to ensure the efficient operation of the Division’s activities and workplan.

jobTitle: Manager/Assistant Director/ Senior Assistant Director (Service Quality)
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.

About Singapore Global Network

Singapore Global Network (SGN) is a division under EDB that grows and engages a 220,000-strong international community of overseas Singaporeans and friends of Singapore. Our mission is to grow Singapore’s global networks by fostering meaningful relationships and communities among international talent, entrepreneurs, students and partners worldwide, while strengthening Singapore’s position as the ideal place to work, live and play.

You will be part of SGN’s Brand & Content team, supporting the development and execution of brand and content marketing initiatives that promote SGN as an international networking community among target audience segments, and building a positive experience with members. This includes building the SGN brand experience, growing its digital channel following, promoting its product offerings, generating new members for the network, and engaging audiences through a mix of online and offline initiatives.

You will also help shape global perceptions of Singapore as an ideal city for international talent to live, work and play in. This includes promoting the many aspects of Singapore’s culture, people and environment. Using compelling storytelling techniques, you will creatively convey Singapore value propositions in a way that gets target audiences excited about the prospects and opportunities that Singapore has to offer.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys creating, experimenting, and collaborating — from shaping creative campaign ideas to producing inspiring content and supporting delivery across digital channels. You will work closely with internal teams, marketing agencies and brand partners to shape how Singapore is represented to global audiences.

Key Responsibilities

Brand & Campaign Management

  • Drive the ideation, development and execution of brand initiatives and marketing campaigns aimed at growing SGN’s digital following, network membership and brand experience.

  • Work with marketing agencies to develop and execute campaigns across online and offline channels.

  • Serve as the custodian of the SGN brand, responsible for reviewing the effectiveness of existing brand toolkit and proposing recommendations that help foster a stronger brand identity and affinity among audiences.

  • Identify brand partners for collaboration to enhance SGN’s value offerings to members.

Content Development & Marketing

  • Shape the content strategy for SGN and drive content development across channels, markets and audience segments.

  • Contribute content ideas and create engaging content across formats that include but are not limited to short-form videos, human-interest stories, explainer videos, editorial content, event coverage, and guides.

  • This includes working with content agencies, media publishers and partners to develop content initiatives and partnerships.

  • Collaborate with product and regional teams to drive content and campaigns aimed at promoting opportunities in Singapore among global talent and entrepreneurs.

  • Identify relevant content creators and key opinion leaders to collaborate on content and campaigns.

Measurement & Optimisation

  • Measure and report on brand, campaign and content-related performance using marketing analytics and social listening tools.

  • Help translate data and insights into learnings and recommendations for improving future campaigns and content.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for a digital native with a fun personality. Someone who is creative, energetic and with a good sense of humour, to bring out the best that Singapore and SGN has to offer.


You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have 1–3 years of experience (or equivalent internships/projects) in digital marketing, content, communications, or social media. Agency and/or media production house experience is welcome but not mandatory.

  • Are a strategic thinker with hands-on experience planning and executing digital marketing campaigns, developing engaging content, and managing social media channels.

  • Are comfortable experimenting with short-form content and open to being behind or in front of the camera when needed (but not required to be an on-screen personality).

  • Have strong writing skills and an eye for attention to detail, from crafting captions to polishing longer-form content.

  • Are familiar with social platforms and trends, and curious about how audiences engage with content.

  • Possess basic experience with tools such as video editing apps (e.g. CapCut), analytics platforms (e.g. Google Analytics), or social listening tools — or are keen to learn.

  • Enjoy working collaboratively in a team environment and contributing ideas and are open to feedback, learning, and developing new skills over time.

jobDescription:
Overview of the Chief Data Officer Office (CDOO)
Advance the data-driven, evidence-based and citizen-centric approach to health promotion through state-of-the-art data best practices to maximize data quality and internationally-recognised governance and policies to promote safe usage of data.

Overview of Data Operations & Architecture Department

Recognising the efficacy of big data and artificial intelligence in optimising sharper insights and outcomes for public health, the Data Operations and Architecture Department will take a proactive role to drive the design of a 360-view citizen-centric data architecture and the implementation of data operations to support and facilitate an evidence-based, data-driven approach to programme delivery. The department will set up and implement data architecture and structuring, cleaning and validation of big data from diverse HPB and partners’ data sources (e.g. food transaction data, sports attendance data, screening and sensor data) to facilitate data feature engineering use cases pivotal to downstream data exploitation. The department will also be involved in strategic collaborations with partners (e.g. public healthcare and data science institutions, academics and technology players) to bring in their data and expertise onto the data operations to benefit citizens.

We are looking for dynamic and enthusiastic individuals, with strong data engineering and data science skills and project delivery experience, to join us on this pioneering journey to build a more data-driven HPB. You will be pivotal in helping to set up and implement a robust data engineering pipeline that can integrate the vast wealth of data HPB has through its numerous data sources. A robust data pipeline ensures that changes from the data sources does not impact the timely delivery of high quality data to our business users.

Given the diversity of data collected from our lifestyle programmes, data science approaches such as machine learning will also be deployed to support the data engineering process. For example, we have build and included machine learning ops to help with standardising event names.

Responsibilities

  • Design optimal data structures for strategic datasets and drive data engineering processes related to data ingestion, data imputation, data transformation and integration to facilitate data science and analytics use cases
  • Build optimised, test driven codes to achieve the above mentioned
  • Translate research and analytics questions into data features to facilitate dashboarding, model training, analytics, and data science applications
  • Build test case on code to ensure that all codes are built to perfection
  • Project manage and be the overall lead for engagement to bring together HPB vendors, partners, IT and business teams to plan, set timelines and drive processes that enable timely delivery of the data engineering pipeline guided by business needs
  • Lead internal cross-functional teams to integrate, process and engineer disparate datasets into structured and meaningful variables to facilitate machine learning and data science use cases
  • Lead the preparation of materials to update senior management periodically on progress of the project and surface issues and challenges for collective deliberation and decision-making

Qualifications and skillsets

  • Bachelor/Masters degree in Computer Science, Engineering or Information Systems with major / project experience in data science and/or business analytics from a recognised university. Professional certifications in data engineering from accredited professional bodies will be highly desirable.
  • Minimum 3-5 years of relevant project management and delivery experience. Experience in end-to-end deployment of data engineering projects in production environment preferred.
  • Proficiency in the use of Python and/or Power BI
  • Experience working on data engineering, and/or database architectural work
  • Experience working on a few of the following component in the data pipeline: data ETL, data cleaning, data modelling, and feature engineering.
  • Able to work in a fast-paced matrix environment, overseeing multiple projects at the same time
  • Good communication skills and able to communicate and express complex data/concepts in a clear and simple-to-understand manner
  • Have the drive, commitment, and perseverance to do well and have strong intellectual curiosity to learn and seek continuous improvements in the work assigned
  • Experience in Big Data technologies e.g. Hadoop and Spark Ecosystems will be desirable
  • Experience with test-driven development will be desirable
  • Take an interest in digital health and healthcare

Rajaratnam School of International Studies (RSIS) is advantageous

agencyDescription:
The Public Service Division (PSD) stewards a trusted Singapore Public Service for a successful and vibrant Singapore. Our 4 key roles include:
•	Developing a flourishing and diverse workforce by supporting our public officers' continual growth of skills and creating meaningful careers 
•	Developing a forward-looking and inspiring community of leaders who are united, resilient, and anchored in public service values and ethos
•	Building future-ready public sector organisations by steering and supporting transformation of our organisations and catalysing innovations for organisations to work more effectively
•	Driving good governance, values and excellence to safeguard the integrity and reputation of the Public Service and uphold the trust of citizens 

Why Join Us
When you join PSD, you become part of a community that learns together and cares for one another. We look out for your well-being and partner you in your career growth. Being in the business of developing People and driving transformation makes our work deeply Purposeful. What you do will impact our public officers and agencies, and in turn make a difference to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you share our passion in reimagining Possibilities and pushing boundaries to shape a first-class Public Service, we welcome you to join us!

|People, Our Pride | Service, Our Pledge | Integrity, Our Core | Excellence, Our Quest |
jobDescription:
The Singapore Public Service offers an attractive career proposition for those who seek to make a difference in service of Singapore and Singaporeans. 

To navigate a more complex and fast-changing environment, the Public Service needs a diversity of strengths and perspectives in our leadership ranks. We therefore welcome leaders with different backgrounds, who wish to contribute their skills and perspectives in the Public Service to make a meaningful impact to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you take up a public service leadership career, we will invest in your development so that you can lead effectively in the Public Service, for today and tomorrow. A key feature of pursuing a public service leadership career is the opportunity for you to undergo structured job postings across different public agencies, to expose you to critical job experiences and key issues facing Government.
jobResponsibilities:
Here are some areas you could contribute to, across the key sectors of Government:

• Social: Shape the ‘heartware’ of Singapore – cultivating a more cohesive, resilient, caring and inclusive society.

• Economy Building: Contribute to Singapore’s growth, macro-economic stability, industry regulation and a conducive business environment.

• Infrastructure & Environment: Contribute to making Singapore a vibrant, clean, liveable city with sustainable development, robust infrastructure and good connectivity.

• Security: Keep Singapore safe and secure through robust enforcement capabilities and sound security policies.

• Central Administration: Ensure effective and efficient use of resources and help develop a consultative and customer-centric Public Service.

• Info-Comm Technology & Smart Systems: Enable better use of data and harnessing of new technologies by the Government to build a digital economy and digital society, in support of Smart Nation.
jobRequirements:
An ideal candidate will be one who: 

• Believes in and demonstrates the Public Service Values of Integrity, Service, Excellence.
• Has the passion to serve and a commitment towards building a better Singapore and to improve the lives of current and future generations of Singaporeans.
• Demonstrates strong leadership qualities, interpersonal skills and cognitive thinking capacities. More senior candidates should have a strong track record in demonstrating these key areas through past work experiences.
• Is a Singapore Citizen.

*Note: The above application route is for candidates who are not currently serving in the Public Service. If you are a public officer, you should contact your Ministry/Agency HR team for more details.

For new graduates, or individuals with around 1 year of working experience, you can look forward to a structured development programme on the PSLP General Phase (GP) that will expose you to the key job roles in the Public Service (i.e. across roles in policy, operations, stakeholder management). This will support your foundational development as a young leader. You will also get to experience work in at least 2 sectors to support you in understanding your longer-term career preferences and aspirations.  

You can obtain updates on the status of your application through the same portal. For shortlisted candidates, PSD will contact you to provide details of the selection process. 
 
• Information on the PSLP and PSC Master’s Scholarship •

For more information on the PSLP, please visit https://www.psd.gov.sg/leadership/public-service-leadership-careers for further clarification.

You may also find out more details of the PSC Master’s Scholarship at https://www.scholarships.gov.sg.
