jobDescription:
The Singapore Public Service offers an attractive career proposition for those who seek to make a difference in service of Singapore and Singaporeans. 

To navigate a more complex and fast-changing environment, the Public Service needs a diversity of strengths and perspectives in our leadership ranks. We therefore welcome leaders with different backgrounds, who wish to contribute their skills and perspectives in the Public Service to make a meaningful impact to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you take up a public service leadership career, we will invest in your development so that you can lead effectively in the Public Service, for today and tomorrow. A key feature of pursuing a public service leadership career is the opportunity for you to undergo structured job postings across different public agencies, to expose you to critical job experiences and key issues facing Government. 

Regardless of where you are in your career journey, you can apply for the Public Service Leadership Careers through the “Apply Now” button below. 

**Note: To avoid duplicate applications, applicants who have applied for the Public Service Leadership Programme (PSLP) should not apply separately for this role.
jobResponsibilities:
Here are some areas you could contribute to, across the key sectors of Government:

• Social: Shape the ‘heartware’ of Singapore – cultivating a more cohesive, resilient, caring and inclusive society.

• Economy Building: Contribute to Singapore’s growth, macro-economic stability, industry regulation and a conducive business environment.

• Infrastructure & Environment: Contribute to making Singapore a vibrant, clean, liveable city with sustainable development, robust infrastructure and good connectivity.

• Security: Keep Singapore safe and secure through robust enforcement capabilities and sound security policies.

• Central Administration: Ensure effective and efficient use of resources and help develop a consultative and customer-centric Public Service.

• Info-Comm Technology & Smart Systems: Enable better use of data and harnessing of new technologies by the Government to build a digital economy and digital society, in support of Smart Nation.
jobRequirements:
An ideal candidate will be one who: 

• Believes in and demonstrates the Public Service Values of Integrity, Service, Excellence.
• Has the passion to serve and a commitment towards building a better Singapore and to improve the lives of current and future generations of Singaporeans.
• Demonstrates strong leadership qualities, interpersonal skills and cognitive thinking capacities. More senior candidates should have a strong track record in demonstrating these key areas through past work experiences.
• Is a Singapore Citizen.

*Note: The above application route is for candidates who are not currently serving in the Public Service. If you are a public officer, you should contact your Ministry/Agency HR team for more details.

For new graduates, or individuals with 1-3 years of working experience, you can look forward to a structured development programme on the PSLP General Phase (GP) that will expose you to the key job roles in the Public Service (i.e. across roles in policy, operations, stakeholder management). This will support your foundational development as a young leader. You will also get to experience work in at least 2 sectors to support you in understanding your longer-term career preferences and aspirations.  

For individuals with more extensive working experience, please refer to the next section on the Mid-Career Leadership Track.
You can obtain updates on the status of your application through the same portal. For shortlisted candidates, PSD will contact you to provide details of the selection process. 


• Mid-Career Leadership Track (MCLT) •

The Public Service values the experiences of mid-career entrants outside of the Public Service and is interested to groom talents with the heart to serve. The Public Service will be introducing the “Mid-Career Leaders Track” - a central gateway for mid-career entrants with the potential and aspiration to serve in Public Service leadership.

Key Features of MCLT:

• Central gateway for mid-career entrants to apply for Leadership Programmes in the Public Service
- Candidates may be considered for the PSLP Sectoral Phase (SP) or the Administrative Service (AS), where they would be supported in deepening their competencies either within a sector (PSLP SP) or across 2-3 sectors (AS).

- Candidates can apply without needing to choose to join the AS/PSLP or any specific government agencies. Successful candidates will be placed onto the appropriate leadership programme, where their past work experiences will be taken into account when curating relevant postings / developmental opportunities, based on the assessed calibre, readiness and seniority.

- The AS aims to develop multi-sectoral leaders with whole-of-government perspectives and capabilities, to formulate and implement policies that will improve the lives of Singaporeans. The career path of the AS can be found here.

- The PSLP aims to develop sectoral leaders for key leadership positions within the Public Service. There are 2 phases in this talent development programme. You will go through structured rotations during the General Phase to explore and gain experience in at least two different sectors of the Public Service, while at the Sectoral Phase, you will focus your development within a sector, building deeper competencies and networks. The career path of the PSLP can be found here.

• Structured job placement and onboarding support to support mid-career officers’ transition to the Public Service 

- For their first one or two postings, officers on the MCLT will select from a list of curated jobs that provides developmental exposure while having adjacencies to their previous work experience. This allows officers to leverage their expertise and experiences in making substantive contributions, while supporting their learning and transition into the Public Service. Officers can look forward to a meaningful career journey across a variety of postings such as job roles in policy-operations as well as stakeholder mobilisation and engagement, which will tap on officers’ knowledge, skills and perspectives. 

- A tailored onboarding experience with structured and personalised onboarding process to support officers’ transition on the MCLT. This is especially for working professions without any prior experience working in the Public Service.

You can apply for the MCLT by clicking on the "Apply" button. 

For more information on the PSLC, please visit https://www.psd.gov.sg/leadership/public-service-leadership-careers for further clarification.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Department of Statistics is the National Statistical Authority responsible for statistics on the Singapore economy and population.

We collect, compile, analyse and disseminate a wide range of economic, business, household and population data, as well as analyse and monitor trends in the economy and population.

With these vital inputs, policymakers, business decision makers and our data users gain valuable insights into current and emerging economic and social trends, enabling them to make calculated and informed decisions in the formulation of policies and strategies for the future. jobDescription:
DECODING THE WORLD FOR SINGAPORE’S DECISION MAKERS

Do you often ask why countries behave in a certain way? Curious about why global trends play out the way they do? Are you passionate about helping Singapore secure its place in the world?

At Security and Intelligence Division (SID), you are a key source of expertise and insight into geopolitics and international security within the Singapore government. We analyse and synthesise myriad information into insights that directly inform national leaders and top policymakers. Join us in decoding a dynamic and uncertain world for Singapore’s top decision-makers.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Build and Maintain Strategic Awareness: monitor and sieve through information to find, verify, and interpret data and information from multiple sources
•	Forecast Trends and Emerging Risks which impacting Singapore’s national interests
•	Provide Timely and Relevant Insights for national leaders and top policymakers in the form of policy briefings and high-impact writing
•	Conduct Deep Research into specific countries/regions, and/or multilateral trends and themes
•	Engage Key Policymaking Agencies in the Singapore government: brief key decision-makers on critical issues and participate in cross-agency discussions as subject matter experts, while also gaining a better understanding of national interests
•	Build Partnerships: engage foreign government partners as part of intelligence diplomacy, and to sharpen analysis, deepen expertise, and build intelligence tradecraft
•	At senior levels: 
        - Lead and manage teams of analysts
        - Develop cognitive tools and methods to ensure robust and insightful analysis 
        - Develop junior analysts

What you will gain:

•	High-Level Impact, Direct Executive Visibility: produce insights that go straight to the desks of top policymakers shaping Singapore's national strategy
•	High-Calibre Teams: be part of a community of passionate geopol geeks and country specialists in an intellectually stimulating environment
•	Access to top thinkers in governments and academia on critical and emerging global issues
•	Culture of Continuous Learning: we invest heavily in professional training, such as in-house training, collaborative training with foreign partners, and access to courses by local universities
jobRequirements:
•     Singapore Citizens only

We value intellectual curiosity and an openness to alternative ideas; critical thinking and evidence-based analytical skills; and a drive for excellence. A good command of English and some comfort with uncertainty and ambiguity are also necessary. If you love dissecting complex international issues and explaining why it matters for Singapore in simple terms, you’ll fit right in.

We will provide the tradecraft training; you bring the curiosity. Your job isn’t to know all the answers today, but to have the drive to uncover them. Desired qualities and attributes include:
•	Keen interest in geopolitical, threat or security-related developments
•	Strong written and verbal communication skills
•	Detail-oriented but also able to see the big picture
•	Able and willing to learn
•	Strong interpersonal skills and able to work collaboratively
•	Motivated and independent
•	Strong problem-solving skills
•	Willingness to learn and apply new tools and technologies to analysis work

We actively welcome candidates from adjacent backgrounds such as (but not limited to):
•	Policy-making Units in both the public and private sector, especially those with a focus on geopolitics and global security
•	Geopolitical & Country Risk Advisory including corporate risk consultancies evaluating political instability and country risk
•	Macroeconomic & Strategy Consulting specialists who cover international economic issues such as supply chain vulnerabilities and trade flows
•	Journalism & Foreign Correspondence
•	Think Tanks & Policy Research analysts who cover foreign policy, multilateral security, or regional dynamics
•	Legal Professionals and Regulatory Counsel

Beyond these professions, candidates with the following foundational skills will hit the ground running:
•	Geopolitical Risk and International Security Analysis including country politics, foreign policy, multi-player dynamics in international affairs, and macroeconomics
•	Structured Analytical Techniques like analysis of competing hypotheses, back casting, red teaming and horizon scanning

agency: Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry
agencyDescription:
Working at METI places you at the heart of Singapore’s economic policy-making. We drive productivity-led growth, safeguard and expand our economic space, and build a future-ready economy where firms can thrive. Together, we create a Singapore which is a city of possibilities, a home to great firms, and a place where the world connects — with people at its heart.

When you join METI, you contribute to our mission of creating good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans, enabling them to improve their lives and secure a better future.
jobDescription:
METI’s Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division plays a key role in creating an energy system that is secure, resilient, cost-competitive, and ready to transition to a low carbon future. Our work keeps the lights on today, and builds the power system for tomorrow.

Energy is an existential issue for Singapore. We import almost all our energy supply and are exposed to global energy market movements. Recent global developments and energy crises have disrupted the global energy ecosystem. The climate crisis compels all countries to accelerate their pace of decarbonisation, even as they manage rising energy costs and unpredictable supply chain shocks. At the same time, our energy system is an enabler for economic growth, as speed to power is critical to capture strategic and economically significant investments.

Amidst this backdrop, Singapore needs a stable, reliable, and cost-competitive energy system that safeguards our economic competitiveness and dynamism.
jobResponsibilities:
METI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships.

The Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in ensuring energy remains a key enabler of Singapore’s competitiveness, climate goals and national resilience via the five ‘Cs’:

•	Confidence - ensure our system resilience continues to be a source of confidence for our people, through multiple lines of defence to safeguard energy security, resilience, and reliability. These include diversifying our fuel sources and strengthening our fuel reserves.

•	Competitiveness - harness energy to bolster our economic competitiveness, through scaling our generation and grid capacity to meet growing needs and attract electricity-intensive investments. The climate crisis requires us to quickly transition to low-carbon energy sources to avoid the devastating impact of rising temperatures. Decarbonising our power sector, which contributes 40% of current emissions, is key to realising Singapore’s commitment to achieving net zero emissions by 2050.

Even as we take steps to secure a low-carbon energy supply, we will also need to safeguard our energy security and affordability. Navigating the energy trilemma successfully will be one of the defining policy challenges of our generation and hold far-reaching implications for our economy and society.

In 2027, Singapore will take on the ASEAN Chairmanship. For the energy sectoral track, this will be an important opportunity to advance regional cooperation and drive progress on energy connectivity through the ASEAN Power Grid (APG).

The intern will assist the Individual Insolvency & Debt Repayment Scheme Division ("IIDRSD") of the Insolvency & Public Trustee's Office (“IPTO”) in the following tasks, in either the Debt Repayment Scheme or Adjudication role.

Debt Repayment Scheme Role

a) Assess debtor's application to be placed under the Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”)
b) Examine documents submitted by the debtor and verify extent of debtor's assets and liabilities.
c) Conduct meeting of creditors to determine debtor’s repayment plan.
d) Handle both general and case-specific enquiries from debtors and creditors
e) Assist DRS officers to review cases for cessation of the debt repayment plans (completion, failure or inapplicable for DRS)  

Adjudication Role

a) Examine the validity of claims filed by creditors.
b) Correspond with creditors, solicitors and/or bankrupts on request for additional information and/or further documentary evidence in support of the claims filed against the bankruptcy estate – may include resolving disputes between creditors and bankrupts which arise in the adjudication of the Proof of Debt.
c) Sending statutory rejection notice to creditors whose claims are not admitted by the Official Assignee.
d) Conduct preliminary adjudication for case classification and the Official Assignee’s asset realisation efforts.
d) Assess creditors’ appeals to file Proof of Debt after the expiration of statutory timeline.
e) Liaise with solicitors in respect of suits, counterclaims, contingent claims, and unquantified damages.

As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. jobDescription:
Shape Singapore’s Health at the National Level

Are you a medical doctor looking to make an impact beyond a clinical setting? Whether you are a junior doctor exploring your career options, or an established clinician contemplating new challenges to contribute at the national level, consider a career at the Ministry of Health (MOH).

Under the MOH Medical Service Scheme employment, you will bring your clinical lens and expertise to national healthcare policies and influence decisions that shape the health of Singapore. You will work at the intersection of medicine and policy to design the healthcare systems and frameworks that aim to improve the health outcomes for the nation, and be part of the national health leadership. 

You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. This is a role for doctors who are energised by complexity, motivated by purpose, and ready to drive healthcare transformation at a national scale.
jobResponsibilities:
You will contribute across four key domain areas:

•	Healthcare Regulation — Safeguarding standards and ensuring the safety, quality, and integrity of Singapore's healthcare system.
•	Manpower Development & Capability Building — Shaping the pipeline and professional development of Singapore's healthcare workforce.
•	Population Health & Health Services — Designing and delivering health programmes and services that keep Singaporeans healthy across their life course.
•	Quality, Value & Informatics — Driving innovation, data-driven decision making, and value in healthcare delivery.

At more senior levels, you may also lead and manage a team.

As part of your development, you may also be rotated to other public sector agencies and organisations within the broader healthcare ecosystem — such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Health Promotion Board (HPB), Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA), or the public healthcare clusters. Your postings will be carefully designed to broaden your exposure and deepen your understanding of how policy translates into operations on the ground, equipping you with a well-rounded perspective to grow and contribute meaningfully throughout your career with MOH. 

While you will mostly be involved in healthcare policy work, you may also continue with sessional clinical practice, if you prefer, at the public healthcare institutions, so that you can maintain your clinical currency and familiarity with ground operations.
jobRequirements:

•	Collaborative Spirit: You work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and are energised by cross-agency initiatives that drive system-wide change.
•	Critical Thinking: You bring your medical perspectives to bear on complex policy questions, evaluating evidence rigorously to inform national healthcare decisions.
•	Capacity for Change: You are adaptable and responsive to evolving health priorities, emerging challenges, and shifting policy landscapes.
•	Commitment to Continuous Learning: You are passionate about growing beyond clinical practice — into the domains of healthcare policy, regulation, and population health strategy.
•	Compassion: You connect with diverse stakeholders with empathy, and understand how policy decisions translate into real outcomes for real people.

We are also looking for doctors who demonstrate strength in systems thinking — the ability to understand complex healthcare ecosystems as a whole— as well as strategic thinking and the leadership capacity to inspire and guide teams through transformation.

Are you ready to build next-generation, sustainable cold chain logistics for life-saving biopharmaceuticals?

Republic Polytechnic's School of Engineering (SEG), in strategic partnership with industry leader SSW Group, is seeking an ambitious full-time Research Staff (12-month contract) to engineer an industrial-scale 1"m" ^3 self-sustained passive cold storage platform under a DGF-funded initiative.

Current biopharmaceutical distribution relies on massive active energy inputs and heavy daily coolant consumption. This project completely disrupts that model by building a zero-power-in-transit, high-performance thermal container (1"m"×1"m"×1"m" ) capable of locking in sub-zero temperatures (2–8°C) for over 72 continuous hours in harsh tropical environments.

Beyond standard transport, this passive design provides critical fail-safe protection against warehouse power outages and opens up new pathways for long-haul air and sea freight to distant international markets without relying on active electrical refrigeration networks.

You will lead the hands-on engineering across two breakthrough technological pillars:

About EDB
The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), a government agency under the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI), is responsible for strategies that enhance Singapore’s position as a global centre for business, innovation, and talent. For more information on EDB, please visit www.edb.gov.sg

About the EDB Associate Programme
The global economy is constantly changing. Technologies are reshaping industries, businesses are rethinking where and how they invest, and competition between economies continues to intensify. For Singapore to stay ahead, we need officers who are versatile, resilient and able to make sense of these shifts to identify opportunities and translate them into meaningful outcomes.

The EDB Associate Programme (AP) is a 10-month programme designed to build the foundations of a career at EDB. Through structured training, personalised mentorship and rotations across different areas of EDB’s work, you will gain first-hand exposure to how we work with companies, industries and partners to shape Singapore’s economic future.

Work alongside colleagues in a high-performing, collaborative environment and be part of a team that cares deeply about Singapore’s success and challenges one another to do better.
jobResponsibilities:
What the Programme Entails

Your Associate journey begins with a structured bootcamp that introduces you to EDB’s mission, work and ways of working, and equips you with foundational skills.

You will then be rotated across multiple divisions. Each rotation will give you opportunities to experience new challenges and work with different colleagues and stakeholders. Through these rotations, you will gain exposure to the core areas of EDB’s work:

1) Investment Promotion – Engage directly with companies to understand their business strategies and make the case for Singapore as an investment destination. This involves building relationships with senior business leaders, analysing industry trends, structuring project proposals, and negotiating with companies on the terms of their commitments to Singapore.

What you develop: Business acumen, relationship management and an understanding of global business dynamics

2) Industry Development – Beyond individual company relationships, EDB works to strengthen our economic sectors. We do so by mapping out an industry’s ecosystem, identifying gaps in capabilities or talent, and working with companies, trade associations, and other agencies to develop strategies that make Singapore a competitive hub.

What you develop: Systems thinking, strategy formulation, partnership building and the ability to translate insights into actionable programmes or initiatives.

3) Policy and Planning – EDB charts Singapore’s long-term economic trajectory – where the economy is headed, what structural shifts are underway globally, and what that means for Singapore’s positioning. You will work on frameworks, policies and incentives that shape how EDB attracts and retains investments.

What you develop: Analytical and research capabilities, skills in policy development and evaluation, and the ability to synthesise complex information

All Associates will also undergo foreign language training, giving you an early foundation to strengthen your ability to engage businesses and partners from around the world.

  • Administer and enforce port clearance requirements to maintain safe, secure and well-regulated vessel movements.

You should have strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to engage diverse stakeholders both in writing and in person. You should also be comfortable working with data and using insights to support policies, strategies and operational decisions. jobDescription: SENIOR/ MANAGER, DATA PARTNERSHIPS — TRANSPORT AI PROGRAMME, LTA SINGAPORE
jobResponsibilities:
Singapore's land transport network moves millions of people every day. As AI reshapes what's possible in transport operations, the Land Transport Authority is investing in AI capabilities that will meaningfully improve how the network is sensed, managed, and optimised — for commuters, operators, and public officers alike.

AI systems are only as good as the data that powers them. We are looking for a Senior/ Manager to establish and lead our data acquisition and partnership function — the foundational capability that will enable our organisation to develop meaningful, operationally relevant data use cases and AI-enabled applications.

Beyond internal organisational data, operationally relevant datasets may be found across government agencies, industry partners, and contractors — each governed by their own access controls, sharing frameworks, and institutional considerations. You will be required to understand our concept of operations well enough to determine what data is needed, and pursue access to that data through establishing relationships, agreements and organisational infrastructure required to bring the right data in securely and sustainably.

What You Will Be Working On

You will lead a team to translate our concept of operations into a prioritised multi-modal data acquisition roadmap, identifying what data we need and sequencing efforts by operational value and feasibility. Your work also involves stakeholder engagement, negotiating access with government agencies, statutory boards, industries and research institutions.

As part of data acquisition, you will lead your team to define and enforce standards for how data is received — covering file formats, data schemas, metadata requirements, and update cadences. This ensures that datasets from disparate sources can be reliably ingested, integrated, and made ready for analytical and AI workloads. Where partners or contractors are unable to meet these standards natively, you will work with them to find practical solutions or manage the necessary transformation processes internally.

You will also be responsible for identifying and building the right platform for consolidating data from multiple sources, particularly where contractor or sensitive datasets introduce security and classification constraints that may rule out standard environments. You will work with technical, legal, and cybersecurity colleagues to arrive at an appropriate approach.

Underpinning all of this is sound data governance — ensuring that what we acquire is handled compliantly, with appropriate agreements and access controls in place. You will work closely with analytical, AI development and product teams to ensure that acquired data is properly onboarded and ready for use case development.

• Exposure to cloud-native development and modern DevOps practices (CI/CD, Docker, Kubernetes).
• Hands-on experience with AI orchestration frameworks.

• Exposure to advanced search architectures, specifically vector search, semantic search, and RAG patterns.

  • Identify risks, dependencies and bottleneck early, to develop mitigation plans to keep deployments on track.

jobDescription: [LTA-TRO] SENIOR/ EXECUTIVE UX/UI ENGINEER, TRAFFIC & ROAD IT
jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for a UX/UI Engineer to own, design, and scale the user experience powering our next-generation applications and digital services. In this role, you will bridge hands-on interface design with a deep understanding of user needs, working across agile squads to champion UX/UI best practices and ensure consistent, accessible, and intuitive product experiences.

You will drive the entire design lifecycle — from conducting upfront user research and aligning design specifications with stakeholders, to building robust prototypes and maintaining post-launch design quality. Beyond crafting visually compelling interfaces, you will ensure long-term design excellence by embedding rigorous usability testing, resolving experience gaps identified through user feedback, and maintaining comprehensive design documentation such as design systems, component libraries, and interaction guidelines.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design, Computer Science, or a related field, with at least 3 years of experience in UX/UI design, front-end engineering, or a related discipline.

  • The following skills are mandatory: a foundational understanding of UX/UI design principles including user research, information architecture, and interaction design; proficiency in at least one design tool such as Figma or Adobe XD to build interactive prototypes, conduct user flows, and maintain design systems; basic experience conducting usability testing and translating findings into design improvements; and the ability to translate wireframes and high-fidelity mockups into semantic, responsive code using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript/TypeScript.

  • The following skills are advantageous: familiarity with modern JavaScript frameworks such as React, Vue, or Angular; knowledge of accessibility standards such as WCAG 2.1; familiarity with the Singapore Government Design System (SGDS); exposure to CI/CD practices including SHIP-HATS; and familiarity with Government Digital Service standards and IM8 compliance requirements.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to contribute across the full product lifecycle from user research and accessibility audits to post-launch design iteration and front-end tracking, and a proactive and user-centric approach to problem-solving with a strong sense of ownership over interface quality and design consistency.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

agencyDescription: The Singapore Prison Service protects society through the safe and secure custody of offenders. We take the lead in providing guidance to offenders under our charge and assist them in their reintegration upon their release. We cooperate with our partners in aftercare and prevention, working with them to rehabilitate, renew, and restart the lives of offenders so they can become productive members of society. This includes conducting routine checks, managing entry and exit points, monitoring surveillance systems, and responding swiftly to any incidents or emergencies.

You will actively interact with offenders, addressing their concerns and supporting their access to rehabilitation programmes and services. Your presence will be critical in fostering a secure and purposeful environment, where order and discipline are upheld.

jobTitle: SCDF Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) - 3 Year Contract
agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.
jobDescription:
The 3-Year Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) contract position with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) presents an exceptional opportunity for individuals seeking to gain invaluable medical experience as part of the esteemed Life Saving Force. This role offers an exclusive pathway for passionate individuals to immerse themselves in frontline emergency response scenarios.

Applicants who hold a valid Class 3 Driving License, coupled with academic credentials such as ‘N’-Levels,  'O' Levels, NITEC, Higher NITEC, or Diploma qualifications, and aspire to contribute to the Lifesaving Force upon graduation, will find the 3-Year EMT position to be an attractive proposition. This career trajectory allows individuals to concurrently engage in meaningful work, earn a competitive salary, and delve into the realm of life-saving endeavours.

Upon joining the SCDF, officers can expect to secure stable full-time employment accompanied by a compelling remuneration package. This package encompasses a potential base monthly salary ranging from approximately $2,940 - $4,370, augmented by supplementary allowances and bonuses.

As valued members of SCDF, employees stand to benefit from a range of perks and privileges, including:
•	Competitive salary range, inclusive of frontline / shift allowance
•	Annual Increments
•	Performance Bonuses
•	14 to 18 Days of Vacation Leave
•	Medical and Dental Subsidies
•	Employee Welfare Benefits
•	Group Insurance Coverage
•	Vocational Section Commander Certification
•	Emergency Medical Technician Certification
•	Emergency Vehicle Ambulance Driving Certification

Successful applicants will receive a $6,000 sign-on bonus (subject to eligibility), with officers also having the chance to secure full-time employment and an additional $24,000 sign-on bonus  (subject to eligibility) upon emplacement as a Fire and Rescue Specialist or Paramedic Specialist.

Embracing this role not only offers professional growth opportunities but also enables individuals to make a tangible difference in emergency medical care provision. Join us in safeguarding lives and property, while embarking on a fulfilling career journey with SCDF.
jobResponsibilities:
Officers enrolled in this course will join the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) as an Emergency Medical Technician-Driver, entrusted with the vital mission of preserving lives and property in diverse emergency scenarios while operating ambulances. Within this capacity, their duties entail swift response to medical incidents and other rescue operations, leveraging their training to deploy essential medical procedures and administer aid to individuals in distress.

Embracing a role within SCDF not only signifies a commitment to community service but also presents a profound opportunity to contribute significantly by safeguarding lives and property amid emergencies.

As a 3-Year EMT Contract Officer, individuals can anticipate a structured career trajectory that encompasses rigorous training in Vocational Section Commander and Emergency Medical Technical skills. Upon successful completion of these training modules, officers will be stationed at a designated fire station. For further insights into your career progression, please refer to our corporate website for EMT Contract Officers.
jobRequirements:
The eligibility criteria for the 3-Year EMT Contract role include: 
•	Applicants with NS obligations must be medically classified as PES C2 or above
•	Possesses a valid Class 3/3A Driving License with more than 1 year of validity, as successful applicants will be required to drive an ambulance that requires either a Class 3 or 3A license.
•	GCE 'N' Level and above

We are an elite team of emergency response professionals from the Fire and Rescue Service (FRS) and Emergency Medical Service (EMS), dedicated to saving lives and protecting property. Join our family as we strive to safeguard and make a difference in the lives of our citizens, both in peacetime and during emergencies.
jobResponsibilities:
Be the source of courage and compassion. As a Fire and Rescue Specialist (FRS) with the SCDF, you'll be trained to become a motivated leader skilled in fire prevention, response, and investigation, as well as emergency rescue. You'll also be equipped with Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) skills. After foundational postings, exciting opportunities for further specialisation (e.g. Disaster Assistance Response Team, Hazardous Material Specialist, Marine Specialist) and skills upgrades across a myriad of career pathways await you.

As you progress in your career, you can expect to take up higher appointments such as Fire Station Deputy ROTA Commander or Fire & Rescue Instructor. Good performing FRS can look forward to accelerated advancement opportunities, with the potential for direct promotion to the rank of lieutenant and beyond.

Upon joining SCDF, you will secure stable full-time employment with an attractive remuneration package. Candidates can earn between $2,940 - $4,370, inclusive of monthly frontline allowances.

As a successful applicant, you will receive a $30,000 sign-on bonus (subject to eligibility) upon emplacement. You will also stand to receive benefits from a range of perks and privileges, including: 
•	Competitive salary range, inclusive of frontline / shift allowance
•	Annual increment
•	Performance bonus 
•	14 to 18 days’ vacation leave (inclusive of other leave types) 
•	Medical and Dental Subsidies 
•	Employee welfare benefits 
•	Learning and Development subsidy 
•	Strategic Payment Scheme 
•	Invest Retirement Package 
•	MHA Group insurance 
•	Obtain a Fire Safety Manager Certification 
•	Obtain an Emergency Medical Technician Certification 
•	Obtain Class 3, 4 and/or 5 Driving Licenses

jobDescription:
MOM’s Work Pass Division (WPD) is modernising its Work Permit (WP) eServices (known as WINS-WP) to deliver reliable, adaptive, and user-friendly eServices that streamlines WP transactions for our customers. The WINS-WP Policy & Planning Office (WPPO) drives this modernisation effort through formulating a transformation roadmap, conducting thorough business process reviews (BPRs), and driving change management.

As a member of the WPPO team, you will play a key role in shaping and transforming the service delivery of Singapore’s Work Permit policies. Working at the intersection of policy, operations and systems, you will lead complex business process reviews and ground-up policy reviews to support the development of the WINS-WP system. You will also conduct engagements and prepare communications materials to ensure that users are well-equipped to navigate the changes. This role is critical in ensuring that WP workflows are robust, future-ready and user-centric, while remaining aligned with policy intent and operational realities.

The roles offers:
•	Meaningful work that contributes directly to national workforce and manpower outcomes
•	Opportunities to work on large-scale policy and digital transformation initiatives
•	Exposure to cross-divisional and cross-agency collaboration
•	A professional environment that values learning, initiative and teamwork
jobResponsibilities:
•	Chart out the WINS-WP transformation journey by contributing to transformation roadmaps, defining user journeys, and shaping success metrics from a business and policy perspective.
•	Conduct complex Work Permit Business Process Reviews (BPRs), re-examining end-to-end workflows, challenging legacy practices, and designing streamlined “to-be” processes.
•	Work closely with MOM policy divisions and operational teams to carry out ground-up policy reviews, translating policy intent into workable operational and system designs.
•	Engage internal and external stakeholders, including system and technology teams and other government agencies, to assess impacts, manage trade-offs, and adjust to changes arising from process and policy changes.

•	Strategic thinker with the ability to challenge the status quo while balancing policy objectives, operational feasibility and user experience
•	Good interpersonal and communication skills, and ability to work across agencies and diverse stakeholders to reach mutually beneficial outcomes

jobDescription:
What the role is

You will be part of the team that develops the specialised engineering capabilities required to establish EMA as an informed technical lead on advanced nuclear power systems. You will be responsible for building internal capabilities to evaluate the engineering feasibility and safety profiles of complex energy technologies, ensuring that the organization can benchmark global designs against international safety, security, and safeguards standards.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on:

1. Engineering Benchmarking & Technical Modelling

  • Technical Specialisation: Build specialised institutional expertise in advanced thermal-hydraulic systems, core physics, and material behaviour for next-generation nuclear energy technologies.

  • Multi-disciplinary Assessment: Conduct engineering research across Civil, Mechanical, and Electrical disciplines to verify the technical claims of emerging global technologies.

  • Conceptual Modelling: Support the development of technical benchmarks and reference architectures for various advanced reactor concepts (e.g., Light Water SMRs and High-Temperature Gas-cooled Reactors).

  • Feasibility Research: Study how global engineering designs might theoretically be optimised, exploring concepts like modular construction and system co-location.

2. Safety Case & Risk Management

  • Hazard Modelling: Develop capabilities in high-level hazard identification and risk modelling using methodologies such as Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA) and Fault Tree Analysis to understand theoretical failure modes.

  • Safety Case Research: Study the development of safety cases to understand how deterministic and probabilistic engineering controls align.

  • Technical Standards Governance: Build frameworks to evaluate how design modifications might affect the overall integrity of a technology's safety envelope.

3. Strategic Technical Partnerships

  • Technical Collaboration: Coordinate with international engineering consultants and research organizations to facilitate knowledge transfer and capability building.

  • Standards Advocacy: Act as a technical lead in researching how international engineering standards can be applied to optimise advanced technology for compact land-use constraints.

  • Technology Horizon Scanning: Monitor global trends in advanced nuclear technology (e.g., SMRs and Generation IV systems) to provide data-driven technical insights to senior leadership.
jobRequirements:
Education

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Nuclear, Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering or other relevant engineering fields.

Preferred Experience

  • 8–10 years of engineering experience in high-complexity engineering environments (e.g., Power Utilities, Aerospace, Oil & Gas, or Chemicals).

  • Familiarity with international nuclear standards (e.g., IAEA SSR-2/1) and advanced risk assessment tools (HAZID/HAZOP, LOPA).

  • Experience with international codes (ASME, EN/ISO, etc).

  • Experience with deterministic, probabilistic, quantitative safety assessments and methodology.

  • Safety case development / process safety experience for Major Hazards Industries (MHI) in Singapore


Competencies and Other Requirements

  • Safety Culture mindset.

  • Design for safety, and maintainability.

  • Critical review of vendor technical documentation.

  • Technical writing for regulatory submissions.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesise technical, and policy considerations.

  • Openness to being stationed overseas for extended periods (3 months –2 years) for specialised training and attachments.

jobDescription: As Director (Assurance), you will serve as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to public agency leadership, leading high-performing internal audit teams delivering Shared IA Services to Ministries and Statutory Boards. This is not simply an audit leadership role — you will be a change agent, driving the evolution of IA practices across the public sector through digital innovation, agile methodologies, and a broadened risk lens that encompasses technology, cybersecurity, and sustainability. You will shape the future of the public sector IA community by building capabilities, professionalising practices, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and intellectual curiosity.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic Audit Leadership

You will direct the planning, management, and execution of risk-based audit engagements across agencies under AGD's portfolio of clients, ensuring timely delivery and consistently high audit quality. Moving beyond traditional compliance-focused auditing, you will develop and maintain a forward-looking audit universe that reflects emerging risks and align audit priorities with the broader governance and risk landscape of the public sector. You will also champion agile auditing methodologies, designing shorter and more iterative audit cycles that deliver faster, more actionable insights to stakeholders.

Digital Transformation 

You will lead the integration of data analytics, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI-assisted audit tools into the audit methodology to enable continuous monitoring and deeper audit insights. You will oversee the adoption of audit management platforms to improve workflow efficiency and documentation standards. Staying ahead of developments in generative AI, machine learning, and other emerging technologies, you will assess their applicability to the IA function and build the team's capacity to leverage these tools effectively. Experience with data analytics tools such as Power BI, or Python in an audit context will be particularly valued.

Emerging Risk and Advisory

As a strategic advisor, you will engage credibly with C-suite and senior public sector leadership, translating complex audit findings into clear, business-relevant insights that drive meaningful governance improvements. You will provide assurance and advisory perspectives on a broadened risk landscape, including IT general controls, cybersecurity risk, digital business processes, third-party and supply chain risk, and increasingly, sustainability and ESG governance frameworks. You will work closely with agency leadership to anticipate risks before they materialise, positioning IA as a forward-looking function rather than a retrospective one.

Community Building and Capability Development

You will work with IA heads across the public sector to build a vibrant community of practice, driving the development of shared frameworks, toolkits, and upskilling programmes that raise the overall standard of public sector IA. You will implement capability development roadmaps that equip IA practitioners with both technical audit competencies and digital skills — including data literacy, AI fluency, and agile ways of working. You will represent AGD in cross-agency forums and professional bodies to advance the ambition of public sector IA.

People Leadership and Culture

You will manage, mentor, and develop a team of IA professionals, building a pipeline of future audit leaders who are technically strong, digitally capable, and strategically minded. You will foster a team culture that values psychological safety, diversity of thought, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine commitment to public service excellence. Attracting and retaining talent in a competitive market will be an important part of your mandate.

•	A strong background in accountancy or a related discipline is essential, along with at least 10 years of progressive audit experience with a meaningful portion in a leadership capacity. 

•	CIA certification is preferred, and additional credentials such as CISA, CFE, CDMP would be advantageous, reflecting the multi-disciplinary nature of the modern IA director.

•	You should have demonstrated experience applying data analytics tools in an audit context, familiarity with AI-assisted audit platforms, and a working understanding of IT general controls, cybersecurity risk, and ESG governance. Experience with agile audit methodologies and continuous auditing frameworks would set you apart.

•	Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills are essential, as is the ability to influence and engage with management at all levels — from operational teams to Audit Committees. 

•	Above all, you bring a growth mindset, a genuine enthusiasm for driving innovation in the audit profession, and a deep commitment to strengthening governance in Singapore's public sector.

1.	Future of Urban Liveability - How liveability can be maintained as Singapore grows, both in terms of population as well as growing older as a society, with more diverse demographics. How can planning and policies in the built environment respond to these changes? How do we measure liveability outcomes, involving complex notions of wellness, sustainability, rather than output indicators?

2.	Urban resilience – How cities can be responsive to citizen’s needs through the inter-play of urban governance and collaborative systems, urban design, districts/infrastructure planning and development to maintain liveablity

3.	Science of cities enablers – How cities can leverage the application of relevant approaches/methods such as urban science, foresight, indices, and social and behavioural sciences in maintaining liveability.
jobResponsibilities:
You will help to drive CLC’s knowledge work in project such as the Future of Urban Liveability, etc, grouped under the broad theme of Urban Futures. The studies take on a systems-level view of the policy pathways and urban governance considerations towards how the changes to the nature of work and shifts in live-work patterns impact how districts and neighbourhoods need to be transformed, as well as the infrastructure and management that needed to be put in place to support the transformation of the city, in the light of future disruptions. You may also work on topics related to the future the urban environment, such as the quality of the dense living environment, as well as review of indicators and metrics used to quantify liveability.

You will work with team supervisors and members on challenging urban systems projects, develop detailed research roadmaps, utilise our research enablers and adopt data/science-based and people-centric approaches for these projects, with the intent of translating the applied research into policy. In your work, you will also synthesise information and analyse data from local and international sources, convene thought leadership sessions and in some instances, commission research to be done by universities and research institutes. There will also be opportunities for you to be involved in other related research projects, to diversify your research portfolio and acquire new skills.   

As part of conducting these policy futures projects, you may also be involved in publications, work closely with policymakers, planners, local and foreign experts, and industry practitioners to drive policy discussions and develop CLC’s interests. You will also be involved in work that helps to support and maintain CLC’s strategic partnerships with our knowledge or corporate partners. 

You may expect to share the output from your policy-futures work at CLC’s capacity development programmes which train urban leaders from Singapore and other cities. You may also contribute to curating and participating in the biennial World Cities Summit, Science of Cities Symposium, and other platforms for knowledge sharing.

•	Possesses a futures thinking mindset and keen interest in the policies and plans that underpin and drive urban development in Singapore, and in other cities.

•	Possesses an inquisitive mind with good adaptive and communication abilities, interpersonal skills, management of stakeholders, and a sense of responsibility and drive for continuous self-development.

1. Data Products Roadmap Development, Planning and Execution:

a) Develop and execute the data product roadmap, defining data products required by STB and industry stakeholders, and aligned with STB's organisational goals.

b) Create and maintain comprehensive data products requirement specifications, acceptance criteria and test cases.

2. AI Roadmap, Use Cases and Proof-of-Concept Development

a) Ideate and develop the AI roadmap for STB's data platforms, identifying high-value AI use cases that enhance data accessibility and user productivity for internal and industry stakeholders.

b) Prioritise AI roadmap items using sound evaluation frameworks that weigh feasibility, impact, and implementation readiness.

c) Lead hands-on development of AI proof-of-concepts, starting with natural language query (NLQ) for conversational access to STB's datasets and analytics.

e) Identify and shape AI use cases in close collaboration with line units, translating domain needs into technically grounded AI applications.

f) Work closely with the product implementation team to ensure AI PoCs are documented and specified to a standard that enables direct handover for productisation.

g) Stay current on applied AI developments relevant to data platforms, analytics, and public sector use cases.

3. Requirements Gathering and Product Design:

a) Conduct deep dives into business scenarios, use cases, user journey mapping as part of data and AI product solution design.

b) Translate complex stakeholder needs into clear, actionable product requirements and specifications.

c) Collaborate with Data Partnerships and Stan product team to ensure product feasibility and technical alignment.

a) Ensure adherence to data governance policies for data integrity, security, and compliance.

b) Support data quality management processes, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of data products as part of productisation process.

c) Apply appropriate guardrails and evaluation criteria to AI features to ensure outputs meet governance and quality standards.

a) Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders across STB line units, government agencies, and industry partners, with varying levels of data and tech maturity.

jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for an experienced GIS professional to lead the standardisation and adoption of GIS solutions across LTA's engineering functions. In this role, you will work closely with engineering teams to understand their workflows, identify opportunities where GIS can add value, and develop reusable solutions that can be scaled across the organisation. You will also play a key outreach and enablement role — helping teams discover, adopt, and get the most out of GIS capabilities.

Your key responsibilities include:

  • Developing a thorough understanding of engineering workflows and processes across the organisation, building a clear picture of functional needs and priority pain points.
  • Defining and maintaining a structured framework of GIS use cases organised by common workflows, user groups, and data needs — mapping existing solutions against this framework to identify gaps, duplication, and opportunities for standardisation.
  • Designing and maintaining reusable GIS templates and solution frameworks, including for areas not yet served by existing tools, and assessing enterprise systems and platforms to ensure GIS solutions are fit for purpose.
  • Creating clear, task-based user guides and quick-start materials to help non-expert users get up and running with reusable templates.
  • Planning and leading outreach initiatives across Groups to showcase GIS capabilities, gather feedback, and drive uptake — including facilitating workshops and clinics to support users, address technical queries, and foster knowledge sharing.
  • Continuously scanning for opportunities to broaden the application of GIS across the organisation, translating these into proposed pilots, standards, or roadmap items.
jobRequirements:
• At least 10 years of experience in GIS, geospatial solutions, or related fields, with a demonstrated track record of delivering solutions for engineering, infrastructure, utilities, or asset management contexts.
  • Strong ability to elicit requirements from users, understand end-to-end workflows, and translate them into practical, scalable solutions — from prototype through to full rollout.
  • Hands-on experience creating reusable GIS assets such as templates, data models, map and app patterns, symbology standards, and reference architectures.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise applications and data platforms — such as EAM/CMMS, document management systems, BIM/CAD tools, and data lakes — and how GIS integrates with them.
  • Ability to produce clear, accessible documentation for diverse audiences including engineers, planners, and operational teams.
  • Experience designing and delivering workshops, training, or enablement programmes to drive adoption and build user capability.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to facilitate alignment and influence outcomes across teams without relying on formal authority.
  • A proactive and strategic mindset — with the ability to spot opportunities, prioritise value, and drive continuous improvement through well-designed standards and reusable solutions.

The successful candidate will be responsible for the full database lifecycle, including installation, configuration, upgrades, patching, performance tuning, backup and recovery, high availability, disaster recovery and operational support. The role also involves evaluating and adopting the latest AI Database capabilities to support future platform modernization. The successful candidate will also work closely with existing vendors and internal stakeholders to ensure successful delivery of database migration, upgrade and operational support activities.
jobResponsibilities:
• Lead the migration of Oracle Database 19c environments to Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) on AWS and Azure, ensuring minimal disruption to business operations.

  • Design, implement and maintain database replication between on-premises and cloud environments.

  • Plan and execute Oracle database installations, configuration, upgrades and database lifecycle management.

  • Perform proactive database administration, including performance tuning, SQL optimization, capacity planning, health monitoring and preventive maintenance to ensure database availability, reliability and performance.

  • Design, implement and maintain backup, recovery, High Availability (HA) and Disaster Recovery (DR) solutions.

  • Apply database patches, security updates and configuration changes while ensuring compliance with organisational security policies and industry best practices.

  • Collaborate with application, infrastructure, cloud and DevOps teams to support application deployments, system integration and cloud migration initiatives.

  • Troubleshoot complex database and infrastructure issues, perform root cause analysis, automate operational tasks using scripting where appropriate, and maintain comprehensive technical documentation.

  • Collaborate with existing vendors and cross-functional teams, including application, infrastructure and cloud teams, to deliver database migration, implementation, maintenance and operational support.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent degree.

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in Oracle Database design, implementation and administration in enterprise environments.

  • Strong hands-on experience administering Oracle Database 19c, including installation, configuration, upgrades, patching, performance tuning, backup & recovery and database security.

  • Proven experience planning and executing Oracle database migrations from on-premises infrastructure to cloud platforms, preferably Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) on AWS or Azure.

  • Strong hands-on experience with Oracle High Availability, Disaster Recovery and migration technologies, including Oracle GoldenGate, Data Guard, RMAN and Zero Downtime Migration (ZDM)

  • Familiarity with Oracle AI Database technologies, including Oracle AI Database 26ai, Oracle APEX, Select AI and related database capabilities.

You will join the core team behind the Phoenix LLM – a family of Sovereign AI models trained right here in Singapore. We are an ambitious and dynamic team of Applied AI Scientists building state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) from the ground up. More about our work: http://go.gov.sg/phoenix-launch and https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10391

In this role, you will have the unique opportunity to push the frontier of Sovereign AI while collaborating on joint Applied R&D projects with global AI labs. You will have access to large GPU clusters for distributed AI training.
jobResponsibilities:
You post-train our LLMs for the agentic era: training it for our custom agentic workflows to call tools, carry out multi-step tasks. You will own the whole loop in a selected post-training domain: the reinforcement learning (RL) environments and harnesses the model learns in, the sandboxes where its actions run safely, the training tasks and the checkers that score them, and the fine-tuning and RL runs themselves.

This is not a role building chatbots or applications on top of LLM APIs; your work forms the core agentic capabilities of our models. 

LLM Post Training:
•	Run SFT and multi-turn RL on our GPU cluster, tune training recipe, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting
•	Read agent transcripts to find where the model fails, and fix it through changes to environments, data, rewards or training recipes
•	Check with our product team that gains hold up in real use
•	Contribute to our technical reports and papers

Environments and harnesses:
•	Build and scale tool-use and use-case-driven environments for agentic RL training, including tool servers and the automatic checkers that score the model's work
•	Maintain the harnesses that run our models through agentic tasks and benchmarks, used for both training and evaluation
•	Build containerised sandboxes on our GPU cluster, and own their security. That means code review, access controls - and testing that nothing escapes
jobRequirements:
•	Minimally Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field, or equivalent experience
•	Hands-on experience fine-tuning or training LLMs (for example, SFT or RL) in PyTorch, through work, research, internships or your own projects
•	Strong Python, and comfortable working on Linux
•	Keen to learn and experiment in a fast-paced Applied AI R&D environment

Good to have:
•	Experience with RL for LLMs (for example, GRPO, PPO or DPO)
•	Experience building agent harnesses, RL environments, evaluation harnesses, coding agents or sandboxed code execution
•	Distributed training experience on GPU clusters
•	Published papers or open source contributions

You will join the core team behind the Phoenix LLM – a family of Sovereign AI models trained right here in Singapore. We are a dynamic team of Applied AI Engineers building state-of-the-art sovereign Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) from the ground up. More about our work: http://go.gov.sg/phoenix-launch and https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10391

In this role, you will have the unique opportunity to push the frontier of Sovereign AI while collaborating on joint Applied R&D projects with global AI labs. You will have access to large GPU clusters for distributed AI training. 

In this role, you are the bridge between the core research team and our users - you guide our LLMs on how it behaves and engage with the developers and users who use it. 

You shape the model's identity and safety behaviour through evaluation and fine-tuning, then publish our models, datasets and code with the documentation that tells developers what the model does well and where its limits are and you work alongside our Technical Product Manager.
jobResponsibilities:
Product Releases and developer community:

•	Publish model weights and datasets on platforms like HuggingFace, through our release clearance process
•	Jointly write the model card and technical blog post with the Product Manager for each launch
•	Write best-practice guides and run developer days for the agency’s engineers and the wider AI community

Model alignment and behaviour:

•	Define how our LLMs should behave, including its identity, tone, refusals and honesty, and turn that into written guidelines and training data
•	Build behaviour and safety evaluations, and track them across model checkpoints
•	Run post-training experiments (SFT, RL, etc) to correct behaviour
•	Provide alignment results to advise launch decisions
jobRequirements:

•	Able to explain complex technical concepts (for example the capabilities and limitations of the models) to both engineers and non-technical users
•	Hands-on experience building with LLMs (beyond just using a commercial chatbot)
•	Keen to learn and experiment in a fast-paced Applied AI R&D environment

Good to have:

•	Clear technical writing, shown in a portfolio, for example: research papers, technical linkedin/blog posts, model cards, documentation, a thesis or talks
•	Models or datasets you have published on Hugging Face, or an open source project you contributed to
•	Experience with designing benchmarks or evaluations for LLMs
•	Talks, workshops or published papers (main, workshop and industry tracks all count)

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every point above. Applicants with 5 or more years of relevant experience will be considered for senior roles.

  • Prepare communication lines to businesses on Singapore’s resource policies

jobTitle: Manager / Senior Manager, HR Business Partners
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription:
At MSF, our work makes a difference to individuals, families and society. Delivering that mission well requires leaders who can make sound workforce and people decisions, supported by HR professionals who understand both the business context and the people implications.

Our Human Resource Division is transforming how we partner MSF and our people, moving beyond traditional HR delivery to become trusted advisers, strategic partners and future enablers. The Business Advisory pillar is at the heart of this shift, providing dedicated HR consultancy and advisory support to leaders on people, talent and workforce decisions.
As Manager / Senior Manager, HR Business Partner, you will partner leaders and managers in your assigned portfolio to turn workforce and people priorities into practical action. You will provide integrated advice across workforce planning, talent, performance, deployment, employee relations and organisational change.

About the Role
You will serve as a trusted people adviser to leaders and managers in your assigned portfolio, building a strong understanding of their operating context, workforce needs and employee challenges.

You will diagnose issues, provide practical and context-sensitive advice, and work with specialist teams across the Division to deliver integrated solutions. You will support leaders in taking ownership of people outcomes while helping them navigate established HR policies, frameworks and governance requirements.

The level of portfolio complexity, independent judgement, stakeholder seniority and professional-leadership expectations will be calibrated according to appointment at Manager or Senior Manager level.
jobResponsibilities:
Partner the business on workforce and people priorities
Build trusted relationships with leaders and managers and develop a sound understanding of divisional priorities, operating context and workforce needs.
Provide advice on manpower requirements, workforce planning, deployment, job and organisation changes, and workforce transitions. Analyse relevant workforce information and recommend practical actions.

 Support talent, performance and career outcomes
Support talent identification, succession, development and deployment discussions and follow through on agreed actions.
Advise managers on performance management, performance conversations and underperformance matters, and connect employees and leaders with relevant development, mobility or capability interventions.

Advise on employee relations and conduct matters
Advise leaders on workplace conflict, grievances, employee concerns, conduct and disciplinary matters, applying policy and professional judgement to the circumstances of each case.
Ensure cases are handled with appropriate care, confidentiality, documentation, timeliness and procedural fairness, and escalate complex, sensitive or high-risk matters appropriately.

Enable organisational and workforce change
Support restructuring, leadership transitions, operating-model changes and other organisational developments by assessing people implications and coordinating appropriate HR actions.
Work with leaders and specialist teams to support communication, implementation and employee transitions, and surface practical implementation issues for resolution.

Contribute insights and strengthen HR practice
Identify recurring workforce, employee and management issues within the assigned portfolio and share insights that can improve policies, processes and organisation-wide interventions.

Contribute to Business Advisory tools, knowledge-sharing, calibration and cross-cutting workstreams, and use data, technology and common practices to strengthen advisory quality and efficiency.
jobRequirements:
Experience & Professional Expertise
•	Tertiary qualification in Human Resource Management, Business, Psychology, Social Sciences or a related discipline. Relevant professional HR certification would be advantageous.
•	For appointment as Manager, typically at least 2 years of relevant HR experience. For appointment as Senior Manager, typically at least 4 years of relevant HR experience, with greater experience independently advising leaders on complex matters.
•	Relevant experience in one or more areas such as HR business partnering, workforce planning, talent management, performance management, employee relations, conduct and discipline, deployment or organisational change.
•	Good understanding of HR policies and people-management principles, with the ability to interpret and apply them to business and employee situations.
•	Ability to analyse workforce information, identify underlying issues and develop practical recommendations.
•	Experience in the Public Service or a large and complex organisation would be advantageous.

Leadership & Personal Attributes
•	Strong relationship-building and stakeholder-engagement skills, with the confidence to advise and constructively challenge leaders and managers.
•	Good organisational and business acumen, with curiosity about how the business operates and how workforce and people issues affect outcomes.
•	Sound judgement, discretion and integrity when handling sensitive employee and organisational matters.
•	Analytical and solutions-oriented, able to connect information from different sources and translate it into practical action.
•	Collaborative and resourceful, able to mobilise expertise across the Division and work effectively across functional boundaries.
•	Empathetic and people-centred while remaining objective, fair and attentive to organisational needs.
•	Adaptable and resilient, able to manage multiple priorities and work through ambiguity and complexity.

Manager and Senior Manager Differentiation
At Manager level, you will manage assigned divisions or workforce matters within established frameworks, seeking guidance on higher-complexity or precedent-setting issues. You will contribute to shared tools, workstreams and team learning.

At Senior Manager level, you will independently lead a more complex portfolio, exercise broader judgement on ambiguous or cross-functional matters, advise more senior stakeholders and coach colleagues or lead workstreams that strengthen Business Advisory practice.
